Chapter 31: 31 - Strange Situation

Hunger...

He was feeling very hungry as he wandered through the forest, alone and lost.

Ever since his pack was attacked, he had been chasing after the enemy to take revenge, but his body was growing weaker and weaker.

The enemy always stayed close enough to attract his attention, but never far enough away for him to forget about it.

This chase lasted over an hour. 𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝙬𝙚𝓫𝒏𝓸𝓿𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝙤𝓶

Without him realizing it, the last few minutes were basically him running in circles around the same area while chasing the enemy.

This enemy was a strange white fox, which, despite showing several times that it had the agility to escape, never strayed too far from him, as if it were guiding him to a specific place.

And to Lohan, who was absorbing the memories of this Goblin, it became clear that the place the fox was prowling with the Goblin was the area around where he had disconnected from the game!

’Is this fox another Player?! How does it know that I disconnected here and that when I returned to the game I would connect again? And how did it know that I would connect again at this time?!’

The Goblin’s simple and foolish mind did not notice small details, but Lohan, with a human mind, quickly picked up on these details.

And that was even more frightening than dealing with the Goblin.

In the games he watched in the other world, he knew that the greatest enemy was never the monsters, even though Players died to monsters from time to time. In worlds with PVP enabled, the most frightening and treacherous creatures were other human Players.

Goblins have basic and shallow instincts, thinking only of the food they would eat and the women they would abuse.

Humans are not like that. Humans are greedy, manipulative, cunning...

Continuing to absorb the Goblin’s memory, Lohan saw his theory prove itself more and more correct.

When the little Slime formed from particles of light in the Goblin’s vision, the little fox darted between the trees at a speed she had never shown before and disappeared, clearly leaving the Goblin to deal with the Slime on purpose!

"But why do you want to deal with me this way? Wouldn’t it be easier to just attack me with the strength you showed?"

From the Goblin’s memories, Lohan saw that fox use her stealth and high speed to deal with a group of 10 Goblins all by herself!

Unfortunately, the memories began to fragment and disappear, even though Lohan continued to devour the Goblin’s brain.

"Is that the limitation of Lv 1 of this skill? Not bad."

Lohan could spend some Biomass to raise the Skill’s level and absorb more memories, but seeing that there was nothing useful in that Goblin’s empty head, he gave up.

While continuing to devour the Goblin’s corpse with the help of the Clone, Lohan read the new Skill he had unlocked.

[Chemosensory Aptitude Lv 1]

[The outer membrane can detect odor particles and mana residues in a much more refined way.]

This skill was the reason why the Goblin was so fixated on Lohan as soon as he saw him.

[Chemosensory Aptitude] was an innate ability that allowed Goblins to "smell" in a much more advanced way, allowing them to easily detect the path to something delicious.

And for the Goblin, Lohan was an unparalleled delicacy.

A beautiful ball of Mana completely saturated with magic (for his level), something that if he ate, could not only satisfy his hunger, but keep him satisfied for several days!

After receiving this skill, Lohan could also "smell" his surroundings.

But at that moment, the only thing he could smell was the foul odor of the Goblin he was digesting.

What was once just another creature, upon activating this skill, Lohan felt as if he were eating garbage.

’HOW DO I DEACTIVATE THIS?? BLARGH’ He thought desperately, controlling the urge to vomit, even though he didn’t have a stomach to vomit anything.

As soon as he thought about deactivating this skill, the odors around him magically disappeared, returning to the peace he felt.

Although the smell was gone, the disgust he felt for the Goblin’s body still lingered.

But Lohan was in no position to refuse such a biomass-rich meal, so despite his disgust, he persisted, absorbing as much as he could and using this new biomass to heal himself and recover Mana.

Since the Goblin was also a low-level creature, its body didn’t have that much Biomass. With Lohan and the Clone’s absorption speed, in less than two hours he finished absorbing it.

’Damn, is the Elf still in that place?

Thinking about it, Lohan quickly rolled in that direction.

To go faster, he even bought another evolution.

[Viscous Flow Lv 12 → Lv 13] 13.53 Bio - 0.61 m/s → 0.67 m/s

With a speed of 0.67 m/s, Lohan finally reached the speed that a 1-2-year-old human child had when walking.

That may seem good, but that was the speed of a child walking. If the child ran after him, Lohan would be helpless.

That’s why he had to use viscosity so well in the previous battle, because even a Goblin, with small, disproportionate, and deformed legs, still ran several times faster than him.

As a creature that terrorized villages of adult humans, if they were slow, it would be easy for any human to exterminate them.

But this was already a good start for Lohan.

He wasn’t that far from the place he had agreed with the Elf to start the conversation, so in a few minutes he got there.

Fortunately, this time there was no other competing Slime around to fight him for the girl’s Mana Stone, just the Elven girl looking around worriedly, but when she saw the small blue and shiny ball rolling towards her, with a Slime Core and a Mana Stone almost completely digested inside it, she smiled and waved at him.

"Little friend, you finally made it!"

Meanwhile, in the distance, a white fox watched the scene with even more curiosity, hidden from both the Slime and the Elven girl.

Chapter 32: 32 - Ego

Running up to Lohan, the girl bent down and picked up the Slime, smiling as she searched her magic cloak pocket for something.

Lohan watched the situation with interest.

If before he felt that the girl could be a good bridge between him and a possible civilization, now he felt that she was essential to his development.

If it weren’t for the [Ice Spike] he learned from the Mana Stone she gave him, he would most likely have died fighting that Goblin.

’Damn, I’ve been playing for a week and I’m still weaker than a Lv 1 Monster! No wonder no Guild believed me when I said my Race was Mythical, even though I’m a Slime...’ Lohan thought frustratedly.

Suddenly, Aeliana found what she was looking for and stood up to show it to Lohan with pride.

"Look, my little friend, look how beautiful this Mana Stone is!" Aeliana said with a huge smile on her face as she brought the stone closer to Lohan so he could see it better.

Lohan didn’t even need her to bring it that close; with his enhanced vision, he could see the Mana Stone perfectly, and from what he could see, this stone seemed to be of a higher grade than the stones she had given him before?

Curious, Lohan even activated [Chemosensory Aptitude] to understand it better, but that was a terrible idea.

As soon as the skill was activated, the best smell he had ever smelled in his life invaded his consciousness, almost like cocaine, and instantly energized his mind.

Shocked, Lohan looked at the stone in the Elf’s hand and tried to understand it better.

’From the Goblin’s memories, the smell I’m sensing is several times better than the smell he sensed from me...’

Approaching the Mana Stone, Lohan tried to extend a tentacle to grab it, only for Aeliana to push the stone away, like a child playing with a small animal.

Despite being tempted by the scent, Lohan felt a bitter taste that did not come from the stone. The girl’s playfulness acted like a bucket of cold water on him, like the dynamic of an owner with his dog, and at that moment he was the dog.

Even though it could greatly benefit him, his pride was hurt by this action.

’I already had a shitty life in the first world, in the second world I’m part of the lowest social class, and now in Elysium I’m also going to become just someone else’s pet? Do I really need to submit to these things just for power? Wasn’t this game supposed to be fun for a hero’s journey like everyone else?’

Disappointed, Lohan deactivated [Chemosensory Aptitude] so he wouldn’t be so tempted by that Mana Stone, and [Selective Viscosity] to slip out of the girl’s arm, much to her surprise.

Although he knew it was a foolish idea, that he would reap a great benefit just by pretending to be a dog for a few seconds, Lohan had his pride and did not intend to submit himself like that to please someone’s ego in exchange for a few handouts.

Upon reaching the ground, Lohan turned and began to roll away, not bothering to stay any longer.

Even the fox, who had been watching all this in silence, raised an eyebrow in astonishment, surprised by Slime’s resolute attitude.

Aeliana was the only one lost in that situation, not understanding what had happened.

Walking up to Lohan in confusion, she bent down and spoke to him.

"Little friend...? Did I... did I do something wrong?" she asked, her voice faltering. The euphoria of before was gone, replaced by an expression of someone who had just realized they had unintentionally hurt a friend. "I just wanted to see you happy with the gift... if you want, I’ll get another one, but don’t treat me like a stranger."

Seeing her sadness, still not understanding why he had acted that way, Lohan also felt guilty.

Analyzing the situation from the Elf’s perspective, Lohan really did seem like a pet slightly more intelligent than a cat, but he also didn’t know how to explain the situation and resolve it.

’Damn it, Lohan... look what you’re doing. She’s an elf, she’s probably lived for decades or centuries dealing with cute creatures in the forest that are actually considered pets, and I’m here expecting her to treat me with human ethics and social etiquette even though I’ve never given her any reason to?

Lohan turned slowly.

Aeliana was still crouched down, the high-quality Mana Stone shining between her fingers, but the sparkle of excitement in her eyes had been replaced by a haze of guilt.

Lohan knew that rolling away would only make him look even more like a "temperamental pet."

He needed to refresh her memory, to show her that he wasn’t just an irrational Pet, but someone truly conscious and thinking, with enough intelligence to be treated as an equal.

Focusing on his [Structural Stability Lv 8], Lohan felt the mass of his body vibrate.

Unlike the first time, when forming that baby hand seemed like a Herculean effort that almost made him faint, now he had more control. The bluish gelatin condensed on top of him, stretching with a firmness he didn’t have days ago.

Aeliana’s eyes widened when she saw the Slime change. She remembered their last encounters where her "little friend" controlled its own body to form a hand to interact and talk with her.

Lohan forced the mass to divide into five thin extensions, creating a central palm, and then articulating what appeared to be fingers. In a few seconds, a small hand, the size of a baby’s, but perfectly formed and translucent, emerged from the top of the Slime.

The hand Lohan formed was more shaky than the first time, with well-defined fingers that opened in a clear "Stop" sign.

Lohan didn’t stop there. He used the little hand to point first at the Mana Stone in her hand and then made a horizontal gesture, as if "cutting" the air... a clear sign of disapproval for the game of hiding the stone.

The silence in the clearing became heavy.

Aeliana froze, her hand holding the stone paralyzed in midair. She looked at the small gelatinous hand, then at Lohan’s glowing core, and finally it dawned on her.

"You... you didn’t find it funny, did you?" she whispered, her voice losing its childish tone.

"You were offended because I treated you like... like I treat animals."

Lohan kept his hand raised for a few more seconds, making sure the point was delivered. Then he relaxed his form, letting his fingers ’melt’ back into his spherical body, but remained upright, "staring" directly at her.

The elf sighed deeply, dropping her playful stance and placing the Mana Stone gently on the ground, right in front of Lohan. She didn’t try to pick it up again. Instead, she sat down on the grass, crossing her legs respectfully, staying at the same eye level as him.

"I’m sorry, little friend," she said, giving a sad but sincere smile. "I’m really sorry. I got more excited than I should have when dealing with you... I was so excited about your return, and you took longer than the day before, so when you appeared I was so euphoric that I embarrassed myself."

"This is a stone from a Level 11 Weaver Spider..." She pushed the stone closer to him, her fingers trembling slightly. "I took it secretly from my master’s warehouse... I could be expelled for this, but I thought you deserved the best to grow strong."

Lohan looked at the stone and then at the girl who had risked herself for a creature that had just given her the cold shoulder. The pride that had seemed so important seconds ago now seemed like selfishness.

’She risked herself for me... and I treated the only person who cared about me like an enemy because of a whim of ego. Is being isolated from human interaction for so long taking away my humanity?"

Chapter 33: 33 - Familiar Smell

A small hand formed again above the Slime’s body. Slowly, the jelly on Lohan’s body moved, and five little fingers appeared in front of Aeliana.

The small hand moved forward toward the stone, but instead of bending down and picking up the stone, the hand continued straight, extending to an uncomfortable limit for Lohan, but he stood firm and placed his hand under the Elf’s hand.

Aeliana was sitting in seiza with her hands resting on her leg.

Feeling that damp, cold little hand rubbing hers made the girl’s heart warm and a smile appear on her face.

"Will you forgive me?" she asked hopefully.

The little hand let go and changed into a thumbs-up, then became a slightly deformed sphere before returning to Lohan’s body.

This was his attempt to make a hand emoji as a way to communicate beyond hand gestures, but this test went wrong.

"If it worked, I could just make a face for myself and at least I could show emotions, right?" He became thoughtful.

"That’s great, my friend!" The elf let out a relieved squeal, then reached out and pushed the Mana Stone toward Lohan again. "Go on, take it, I brought it for you."

This time Lohan was no longer polite, rolling forward and "swallowing" the Mana Stone directly.

As soon as the Stone entered his body and began to be digested, Lohan was shocked by the energy he was absorbing from the small chips he was able to pull out of it.

This Mana Stone was so energetically charged that Lohan was having difficulty corroding it!

’This would be a great backup battery... but being a Mana Stone from a Lv 11 creature, I wonder what ability I’ll receive when I absorb it.

"How come you seem so much stronger?" She wondered, confused, after observing Lohan more closely. "I feel like the energy in you is much stronger than yesterday!"

With that said, she moved even closer to Lohan, looking at him in detail, but this time without picking him up.

Analyzing his blue and transparent body, it wasn’t difficult to notice the biggest difference between yesterday and today. "Was this change because you finished absorbing that Mana Stone?!"

Lohan looked at her for a few seconds before giving her a thumbs up with his little hand.

"My teacher already had me study the evolution process of Slimes, but theoretically it shouldn’t be this fast... do you have some kind of Rare Innate Ability?" She asked in a low, surprised voice.

Lohan didn’t know how to respond, and in the end, he just remained silent.

Aeliana didn’t worry and continued to look at Lohan with curiosity before asking about something else, telling him about her day, complaining about the lesson her teacher had given her...

After the misunderstanding was resolved, Lohan and Aeliana talked for a few more minutes before the Elf left and said goodbye to Lohan.

"My friend, I’ll be here again tomorrow!" She shouted as she waved back at him, waved her staff conjuring a small tornado of wind around herself, and disappeared into the forest.

Lohan looked at that convenient magic with envy and turned away, ready to leave.

He didn’t mind spending so much time talking to Aeliana, since he had more than enough Biomass to absorb in the two Mana Stones he was digesting.

To speed up the digestion process and not destroy the forest in front of Aeliana, something he discovered she didn’t like from one of the girl’s many ramblings, Lohan gave the smaller Mana Stone to the clone and kept the large one.

Thus, the two little Slimes could roll around the forest without destroying any grass at maximum efficiency at all times!

As they rolled around in search of enemies, Lohan noticed his Biomass reserve filling up again and bought a few more evolutions.

This time, he didn’t focus solely on increasing digestion efficiency, as he now felt he was already gaining enough Biomass per hour, but rather on utility.

Being just a ball of Slime jelly was very disappointing.

[Efficient Digestion Lv 13 → Lv 14]

[Structural Stability Lv 8 → Lv 9]

[Reinforced Exoskeleton Lv 4 → Lv 5]

[Instinctive Perception Lv 5 → Lv 6]

[Body Density Lv 4 → Lv 5]

[Membrane Reinforcement Lv 9 → Lv 10]

[Memory Resonance Lv 1 → Lv 2]

[Chemosensory Aptitude Lv 1 → Lv 2]

With this wave of evolutions, not only did the Biomass he digests per hour increase from 28.54 Bio/h to 31.40 Bio/h, but his entire body felt renewed.

The jelly of his body became less viscous and easier to control, more malleable. His exoskeleton became more resistant, his Perception sharper, his Body Density greater, his Membrane more elastic and resistant...

As for the last two skills, he felt no difference, since Memory Resonance only activated in the brains and memories he consumed, while Chemosensory Aptitude could be tested again.

Activating this skill, Lohan was surprised to realize that he could perfectly smell the Mana Stone inside him, but this smell was different from the smell he had smelled before...

But ignoring that, another familiar smell was slightly picked up by his skill.

Intensifying this with [Instinctive Perception Lv 6], Lohan saw a faint trace of magical odor around him.

This odor was unfamiliar to Lohan’s own memory, as he had not smelled it personally until now; in fact, it came from the Goblin’s memory.

It was a smell that Lohan not only paid attention to when reading the creature’s memories, but also made a mental note to be on alert when he smelled it around him.

Although it did not change the way he moved at all, Lohan’s 360-degree vision was working at full speed as [Instinctive Perception Lv 6] analyzed everything around him like a scanner searching for the source of that smell.

"Very well, you cunning fox, let’s see if you can escape me now..."

Lohan thought, as he planned how to deal with that fox even though its speed was much faster than his.

Chapter 34: 34 - Stressful Encounter

A faint red smoke floated through the forest, tracing a path through the trees to the little Slime.

This smoke was not something anyone could see, only those with Chemosensory Aptitude could sense it... and Lohan looked at them intently.

’Should I follow this trail? If I find that fox, what do I do? If they try to do something to me, maybe I can defend myself, but if I have to rely on my slow speed to do something to them, maybe I can only shoot an Ice Spike and run out of Mana right after...’ He thought doubtfully.

If he did nothing, it was possible that the fox would do something to him that would put him at risk again... but if he went after it to get revenge, he also had nothing to do against it.

Fortunately, or unfortunately, he didn’t have to decide on that.

The red smoke that had seemed so sparse before gradually became denser.

Lohan looked at them a little confused, but when he "felt" that smoke, he understood... the smell was stronger!

’Shit, I haven’t even decided what to do and they’re getting closer?’

With no time to lose, Lohan used all of his stored Biomass to recover to peak condition, controlled the small Clone to merge with him again, and faced the direction from which the smell was approaching.

The seconds dragged on much longer than normal... a minute waiting for the fox to approach seemed like hours to Lohan, who was on edge, prepared for the worst.

But surprisingly, when a small white head appeared from behind a large, thick tree, Lohan controlled himself so as not to shoot an Ice Spike directly at that creature.

With no means of communication, Lohan just stared at the fox, analyzing for the tenth time whether his position was bad or if he should move to a better place.

Unlike him, the fox walked calmly and confidently, without a hint of fear as it looked at Lohan with curiosity.

Tap... Tap... Tap...

The steps of the surprising little fox made no sound other than the ground being touched. Although the ground was covered with dry leaves and broken branches, her paws did not touch anything undesirable.

Finally face to face with that curious Slime, the Fox also looked at the creature with curiosity. 𝗳𝗿𝐞𝕖𝘄𝗲𝕓𝗻𝚘𝚟𝕖𝐥.𝚌𝕠𝕞

She noticed that unlike when the Slime was facing the Elf girl, where its membrane was soft and relaxed, now in front of her, the creature had entered "attack mode," with a hard and resistant exoskeleton formed above the surface of its body, with a matte and reinforced membrane underneath, and its body perfectly tensed to jump away from her at any moment.

’It seems they’re not an idiot...’ She thought with an internal smile, but outwardly showed only indifference.

Confirming the advanced thought process of the monster in front of her, the fox was almost 100% sure that she was facing another Player, like herself.

With a little caution, and surprisingly relief, she used one of her innate abilities.

"Hello Slime." A young, graceful female voice sounded in his mind.

If it weren’t for the immensely stressful situation Lohan was under, it would have been a very pleasant voice.

But upon hearing it, Lohan was shocked. With his 360-degree vision, he was sure there was no one else nearby who could speak to him, and the strangest thing was that he didn’t see the fox move its mouth!

Frightened, the Slime rolled backward at full speed to distance itself, trying to keep itself safe by distance.

"This is my innate ability, telepathy." The voice sounded again in his mind, a feeling so strange that Lohan was ready to cast an Ice Spike at it.

Even more so after hearing the explanation.

’Shit, did she say telepathy?! Is she reading my memory?!’ He was startled, worried that this was somehow real.

Although he had seen videos and livestreams of other games in the other world, he had never heard of a game that allowed telepathy, let alone something involving the real mind!

This feeling was so strange that Lohan felt as if her voice was sounding in his real mind, not the Slime’s!

Then the voice sounded again, surprisingly patient despite Lohan’s outburst. "Calm down, I can only read your shallow thoughts, just your shallow thoughts. If you want me to lose access to your mind, you just have to try a little harder."

He was suspicious, but having no other choice, he mentally focused on denying anyone any kind of access to his mind.

At first, nothing changed, but after a few more attempts, he finally felt as if something had left his mind.

’Damn, I didn’t even feel that get in there! Since when has she been reading my mind?!’ he wondered in shock.

"Okay, now can we talk?" she asked as she snuggled into the grass beneath her and lay down, looking at the Slime with a playful expression.

Lohan looked at her for a few seconds, seeing that she showed no hostility, he tried to answer. "Yes..."

"Great, you’re really a very interesting Slime... how did you manage to survive the brutal first day as this race? Didn’t that wave of monsters find you?" She asked curiously, looking him up and down.

Although Lohan always considered himself small, his body was already about 30 centimeters in diameter, which meant he was a sphere about 30 centimeters high and 30 centimeters wide.

The white fox in front of him was just under 30 centimeters tall, slightly smaller than him, and when lying down, she was even smaller. But on the other hand, she was thinner and longer than Lohan.

It was what she said that confused him. "Wave of monsters? What’s that?"

At his response, the fox looked at him, also confused. "The monster wave on the first day, most players with rare non-human races died before the first night because of this monster wave. How did you survive it with such a fragile body?"

???????

Lohan became even more confused.

’Wave of monsters? I have no idea what she’s talking about... but as far as I remember, after entering Elysium for the first time, the old Lohan didn’t stay online for more than 5 minutes before disconnecting and going to look for a good guild, unsuccessfully, he killed himself before even logging back into the game.’

Analyzing the small changes in Slime and realizing that he was as confused as she was, the fox asked incredulously. "Don’t tell me you were one of the lucky ones who wasn’t in the game during the monster wave?"

’Can I call a rope around my neck luck?’ Lohan thought to himself.

Chapter 35: 35 - Invitation

"So you mean that 30 minutes after a monster player logs in for the first time, an intense wave of monsters turns the forests near him into a battlefield and logging out is temporarily disabled?" Lohan asked, still shocked.

Wasn’t it enough to come to the other world as someone alone from the Lower Zone, but he was also lucky not to lose the character that could change his destiny?

But on second thought, he remembered that when he first logged in after taking over this body, even though the forest was corroded by slimes, there were no signs of a fight.

Not even the total number of slimes had decreased much since the first time.

"Yeah..." She said lazily. "Anyway, that’s not why I came here. Whether you survived by luck or skill, it doesn’t matter anymore. I’ve been watching you for a few days now, and I’ve realized that you’re far superior to an ordinary Slime..."

Hearing that, Lohan became alert again, his exoskeleton reinforcing itself and his membrane becoming more opaque again.

He knew how valuable Players with Rare races were. Players with Epic races had practically noble or celebrity status. Legendary races, as the name suggests, were so far only legends, with no publicly available documentation about them. As for Mythical races, Lohan wouldn’t even know they existed if he didn’t have one himself.

So he knew how valuable he would be to the other side.

Noticing Lohan’s renewed alertness, the fox rolled her eyes and explained. "You don’t need to be afraid, I also have a rare race..."

What she didn’t say was that she was 99% sure that this Slime had a race much rarer than any other she knew of so far.

But with how skittish he had proven to be, the fox did not make her knowledge of this information clear and acted naturally.

Having been trained in a powerful family since birth, even though she let loose in Elyisum much more than in real life, since no one here knew who she was, she still knew how to behave and how to influence people with her own attitude.

And her attitude proved to be correct when the Slime relaxed slightly.

"Right... why were you watching me and why did you come into contact with me?" Lohan asked, until she remembered the most important thing. "And why did you bring that Goblin to me?"

The first part was within the fox’s expectations, but the second part surprised her. 𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶

"What makes you think I brought the Goblin to you?" she asked, her white head slightly tilted, looking at Slime with half-closed eyes.

Lohan could tell that she had read the Goblin’s memory and seen everything that happened before the situation, imagining the weight of such information, so he quickly thought of a response.

Fortunately, Slimes had no faces or facial expressions, so it was much more difficult for anyone, even an expert in analyzing facial microexpressions, to analyze him.

This was still possible, since Lohan had not bothered to control his own body and his movements already said a lot, but the reinforced membrane and exoskeleton on top made this task very difficult.

"I am a Slime, my vision is far superior to other creatures," he said, trying to regain his composure. "When the Goblin appeared in my vision, I saw you running through the bushes at a much slower speed than you used to escape after he saw me. If you really wanted to escape, you would have gotten away long ago."

The fox looked at him for a few seconds before nodding. "You’re right, I’m sorry about that, I’ll make it up to you, but it was extremely important to ensure your ability before approaching."

Lohan looked at her suspiciously. If he had eyes at that moment, he would have had the same expression she had moments ago. "Why did you need to ensure my ability?"

Depending on her answer, Lohan was ready to send an Ice Spike and split her skull in half, especially with her in such a relaxed pose in front of him, but it was that same pose that also made him keep his cool and listen to what she had to say first.

It wasn’t enough that he had acted rashly with Aeliana a short time ago; he didn’t want to rush into things again.

The fox got up from where she was lying, making Lohan even more alert, and approached him.

When she saw that he rolled away a little as she approached, she stopped and looked at him intently.

"I want to invite you to my Guild," she said in a serious voice.

????

Lohan thought that was absurd.

When the old Lohan was desperate to get a spot in a guild, everyone mocked him, hung up on him, or at best, just treated him like a liar.

Now that he had given up on joining a guild and discovered great potential in his race and class, some crazy fox brought a Goblin to try to kill him and then invited him to join her guild?!

What kind of macabre initiation ceremony is this?

To be promoted in the guild, would he have to face a Troll?

"No thanks. I’m doing just fine developing on my own, and I think you have serious problems if you bring a monster to kill me and then invite me to your guild as if nothing happened." Lohan refused without thinking twice.

This surprised the fox.

Unaccustomed to hearing "no," she thought the Slime would gladly accept to join her Guild.

Especially considering her influence in all the social circles she participated in, someone unwilling to join her to do something was unheard of.

Any investment idea she had, since she was 12 years old, was always received with interest and excitement by everyone.

And here she was, being rejected by a bluish jelly bubble in the middle of a forest.

The fox blinked, processing the "no."

It was a strange feeling. It wasn’t the anger she felt when some spoiled heir tried to flatter her, but something... weird.

The Slime obviously didn’t know he was talking to someone of her identity, and that feeling wasn’t bad, despite being rejected.

She took a step forward, swaying her tails elegantly as she looked at him curiously.

"I’ve already admitted that I was wrong in how I handled your test, and I’ve also said that I’ll compensate you for it, isn’t that enough?" she asked.

Hearing that, if Lohan had eyes, they would have rolled now.

Although he had controlled himself not to turn around and walk away a few moments ago, his patience had limits when dealing with unreasonable people.

He understood that he was talking to someone who lived in a different world than his, which was the only explanation he had for someone acting that way.

And the more he analyzed the situation, the more the way this fox acted reminded him of the students, teachers, and staff from the Upper Zone he had met in college, which further diminished his intention to continue this conversation.

Even though he hadn’t lived his whole life in this world, just the last few days had been enough to make Lohan detest those people.

"I don’t need any compensation. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have better things to do than play initiation games with you," Lohan replied, his body tensing as he prepared to roll away.

Even though he knew he wasn’t as fast as her, this whole conversation was stressing him out.

"Wait!" the fox exclaimed, her sweet voice now carrying a note of urgency she hadn’t used in a long time. "You don’t understand... I’m not inviting you to be just any member."

Based on her assumption, which had proven to be more accurate each time she had come to observe him over the past few days, and which had been further confirmed by the news she had recently received, the importance that this Slime would have in her future plans was immeasurable.

Something that affected not only her, or her guild, but also the future of several planets under her command.

Lohan stopped, but still did not relax the membrane. "Oh, no? Are you going to tell me that you want to invite me to be a Captain in your Guild, or rather, the Vice President?" He asked sarcastically, already thinking that it was not worth wasting any more time here.

The fox let out a short laugh, which made Lohan’s sixth sense stir, and spoke in surprise, staring at him. "I really don’t want you to be a normal member... your guess is correct, I want you to be my Vice President."

Lohan froze completely.

[🪼 End of Volume 1: A Tiny Hunger! 🪼]

Now that the main foundations have been laid, the story will focus more on Lohan’s involvement with both worlds.

I hope you’ve enjoyed the story so far!

I’m counting on your support for Volume 2!

Chapter 36: 36 - Guild

"Vice President?" Lohan asked, confused, thinking that some interference had caused him to mishear what her telepathy meant.

But the fox nodded, indicating that he had heard correctly.

"Yes, ever since I awoke in this forest, I’ve been killing every monster I’ve encountered along the way." She narrowed her eyes as she spoke. "The number of low-level monsters I’ve killed is very high, and among those monsters, there are dozens, if not hundreds, of slimes... but among the various monsters I’ve seen in this forest, you were a surprise."

"What do you mean?" Lohan asked, confused, shocked by the information she gave him.

’So she’s the reason I can’t find any monsters to kill?! All this time I spent hours looking for a monster, only to find the leftovers of what she hunted?’ He realized.

"You see, in the world of Elysium, all races have some potential. Elves are gifted with above-average agility and magical affinity, making even a half-elf an ’Uncommon’ race. Orcs have great potential in physical combat, being strong and physically resistant, but with low magical affinity. Spirit Foxes, like me, have high agility, stealth, and Spiritual affinity, hence my innate telepathy ability." She said in a calm voice, pleased that the Slime was more willing to listen to what she had to say.

’So she’s not an ordinary fox, but actually a Spirit Fox...’ He made a mental note of this information, to try to find out more about it in the future.

With the explanation, Lohan could also see where this conversation was going.

Having played as a Slime for a week, Lohan had already realized how broken Slimes were.

With the ability to devour enemies and evolve by absorbing their biomass, theoretically the Slime had potential in all areas, being practically omnipotent.

And this was clear from his development.

Lohan had skills to become more resistant, more agile, stronger, magical affinity, and even Spiritual affinity, if you consider [Memory Resonance Lv 2] as a Spiritual skill.

’And my potential isn’t limited to that, I probably haven’t developed other areas just because I haven’t come into contact with them yet, as was the case with magic...’

Understanding this point made Lohan understand his value even more.

"Right, I see where you’re coming from. But what gives you the confidence to delegate the Vice-Presidency of your guild to a complete stranger? Not only considering the current influence of guilds in the real world, but from what I’ve heard, even in Elysium this type of organization wields great influence and prestige. Not to mention, won’t the other members be dissatisfied?" Lohan finally asked the crux of the matter.

In the real world, Elysium Guilds were mostly controlled by large financial and political conglomerates. Small groups that tried to venture into this area were met with great resistance from larger groups, which nipped potential competitors in the bud.

Lohan didn’t understand why these billionaires placed so much importance on a guild in a game... sure, it was possible to make money from players who converted gold in Elysium, but that was it, right?

’It’s not like the game gives you any other advantages in the real world...’ His thoughts were interrupted by the memory of the changes he had felt in recent days.

The gain in strength, the increase in nutrient absorption, even the possible ability to nourish himself through the air...

’If these billionaires already knew about these advantages, it’s obvious they would try to monopolize control over the game!

The fox didn’t know what Lohan was thinking, so she explained in response to his question. "I have no mental burden in inviting you to be my Vice President for one simple reason..." She was silent for a few seconds. "The Guild doesn’t exist yet."

-- BOOM!

Lohan’s mind practically exploded with this revelation.

After all this proposal, with so much information and attempts at persuasion, he was actually being invited to a non-existent Guild?!

At that moment, he felt the urge to turn around and leave again, but he calmed down and asked for an explanation. "I believe there is a reason for this."

The fox nodded positively. "Yes, humanoid races that are born in civilizations can open Guilds immediately as long as they have people and money, but monstrous races like ours must first claim a territory by right of conquest and obtain a ’Dungeon Core’ or a ’Seal of Sovereignty,’ and only then can the guild be formed. Unlike humans who buy a license at city hall, we have to force the system to recognize us as a legitimate faction before the world."

This was eye-opening for him, who had never come into contact with these game mechanics.

From the information this fox had, it was clear that her identity was not ordinary, even outside of Elysium.

This access to information was something Lohan valued.

"And how could we get a Dungeon Core or a Sovereignty Seal?" He asked curiously.

Hearing this, the fox underwent a slight change, from a serious and relaxed face, Lohan felt a fire arise in her gaze. "That’s simple, we just need to conquer a Dungeon to get the Core or dominate a territory to get the Sovereignty Seal."

Lohan looked at her skeptically.

What she said was anything but simple!

Feeling Lohan’s gaze, even though he had no eyes, the fox came to her senses. "Ahem, I mean that the process is simple because it is linear and uncomplicated as long as we have enough strength to conquer a dungeon, killing the monsters and the Boss that live there, not that completing this will be easy."

That made more sense.

"I believe you already have a dungeon in mind for this?" Lohan asked, wanting to test how committed she was to this.

Honestly, up to this point, he had been playing a game of eating grass and insects, getting stronger every day at an acceptable pace.

He could continue like this until he became very strong, but would this pace be enough for him to earn money to pay off his debt in three weeks?

It had already been proven that feeding on monsters was much more profitable, not only in terms of biomass due to the Mana Stones they might have inside them, but also because of the skills they knew Lohan could learn by digesting them.

Not to mention that having a goal ahead would be much more interesting than just wandering aimlessly, and probably much more useful for the future than being a "lone wolf."

To his question, the fox nodded again. "Yes, I’ve already explored the entire surrounding area, and of the three Dungeons within our reach, only one is low enough in level for us."

"Hmm, and what is the level of that dungeon?" Lohan asked with interest, thinking about how many monsters he could absorb and how strong he would become after that.

The fox was silent for a few seconds before sighing and replying. "That dungeon is Level 10."

Lohan was shocked.

’I’m not even halfway through Level 1... at least she must be high level, right?

"What’s your current level?" he asked curiously.

The fox was quiet again, making a strange feeling arise in him.

"I reached Level 3 today," she said as she looked away.

-- BOOOM!

Lohan’s mind exploded again.

Chapter 37: 37 - Lisa

Before Lohan could say anything, the fox explained herself. "Calm down, first of all, this forest, and all the ones around us, are low-level forests. The monsters in these places are low-level and therefore give us very little experience, which is why my level has risen so little."

"Why didn’t you go to higher level places?" Lohan asked, confused, thinking of various reasons such as geographical barriers, too large a level discrepancy, lack of mobility, too long a distance, but the answer he received surprised him.

"Because of you," she said, looking directly at him again.

"Because of me?" Lohan asked, confused.

She nodded. "I’ll be honest with you, the process of developing a Guild is not easy, and for me it can be even more difficult for personal reasons that I can tell you if you join me, but even with this difficulty, I have a very high chance of success because my Spiritual Fox Race is a Legendary Race, and my Illusion Weaver Class is a Rare Class. With this combination alone, I already have enough confidence to face the challenge head-on."

Lohan was completely shocked.

Having an Uncommon race or class was already rare, since in his college class, among the Elysium Players he identified, 65% had Common races or classes.

19% were among the "Uncommon."

12% were among the "Rare" ones.

And only one person had a race above that, which Lohan had not yet identified what tier it was, despite hearing a girl comment that it was an Epic Race or Class.

This data was not entirely accurate and could be adjusted up or down in a larger sample for the Common, Uncommon, and Rare ones.

As for the Epic ones, these are even more difficult to account for, let alone Legendary ones.

And to intensify this even further, not only did this fox have a Legendary Race, but her Class was already a Rare Class.

Although Classes could be changed, as Lohan saw in comments from Players who got involved with NPCs and got more advanced classes, that didn’t mean getting a Rare class was easy.

And unlike Class, theoretically, race couldn’t be changed!

If it weren’t for his own luck in having a Mythical Race and Class, Lohan would have been green with envy at the luck of this fox in front of him.

"With such a powerful combination, why wait for me?" Lohan asked, genuinely confused.

Despite showing talent, he didn’t think he showed potential superior to that of a Rare Race, and for someone at her level, that shouldn’t be so shocking.

But the question she asked surprised him. "Someone called other guilds offering themselves as a Mythic rarity Slime a few weeks ago, my contacts learned this information and adding to the strangeness of seeing you evolve so fast, a suspicion arose. Tell me, are you the Player who offered yourself as a Mythic Race?"

-- BOOOM!

The third mental shock hit Lohan.

’Holy shit, was the former owner of this body an idiot? I took every precaution when researching my physical growth so as not to be tracked, and the idiot called the most powerful guilds controlled by interplanetary billionaires and trillionaires from his own cell phone... Great, as if a 30,000 debt that already seemed desperate enough wasn’t enough, now I also have to worry about guild owners who will connect the dots if they hear about a Slime standing out?

This was the most shocking and worrying information Lohan received today. Compared to what he had just heard, which directly involved his safety, the other information was of little relevance.

Thinking quickly, Lohan realized that perhaps the only person who could help him in this situation was that little white fox.

As someone capable of gathering information in this way, with enough power in the real world to resist attacks from other guilds while creating her own, and enough in-game power to also stand out and with a clear interest in helping him, this could be a beneficial exchange.

’My value from here on out will only increase, not only because of my Mythic Race, but also because of my Mythic Class, which together give me an increase much greater than 1 + 1 = 2. And with my value constantly increasing, I would inevitably get in the way of other guilds. Between someone who rejected me without mercy and someone who delayed their own development because they saw value in my potential, the choice is obvious.’

And after calming down, Lohan didn’t blame the former owner of this body so much. After all, he didn’t even know that this was more than just a game.

The fox did not rush Lohan, seeing that he was in doubt, and considering the weight of this information, she understood his shock and fear now.

What she didn’t say was that this was also a test.

She wasn’t 100% sure that this Slime was the Mythical Slime she had heard about, nor did she know if that Slime was real, but she was sure that the rarity of this Slime’s Race was at least as high as hers.

If he lied and said he had an Epic race, she could still maintain the invitation out of respect for the power he would have, but her trust in him would also decrease a degree and would need to be regained little by little.

Considering the sincerity she showed in revealing that she had a Legendary Race, she at least expected the same in return.

And after a few minutes of consideration, the Slime sighed mentally and replied in a calm voice. "Since you were also sincere with me, I will treat you the same way... yes, I am that Slime with a Mythical Race you’ve heard about."

It was as if a shock had struck the little fox.

As much as she imagined that this would be the result, a part of her still imagined that the part about being a Mythical Race was a lie, and that in fact he "only" had a Legendary Race.

This was one of the few times she had been surpassed by someone apparently of her generation.

But seeing that he was sincere with her, an involuntary smile appeared on the fox’s face, which, although it looked sinister to an outsider, still made her happiness clear.

"That’s great, then my wait was worth it!" She said excitedly, unaware of the white, furry tail wagging behind her.

"Then let’s start from the beginning. Hi, I’m Lisa." She said, extending her small paw forward.

Lohan looked at it and formed his small childish hand as well. "Hi, I’m Halon."

Chapter 38: 38 - New Mount

"Hi, I’m Halon." Lohan introduced himself using his ID on Elysium.

Although he sensed goodwill from this fox, he still didn’t know her well enough to trust her with his real name, especially after realizing that she was someone from the Upper Zone. He didn’t know how she would react when she found out that he was someone from the Lower Zone.

"Halon... great name, I’ll send you a friend request." She said as she focused on something invisible in front of her.

Soon a floating window appeared in front of Lohan.

[The player "Lisa" has sent you a friend request. Accept?]

Lohan didn’t hesitate and accepted, causing his friend list, which had always been empty, to finally have a [+1] next to it, indicating that a friend was online. 𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢

Curious, he opened this menu and saw Lisa’s profile.

[Name: Lisa

Level: 03

Status: Online]

This Status screen was simpler than Lohan had imagined, showing only three basic pieces of information, but on second thought, this information was already essential.

Just as Lohan looked at Lisa’s profile, she also looked at Halon’s profile.

[Name: Halon

Level: 01

Status: Online]

Looking at such a low level, she was surprised.

’Shouldn’t he be at least at level 02? With the strength he showed in dealing with that Goblin, his strength is not only much greater than that of other Slimes, but also stronger than the other Lv 01 monsters I’ve encountered, probably around Lv 02 now... is that the advantage of a Mythical Race?’ She thought, confused.

Suddenly she noticed another detail. "Are you still at Lv 01? When did you start playing?!"

Although she had been following this Slime for a few days, Lisa didn’t know how long he had been playing, but she estimated that he had also been playing since the first day, like her, but how did he gain so little experience in that time?

Hearing her question, if Lohan had eyes, he would have rolled them now. "Maybe it’s because there was a Legendary Fox running through the forest at high speed and killing all the monsters? In the last few days, I had to search for over an hour to find each monster."

Lisa’s eyes widened and she looked away. "I’m sorry, I didn’t think the respawn rate of these monsters was so low."

"Don’t worry, I was still able to get stronger even though I didn’t kill monsters." Lohan replied without caring much, as he said, he didn’t even necessarily need to kill monsters to get stronger.

If he had a large stock of plants to digest, he could stay at Lv 01 forever and still be stronger than higher-level players.

Lisa related this answer to what she had observed from this Slime over the past few days, and her curiosity could finally be satisfied. "Are you talking about your skill of digesting things? Is that how you got that ice magic?"

Remembering using Ice Spike against the Goblin Lisa brought to him, Lohan didn’t bother to hide it.

"Yeah, I have a chance to gain characteristics from things I absorb," he said.

"But what did you absorb that gave you that magic? I don’t remember anything in this area with magic like that," she asked, tilting her head curiously.

Introducing herself as Lisa, she felt much more free to act as she pleased. After all, no one knew her true identity, so there was no need to strictly follow etiquette and maintain the image of a perfect girl all the time.

Although she felt more free in Elysium, Lisa still unconsciously restrained herself quite a bit. It wasn’t so easy to change habits developed over almost two decades.

In response to her question, Lohan moved the Mana Stone inside him and held it in his small hand. "As you may have noticed, I received some Mana Stones as gifts, one of which gave me that skill."

Lisa didn’t doubt him; she saw how he grew stronger by absorbing other Slimes.

Her Legendary Race also had great advantages that other weaker races did not have, so she accepted this naturally.

"Great, now that I’ve added you, I can finally leave this area." She said as she looked around, analyzing which direction she should go to continue leveling up. "Do you want to come with me? With my help, getting you to Lv 03 will be pretty quick."

This proposal interested Lohan.

From what Lisa said, leveling up really increased one’s power, so he was curious to know what it would feel like to get stronger this way, and what he would receive for leveling up.

Thinking that he still had a few free hours to play before having to sleep to go to college tomorrow, and that he had already talked to Aeliana today, Lohan replied excitedly.

"Sure, where are we going?"

Finding the right direction, Lisa started walking, and Lohan rolled around, her speed increasing whenever she noticed he could keep up, until she reached his maximum speed, which to her was still terribly slow.

"Hmm, I was planning to take you to a Kobold camp on the edge of the forest, but with your speed I think it will take us too long to get there..."

Lohan was embarrassed.

[Viscous Flow] was already at Lv 13, which made his current speed 0.67 m/s.

For him, that speed was already very high, but compared to the speed Lisa showed, Lohan was like a small child running alongside Usain Bolt.

Suddenly, Lisa had an idea, but she felt a little uncomfortable.

"You can adjust your grip, right? Just like you did with the Goblin... does that skill use a lot of Mana?" She asked as she stopped and looked at him, internally hoping that he would say it was unfeasible.

Lohan was confused, but still answered honestly. "No, the cost is practically irrelevant, why?"

Hearing this, Lisa hesitated for a few seconds.

Looking at Halon in front of her, just a cute blue jelly ball, faceless, limbless, looking like a small fluffy pillow, she sighed.

"Can you climb on my back and use that skill to stick to me? The place we’re going is 5 kilometers away from here, at your speed it will take us over 2 hours to get there..." She said, accepting her fate. "But if you climb on my back, at my speed it will only take us 8 minutes."

Lohan was shocked.

’Damn, I thought I was getting fast with my current speed, but apparently I’m far from the real powerhouses... but come to think of it, an average adult human runs at an average of 8 m/s, running 5 kilometers in 8 minutes is equivalent to a speed of 10 m/s, just a little faster than the speed of a normal human.’

With the possibility of saving 2 hours, Lohan didn’t hesitate and rolled towards Lisa, gently climbing onto her back and using [Selective Viscosity] to stick to her without hurting her.

Fortunately for Lisa, the feeling of the Slime climbing on her back was not as unpleasant as she had imagined.

Although large, its density was much lower than that of other creatures, making its weight much lighter than hers. And with the flexibility of its body, the feeling was as if she were wearing a gel coat, cold and a little sticky, but it did not hinder her movement at all.

"Ready?" she asked, without looking at him, still a little uncomfortable with the proximity. (Not in the way you’re thinking, hehe >:D)

"Yep," he replied relaxed, excited to experience the sensation of riding a Legendary Fox.

He had always seen videos of people riding horses and other animals and felt very envious, so now that he could have a similar experience, Lohan was excited.

Chapter 39: 39 - Adrenaline

NunuNote: Bonus Chapter for reaching the Power Stones Goal, Thanks for the votes! Enjoy the Chapter. ;)

-xXx-

-- Swooosh!

Among the trees, a white fox ran at high speed, dodging the trees and plants in its path with great grace and ease.

On the fox’s back, a Slime larger than itself clung easily, as if it were a natural part of its body.

As she ran, Lisa used the sensation of speed to ignore the thought that there was a man riding on her back, focusing all her attention on running as fast as possible, wanting to reach her goal quickly and break free.

Lohan, on the other hand, was elated by this sensation.

Although he could run at a speed close to his current one if he used his real body outside of Elysium, this was completely different.

With Slime’s body being almost 6 times smaller than his human body, the current sensation of speed was also 6 times greater!

Instead of feeling like he was running at 10 m/s (36 km/h), it felt like he was riding at over 200 km/h!

If riding a motorcycle at that speed already generates an astronomical adrenaline rush, imagine riding a living being at that speed, without controlling the direction, speed, and with much faster and more intense acceleration and braking than when riding a motorcycle at that speed, leaving all decisions to someone else?!

"Hahaha, what an incredible feeling! Thank you for giving me this second chance, how I love being alive!!!"

It is not known why, but instead of taking 8 minutes, Lisa took only 7 to reach her destination, leaving her breathless and having to stop to catch her breath while bending down for Lohan to get off as quickly as possible.

Lohan got the hint and proactively climbed down the fox’s back, still euphoric from the adrenaline rush he felt.

While Lisa rested, panting, Lohan’s membrane occasionally vibrated with excitement.

’Okay, I have to increase my speed urgently,’ he thought decisively, addicted to this feeling.

Without him knowing it, this would be one of the best choices he would make for his development.

Using his enhanced vision to analyze his surroundings, Lohan realized he was in a completely unfamiliar area.

Even though he had searched for hours for other monsters in the past, his speed was so low that Lohan never strayed far from his starting area, making the novelty of this location even greater.

Although he was still in a forest, the current scenery had many more rocks and thick trees, but fewer flowers and smaller plants than he was used to digesting.

Sure, it didn’t make much difference to him now that he had two Mana Stones inside him, and even after digesting 30 Biomass of it, they still remained firm for him to digest.

Seeing that the Mana Stone he received today was much richer in energy, Lohan stopped digesting it and focused on the smaller one, wanting to finish it as quickly as possible to receive the new skill.

Two minutes passed and Lisa finally recovered and made an excuse for it. "I’m not used to carrying people on my back."

Lohan, who hadn’t even thought about it, didn’t mind and continued rolling around, absorbing a little from each plant around him, seeing if there were any special plants that could be useful. "No problem, you can rest for another hour and a half and we’ll still be ahead for not coming at my speed, take as long as you need."

"No need, I’m fine now. The Kobold camp is about 500 meters ahead. Since you’re not very fast, I’ll use my speed to lure them to you one by one, just like I did with the Goblin, okay?" she asked.

"How strong are they compared to the Goblin I faced before?" Lohan asked worriedly.

Lisa thought for a moment and replied. "They are slightly superior to Goblins, but the Goblin you faced before was Lv 02, I’ll try to bring you a Lv 01 Kobold."

"Okay." Lohan found it acceptable.

With his confirmation, Lisa became slightly transparent and set off towards the Kobold camp.

Seeing her become transparent, Lohan was surprised.

’So it’s with this skill that she was able to watch me without me noticing? Even if it’s not invisibility, just the fact that she becomes transparent makes her camouflaged with her surroundings... and even her "smell" has become weaker, what an interesting skill...’

This made Lohan wonder. ’If I absorb someone from a rare race, would I be able to absorb their innate abilities as well?

Thinking about the bird he absorbed and learned [Magic Core] from, it seemed perfectly possible.

He didn’t have to wait long. In a few minutes, a white shadow ran past Lohan at high speed.

"I couldn’t separate just one, in a few minutes another Kobold will arrive, if you need help you can let me know." Lisa said as she passed him and activated her transparency again.

Behind her, a grotesque creature screamed and waved a piece of wood in anger.

-xXx-

The creature that emerged from the trees was a disturbing sight, a bizarre cross between a reptile and a canine.

The Kobold was about a meter tall, covered in reddish, dull scales that looked like dried leather. Its head resembled that of a thin dog, but with an elongated snout and yellow eyes that glowed with rage.

It wore only filthy rags around its waist and held a wooden club.

Grrrr... Kuaa!

The monster growled, stopping abruptly when it lost sight of the fox, but its eyes soon landed on the blue Slime standing in the middle of the path. 𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺

Seeing that fragile little ball and sensing how dense it was in Mana, the Kobold’s anger disappeared, giving way to greed.

Lohan, however, had no intention of being prey.

’Slightly superior to a Goblin Lv 01? Let’s see the difference between us then...’

He felt the flow of mana coursing through his slimy body. Thanks to the Mana Stones he was digesting, his reservoir was being pushed to the limit. He didn’t wait for the Kobold to attack.

In one fluid motion, Lohan’s upper body contracted and fired a sharp, translucent ice spike.

The Kobold, who was about to roar to intimidate the Slime, was taken completely by surprise by the speed of the magical projectile.

SHLICK!

The sound of flesh being pierced echoed through the clearing. The ice spike hit the center of the Kobold’s chest, piercing through its scales and opening an ugly hole from which dark blood began to gush.

The impact was strong enough to knock the creature a step back, causing it to drop its club as it tried, unsuccessfully, to staunch the wound with its claws.

’Great, with him weakened, it will be easier to finish this before the next one arrives.

This time he controlled his Mana production, making a slightly smaller Ice Spike, a little weaker but using less Mana to conjure, making the weakness from lack of Mana less severe.

Lohan noticed that the Kobold’s movements became slow and erratic. The wound on its chest was not just physical damage; although the ice from the magic stopped the bleeding a little, the low temperature also burned.

Taking advantage of the break, Lohan focused his consciousness on the smaller Mana Stone within himself.

"I need to recharge my Mana now. If the next Kobold arrives, I can’t fight with an empty tank."

While his passive devouring ability worked frantically to convert the stone into usable mana, Lohan advanced on the wounded Kobold.

He didn’t use another spell, instead using his own physical mass, leaping toward the wounded Kobold’s legs.

The monster attempted a clumsy kick, but with its agility reduced by the ice burns from the Ice Spike, it barely hit the air, even though the slime wasn’t that fast. Lohan slid underneath it, wrapping the creature’s ankle with his viscous membrane and began digestion.

And to the Kobold’s despair, a smaller Slime appeared behind him and clung to his other leg, slowly climbing up the monster’s body, leaving a trail of blood wherever it went.

Although it wasn’t fast to move, Lohan’s digestion speed was on a completely different level from other Slimes.

Digesting 24.45 Bio/h (Disregarding Passive Digestion), the Kobold’s skin and flesh were disappearing and being corroded before our very eyes!

K-Kuaaaaa!

The Kobold screamed in pain and terror as he felt the Slime begin to secrete digestive fluids onto his exposed flesh.

In a rage, he tried to hit the two Slimes that were digesting him, but the bodies of these slimes were much more resistant than those of the slimes he had encountered before.

If he had been in perfect condition, he could have used his club and taken advantage of the difference in strength and size to break the exoskeletons of these Slimes, but immobilized by intense pain, the full strength the Kobold could exert was less than half!

From a distance, Lisa watched the bloody scene with shining eyes, not because she enjoyed the carnage, but because she approved of the power Lohan was showing, becoming even more satisfied with her choice.
