Chapter 40: 40 - Scammed

Lohan was relentless in dealing with the Kobold, even though the scene was bloody, and his enhanced vision allowed him to see everything in great detail, he forced himself to continue the battle and finally killed the monster.

"This is just a game, Lohan, an extremely realistic game, but still a game, don’t feel guilty. This is an irrational monster that wanted to kill you a few moments ago, if it weren’t for him dying now, it would be you, so don’t let yourself be shaken by the suffering he showed."

He tried to calm down and find an excuse to maintain his sanity in the face of such carnage.

Despite watching horror movies with explicit gore in the other world, the difference between watching a fictional character on TV doing this and doing it with your own hands is huge.

Lisa, watching the scene, nodded in satisfaction.

She had already killed dozens of monsters like that, to the point that she had lost much of her sensitivity to scenes like this.

That was the main reason she wanted to bring Lohan here.

There were other easier monsters she could take him to fight, but considering that what mattered most now was his growth, there was nothing better than bringing him here to gain as much experience in the game as mental experience.

But if she knew he was treating it just like a game, she would have to find a way to change his attitude.

With the information her family had about Elysium, Lisa had known for a long time that this world was much more than that.

-xXx-

Suddenly, the sound of dry branches breaking violently to Lohan’s left brought him back to reality.

The second Kobold emerged from the dense forest with a leap.

Unlike the first one, which was attracted in a mode of extreme fury, this one was a little more rational and arrived in full combat mode, probably alerted by the smell of blood and the screams of its companion.

It was slightly more robust, with darker brown scales and a club that had a rusty metal tip at the end.

Lohan mentally checked his Mana: [Mana: 4.8 / 18.1].

’Damn, the Mana recovery speed is still not enough, I need to increase my total Mana as quickly as possible... An Ice Spike now would leave me too vulnerable if I missed the vital point.’

The Kobold gave him no time to think and advanced with a sideways swing of its club. If Lohan were an ordinary Slime, he would have been crushed, but he used the elasticity of his body to flatten himself against the ground, feeling the displacement of air pass millimeters from his membrane.

’Don’t panic. Even without Mana, I still have the means to deal with this.’

Instead of trying to retreat, Lohan knew he wouldn’t have enough speed for that and propelled his body forward, sliding between the Kobold’s legs.

The monster, confused by the maneuver, tried to turn its body to find him, but the rocky terrain of that area worked against it.

Lohan noticed a rock protrusion and, in one swift motion, expanded part of his biomass to wrap around the base of the monster’s heel, creating a kind of biological "glue," using the physics of the monster’s sudden movement against it.

The Kobold stumbled, letting out a yelp of frustration.

Lohan kept moving, circling the patient enemy. He didn’t attempt a direct digestion this time; he knew this Kobold was at full strength and could tear him apart if he got stuck for too long.

Instead, he began to use his hardening ability intermittently, only on small parts of his body, to strike the Kobold’s tendons every time it tried to get up.

It was a battle of attrition.

The Kobold struggled with all its might to get up or hit this annoying Slime that wouldn’t leave it alone, while the Slime used its speed and agility to the fullest to dodge these attacks while constantly hitting the Kobold.

’5.9... 6.4... 7.2...’ The Mana count in Lohan’s mind slowly rose as he focused on the smaller Mana Stone that was about to run out, forcing his digestion to the maximum.

The Kobold was getting furious.

He struck the ground frantically, trying to hit that blue blur that seemed to read all his movements. Lohan was using the advantage of his enhanced vision and low center of gravity to exhaust the monster’s stamina.

Five minutes of deadly dancing passed. The Kobold was now panting, with shallow and deep cuts on its legs and arms heavy from swinging its club uselessly.

’Now.’

Lohan saw the Kobold rest its club on the ground for a brief second to catch its breath. It was the opening he needed. The Mana reservoir finally glowed with the number he had been waiting for: [Mana: 12.0 / 18.1].

But instead of using Ice Spike, Lohan waited another 10 seconds, enough time for the second Mana Stone to be completely digested!

-- CRACK

-- BOOOM

With a sound of something breaking and cracking, unlike the icy barrage of Ice Spike, the new skill brought a tingling electric sensation that ran through every inch of his membrane.

It was as if thousands of points of light were reorganizing beneath his surface, transforming the dense texture of his jelly into something more fluid and sensitive to ambient light, bringing an acute awareness of how the surrounding colors interacted with his body.

Lohan felt a gentle warmth emanate from his core, expanding in waves that made his vibrant blue color oscillate and dilute.

It was a strange sensation, as if he had ceased to be a solid object and become an organic mirror, capable of absorbing the brown tones of the rocks, the earth, and the green of the treetops, allowing him to blend into the scenery almost instinctively.

Meanwhile, strange memories flashed before him: a chameleon the size of a dog was crouching, its body hanging from a tree trunk, descending vertically without making a sound.

Below the large chameleon, a gazelle drank water from the river, unaware of the danger.

-- SWOOOSH

Suddenly, the chameleon pounced on the gazelle, which, despite sensing that something was wrong, did not react in time and had its neck bitten by the creature. 𝐟𝗿𝐞𝚎𝚠𝐞𝚋𝕟𝐨𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝕔𝕠𝚖

...

[Magic Core Lv 3 → Lv 4]

[Mana: 12.1 / 18.1 → 12.1 / 19.9]

Lohan was ecstatic to see that the [Magic Core] had leveled up, but he forced those memories out of his mind, unable to be distracted in the middle of battle, and came up with an even better idea for dealing with the Kobold.

With a mental command, he focused on his surroundings, something that his 360-degree vision helped greatly.

In a second, the vibrant blue of his membrane began to fade, replaced by a dull, uneven pattern that perfectly mimicked the rocky ground and shadows of the trees.

The Kobold, already dizzy from blood loss and the excruciating pain of digestion in his legs, widened his yellow eyes.

To the creature, it was as if the blue monster devouring him had simply become part of the ground.

Panic took hold of what remained of the Kobold’s mind, causing him to strike the air even more erratically, trying to get rid of an enemy he could now barely distinguish.

In a surge of adrenaline and agony, the Kobold did not try to flee. Instead, he roared and swung his club in a desperate horizontal arc, covering the entire area where Lohan had been seconds ago.

’Shit, he’s going to hit me!

Lohan realized too late that, even though he was camouflaged, he was still a physical object in the path of a piece of solid wood. At that distance, the impact would shatter his exoskeleton instantly.

With no time to dodge or even attack, Lohan had a bold idea and used the only thing he could think of to deal with it.

[Partial Division Lv 3]

PHUT!

A small part of Lohan’s mass violently separated from his main body, without concern for stability or the pain of forcing it out of himself so urgently, and was hurled into the path of the club.

BAM!

The sound of the impact was sharp.

Lohan’s clone was smashed against a nearby tree, exploding into a useless puddle of jelly under the Kobold’s brute force.

But the recoil from the blow made the monster’s arm vibrate, momentarily opening its guard.

Lohan, now smaller due to the loss of the clone’s mass, felt a chill run through his core. If it weren’t for the sacrifice of that small part of himself, he would be the puddle of jelly now. The sense of real danger dispelled any arrogance he might have felt.

’That was a close call...’

Taking advantage of the Kobold still recovering its balance after the heavy swing, Lohan took no more chances.

He planted himself firmly on the ground, and without the telltale blue glow of his body to give away his position, a shot came like a ghost from the shadows.

The translucent ice spike emerged from nowhere, fired from an angle the Kobold did not expect.

--SHLICK!

The projectile pierced the monster’s throat from side to side, passing from one point to another.

The Kobold let out a gurgling sound, falling to its knees as the ice began to spread through its jugular, while the glow faded from its eyes.

[Experience: +5]

Lohan deactivated his mimicry to conserve Mana, returning to his original blue as the creature’s body fell heavily to the ground, lifeless.

’Two down... but my speed and Mana are still very deficient...’

He quickly moved to the body of the first Kobold, which he was sure was dead, and began the massive absorption of biomass.

[New Digested Matter — Incessant Hunger]

[Conflict with: Efficient Digestion]

[No Evolution available.]

Looking at the notification screens, Lohan was shocked.

’I got scammed?!’

Chapter 41: 41 - Level 02

"Why was there conflict in the evolutions?" Lohan wondered, confused.

He opened the game menu without stopping the Kobold’s digestion.

[New Digested Matter — Incessant Hunger]

[Improves digestion, consuming nutrients from any food to increase strength, but greatly increases hunger.]

[Conflict with: Efficient Digestion]

[Unrelenting Hunger and Efficient Digestion have similar characteristics, attempting fusion... fusion unsuccessful, Unrelenting Hunger level too low.]

[No Evolution available.]

Reading the System’s warning logs, Lohan more or less understood what had happened.

Apparently, [Unrelenting Hunger] was a much inferior version of [Efficient Digestion], to the point that even merging the two skills didn’t work, something that would probably increase the level of [Efficient Digestion] just like when he ate other Slimes.

’What a pity... I thought I would get another useful skill... I wonder if the other Kobold will also yield nothing good for me?

Thinking about it, Lohan confirmed again that the second Kobold was also dead and began digestion.

At that point, the little white fox also approached, curious.

"Have you always had that camouflage skill?" she asked, looking at Lohan with sparkling eyes. "I don’t remember seeing you use it at any time."

"No, I just received this skill by digesting the Mana Stone that Aeliana gave me yesterday," Lohan explained.

This made the fox’s eyes sparkle even more. "Your skill acquisition speed is very high... even higher than mine."

Now it was Lohan’s turn to be curious. "Do you also get new skills constantly?"

The fox nodded. "Yes, but instead of getting my skills from other creatures, I need to control my Mana and Spirituality myself to create them."

"Create your skills? Based on your imagination?!" Lohan was stunned.

The possibility of Lisa acquiring new skills didn’t surprise him that much, after all, she was a legendary race, but to be able to do that based on her own imagination? How powerful was Elysium’s processing power to allow something like that? One must take into account that Lisa is not the only one with Legendary Races or Classes, just imagining all the Legendaries creating skills as they pleased was frightening.

Lisa nodded. "The potential of this body is very high, and added to the high Spiritual Affinity, it’s not that surprising. Soon you will discover that this world is much more surprising than you imagine."

After that conversation, Lohan focused on finishing digesting the Kobolds, and Lisa stepped away to rest for a while.

Without Lisa knowing, she described [Pigmentation Mimicry] correctly as a Skill, which for her didn’t make much difference, but for Lohan was a very important factor.

Unlike the [Reinforced Exoskeleton] that was unlocked for Lohan as a separate evolution, where he could invest Biomass at will to evolve further, [Pigmentation Mimicry] did not have this option, being considered by the game system as a Magic Skill, just like Ice Spike.

That’s why he had to deactivate this Skill right after the battle, because instead of consuming Biomass to work, like his evolutions, this Skill spent Mana.

This could be both good and bad.

On the one hand, an Evolution had infinite potential without the need for training. Lohan could invest a million Biomass in an Evolution and it would level up without any bottlenecks.

On the other hand, as long as he evolved his [Magic Core], increasing the available Mana, he could improve these skills without spending a single Biomass point on them individually.

If he had twenty Magic Skills, a single evolution point in the [Magic Core] would increase the potential of all twenty Magic Skills.

There were pros and cons, and Lohan liked the variety it brought, not making him dependent on just a single resource or a single way to progress.

-xXx-

Although the battle seemed long, it was only ten minutes. Lohan didn’t even intend to completely digest the bodies of these monsters, just enough to recover his Mana and the Biomass he lost from the blow the Kobold dealt to his clone.

[Body Density Lv 5 → Lv 6]

Upon digesting part of the second dead Kobold, Lohan finally received notification of a successful evolution.

Even though he hadn’t received anything new, just having a free evolution was already very good.

When he recovered, Lisa repeated the process, attracting two more Kobolds, and Lohan neutralized them both, this time much more easily.

His clone was also able to use [Pigmentation Mimicry], so setting up a trap with Lisa attracting them, the Clone distracting them, and Lohan ambushing them was very easy and effective.

Every 10 minutes, a new group of Kobolds arrived, Lohan killed them, received the experience, and rested.

Lisa didn’t gain anything in this process, but she didn’t mind. With Lohan leveling up, they would soon be able to go to other areas and hunt higher-level monsters, where she would participate in the battle and also receive experience.

With a Legendary and a Mythical creature fighting together, she was confident that she would make up for lost time here.

Lohan also didn’t let the Biomass he earned accumulate indefinitely.

Realizing that his greatest weakness was speed, something that was constantly hindering him in battles, Lohan purchased two more evolutions in this area.

[Viscous Flow Lv 12 → Lv 13]

With that, his speed rose from 0.67 m/s to 0.81 m/s.

He was still far from the ideal speed to face such a monster head-on with ease, but this increase of more than 20% in his initial speed was already a great help.

And he didn’t intend to stop there, even though the price for evolving this skill was getting high, now costing 19.48 Bio to upgrade to Lv 14. Lohan still intended to invest in it even more, at least until he reached a speed of 1 meter per second.

After that, the price would be so high that he would need hours of grinding to accumulate enough biomass, and that wouldn’t be worth it for now.

A little over an hour after they started, the notification Lohan had been longing to hear finally arrived.

[Experience: +6]

[Experience: 102/100]

[Level Up?]

Looking at that, his eyes sparkled.

Without hesitation, Lohan agreed.

Then a refreshing wave passed through his body, nourishing his jelly, making it denser, the membrane more resistant, even slightly accelerating the base digestion speed by +1 Bio/h.

It was as if he had undergone a complete evolution in his Slime’s base characteristics!

[Name: Halon

Race: Slime (Mythical)

Class: Devourer (Mythical)

Level: 02

Experience: 2 / 200

Mana: 19.9 / 19.9]

Looking at the Status screen, he realized that nothing but his level had changed, even though he felt more powerful, not even his Mana had increased.

Confused, he asked those who had experience with both.

"Why does my status remain the same?" He asked Lisa.

"Status? Oh, status is just a representation of your strength. When you level up, your skills get slightly stronger, but you have to feel that change for yourself," she said casually.

Lohan heard that and analyzed himself again.

It was really like she said, when he leveled up, he became stronger as a whole, but only his basic natural Slime characteristics.

The external skills he received from other monsters remained the same.

But that wasn’t a problem. Just increasing his Base Biomass digestion speed by 1 Bio/h, disregarding the other evolutions, was already a big help.

With the extra Biomass he would receive from that, he could buy other evolutions over time.

But at the end of the night, both Lohan and Lisa were satisfied.

Before logging off, Lohan asked her to take him back to the previous location so that the next day he could meet Aeliana without having to roll for two hours, which Lisa agreed to, despite still being a little shy about this type of contact.

As he took the Elysium helmet off his head, Lohan felt much more positive about this life.

Killing monsters while chatting with a friend was the dream he had always had in the other world, especially seeing how streamers and other players enjoyed doing it.

Being able to do something like this in person was incredible.

"I think I was really getting lonely."

Thinking about how many people he would interact with in the future, and that perhaps the possibility of paying off his debt was getting closer and closer, he became even more excited.

So much so that he bent down on the floor and did a few more exercises before going to sleep, without noticing the changes in his body.

Chapter 42: 42 - Level 02 Changes

When he opened his eyes the next day, Lohan noticed something different.

This was the first night he had slept comfortably, without coughing or choking on the polluted air, or feeling discomfort in his body because of the hard mattress.

Although the sky was covered with smoke and soot, the faint sunlight that penetrated this barrier dimly illuminated his room, but even with such a faint light, the definition of what he was seeing was even greater.

’Something has changed... could this be the difference from becoming Level 02 in Elysium?’ He wondered mentally, reaching out his hand and looking closely.

There was a change in his body control, both in strength and agility, but the difference was subtle.

’This is getting weirder and weirder... how can a game influence someone’s body in the real world so much in such a short time? I’m still at Level 02 and I’m already feeling the changes, imagine when I reach Level 20? Level 50? Or even Level 100.’

’Not to mention the importance that large corporations are giving to this game... and with how realistic that world proved to be in all aspects, is Elysium really a game?’

When he had his "breakfast," the nutrient solution mixed with dirty tap water, his nutrient absorption also became stronger.

Like the other changes, the difference wasn’t that big, but for him, who was used to constantly analyzing his digestion in Elysium, these small details did not go unnoticed.

And the last week of evolving [Efficient Digestion] finally brought about a qualitative change, to the point that his body, which was previously thin and malnourished, now had a healthy fat and body mass index.

The workouts he started doing twice a day also showed faster results, with his muscle lines becoming more defined, even if only slightly. After all, muscle gain was still a slow process, even with Evolutions to help.

But Lohan was satisfied.

When he left the house, even with the mask on his face, he still felt discomfort in his throat and lungs, but then an idea came to mind.

"If I’m getting my Evolutions from Elysium in the real world, could [Digestive Filter] also work here?!"

It was a bold idea, but with so many changes happening in their lives in recent days, Lohan decided to give it a try.

Closing his eyes for a second, Lohan remembered the feeling of using this Feature. In Elysium, he didn’t need to be too specific with the use of this Feature, since theoretically it was made to be used by a Slime, so the difficulty couldn’t be too high.

Visualizing the dirty air around him and thinking that he wanted to filter out the pollution, in a few moments the uncomfortable feeling when breathing disappeared!

It was as if he had stopped breathing the air near an erupting volcano to breathe the air a few thousand meters above sea level.

The air was now thinner, requiring him to inhale longer or harder to fill his lungs as he had done before, since after filtering the air he breathed, the contaminated part that represented the majority in the Lower Zone was ignored, requiring even more air with each breath to fill his lungs as normal.

Fortunately, [Efficient Digestion] and [Passive Digestion] also helped with this, allowing him to extract more nutrients from the air.

As he got on the bus and smelled the stench of other people, another bold idea came to mind.

’Is it also possible to filter out these bad smells?

Spending two hours on a flying bus with the stench of people who don’t bathe or practice personal hygiene was a torment he had to accept when he came to this world, but now that could be solved!

With a thought, Lohan tried to filter out the bad smell he smelled, and surprisingly, it worked!

Sure, he didn’t filter out "all the bad smells," just the most annoying and harmless ones, afraid that at some point he might inhale some dangerous gas for too long because he couldn’t smell it.

But just these small changes in quality of life greatly improved his mood!

After a few minutes, even though the current passengers were already squeezed in there, the bus stopped to let other people get on again, not caring about the comfort of those who were already there.

Despite this, no one complained because there was no one to complain to. The bus was driven by AI that would stop at every bus stop, regardless of the current occupancy, and those outside would not fail to get on because of how many people were inside before them.

Among the people who got on, even though everyone was wearing masks, there was someone familiar to Lohan.

The clothes and mask covered that person’s entire body, but as soon as he got on the bus, Lohan felt that the nutrition of the air he was absorbing had increased considerably!

Looking in that direction, he saw again the boy he had accompanied yesterday, whom he believed to have a Rare Race or Class in Elysium.

On a bus with nearly 100 people, that boy was the only one who had played Elysium, and surprisingly, he had obtained not a Common Base, nor an Uncommon Base, but a Rare Base!

(NunuNote: I will refer to "Class or Race" as "Base" from now on, as it is very tedious to repeat this constantly. If I’m talking about a Rare Class or Rare Race, then I’ll use the specific name, but without confirmation of which one it is, I’ll call it "Base" for now.)

Unfortunately, with so many people on the bus, Lohan couldn’t get close enough to get a better look, but when they arrived at the college, only the two of them got off the bus, making it much easier to observe.

Sure, neither of them had any intention of communicating, both because the boy didn’t notice anything unusual about Lohan, and because Lohan knew nothing about this boy and didn’t want to reveal that he also played Elysium.

An Elysium helmet costs $30,000, and at a time like this, when Lohan had no powerful means of protection, someone malicious could use privileged information to break into his apartment while he was at college and basically ruin his life. 𝑓𝑟𝑒𝘦𝓌𝑒𝑏𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝘭.𝒸𝘰𝑚

So this contact could be left for the future.

The walk to class was uneventful. After having his backpack scanned twice, Lohan walked through the college trying to hear important news about Elysium from the Upper Zone Players.

The news was varied, with Players bragging about monsters they had killed, adding nothing to Lohan, while others showed some usefulness, commenting on the structures of the starting villages they lived in.

Basically, there were thousands of starting villages, and apparently Official Guilds could only be created when Players unlocked the next city.

To do this, Guilds actually organized themselves manually in the starting villages, inviting Players by word of mouth and organizing loot, payments, and benefits manually, without using any game mechanics.

Since these places were starting villages, Players couldn’t even buy houses or shops, also having to wait until they reached the next city to buy these.

Because of this, most players were desperately rushing quests and looking for the best spots to grind monsters.

The high interest in these spots generated many conflicts between players, especially between guild players and solo players, who felt entitled to occupy the best spots to the point of threatening and killing players who did not go elsewhere.

Lohan had seen a post on the internet complaining about being killed by an arrogant group from a large guild while researching the physical changes they received from the game, but he didn’t pay much attention to it for several reasons.

But now that he was on his way to developing a guild in the game, information like this became more relevant.

’Too bad I don’t even know if there’s a Starting Village near where I am in the game, much less how I’ll be treated if I’m seen... Players would probably try to kill me to gain experience, right? After all, in their view, I’m no different from a common slime.’

Returning to the classroom, Lohan noticed that the place was completely empty.

Confused, he looked around and tried to think of the reason for this, until he remembered that today’s class would be held in the lab!

Realizing this, Lohan quickened his pace and soon arrived at his class’s lab.

The classroom was practically full, with only a few empty seats.

Looking for the most discreet place, Lohan saw an empty table with two seats and sat down in one of them, waiting for the teacher to arrive.

Looking around, Lohan saw that the boy who had come on the bus with him was also in the room waiting for class to start, sitting in another isolated corner next to another boy from the Lower Zone who kept his head down.

Near the podium where the teacher would stand, the group of students from the Upper Zone chatted animatedly, boasting about their adventures in Elysium.

In the center of that group, despite showing no interest in the conversation, Isabella Vance’s long red hair stood out in the crowd. She sat with impeccable posture while controlling a hologram in front of her face, reading something only she could see.

Suddenly, the classroom door opened and a gasp of breath escaped, attracting the attention of almost everyone.

Chapter 43: 43 - Wrong Data

The door to the Environmental Biology Laboratory opened, and a panting boy appeared on the other side. Looking around and realizing that the teacher was not yet in the room, he let out a sigh of relief and ran to the group of students from the Upper Zone, bumping his backpack into a boy from the Lower Zone without even bothering to apologize.

The boy from the Lower Zone also didn’t dare say anything, pretending that nothing had happened.

In a few minutes, the teacher arrived and class began.

The holographic projector in the center of the room displayed complex graphs about the saturation of carbon particles in the atmosphere of the Lower Zone.

Dr. Aris, a man with excessively smooth skin, a sign of expensive cosmetic treatments from the Upper Zone, pointed to a green line that floated dangerously close to a red zone. 𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖

"As you can see in the scatter plot, the corporations’ macromolecular purifiers have stabilized residual toxicity at exactly 14.8%." Dr. Aris pointed to a static point on the hologram, speaking in a monotone voice, without showing any real importance in what he was explaining. "This index represents the ’Induced Homeostasis Plateau,’ which is basically the technical threshold at which the human immune system can metabolize heavy metals and sulfur dioxide without acute systemic failure or short-term tissue necrosis."

The professor adjusted the cuff of his impeccable shirt before continuing indifferently.

"In layman’s terms: the air in the Lower Zone is perfectly functional for productive life. As long as the sealing protocols for HEPA-4 filter masks are not violated for more than six continuous minutes, alveolar damage remains within the body’s natural repair margin. As long as they do not neglect the equipment provided by the company, these people will be perfectly safe."

Lohan, sitting at the back of the room, felt a bitter taste in his mouth.

Thanks to the [Digestive Filter] he had activated on the bus and his [Efficient Digestion], he could now "feel" the composition of the air in a way that no one else there could. He knew Dr. Aris was lying.

The actual green line should have been dipped in red, as the air he actively filtered contained more heavy metals than the simulator conveniently ignored.

In the other world, Lohan had spent years analyzing blood tests and biochemical reports to understand why his body was dying.

He knew toxicity tables by heart, and although there were slight differences in exposure and analysis of this knowledge between the two worlds, with enough knowledge it was possible to understand the relationship between them.

What the professor was calling an "acceptable limit" was, in fact, almost genocide in slow motion.

"Are they doctoring the data to avoid panic? Or out of greed? Or both?" Lohan thought, keeping his eyes down.

He had no intention of speaking up and becoming the "prodigy student" of the Lower Zone... that would only attract unwanted attention to him.

The conflict, however, did not come from his will.

Next to him, a girl from the Lower Zone, visibly pale and with a dry cough that she tried to stifle with her hand, ended up letting her tablet slip. The device slid down the sloping floor and stopped right at the feet of Julian Neal, the boy who had arrived late, panting, and who was now sitting a few rows down, surrounded by his friends.

Julian looked at the tablet, then at the girl. Instead of returning it, he kicked it further away, causing the device to collide with the corner of a table.

"Watch your trash, stinky girl..." Julian said, without even turning around completely. "With the air being as good as Professor Aris says, you should stop pretending you’re dying to get attention."

The girl blushed with embarrassment, her eyes watering as she tried to get up under the muffled laughter of Julian’s group.

Dr. Aris just cleared his throat and pretended not to see anything.

Scenes like this were very common in college; it wasn’t worth offending someone’s important child for a nobody from the Lower Zone.

"Mr. Neal, please, no interruptions. And you, young lady, if you can’t control your belongings, perhaps you should reconsider your presence in this technical class."

It was the professor’s disregard that made something snap in Lohan.

He saw the mathematical injustice of the data on the projector merging with the social injustice in front of him.

In the other world, he had seen doctors speak with the same coldness about "clinical stability" while his body wasted away, ignoring the pain he felt because the numbers on the papers met bureaucratic protocols.

Without realizing it, his hand gripped the arm of the chair with a force that the Lohan of a week ago would never have had.

"The data is wrong." Lohan’s voice was low, but the sudden silence in the room made it echo.

Dr. Aris stopped talking. Julian turned his neck, a mocking smile growing on his face. Lohan cursed internally.

He didn’t mean to say that, but just as he would argue with doctors who gave wrong diagnoses and thought themselves superior in the other world, his response here came out almost automatically.

"What did you say, sir...?" The professor narrowed his eyes, trying to read Lohan’s name on the terminal.

"The sulfur saturation isn’t just 14%." Lohan forced himself to keep his voice steady, trying to sound like just a confused student rather than a defiant expert. "If it were, the oxidation rate in the filters of ordinary masks would last twice as long as it does in practice. You’re using the purification constant for the Upper Zone to calculate the impact on the Lower Zone. That’s a basic sampling error."

Julian let out a nasal laugh when he heard that and turned to his friends, mocking him loudly.

"Look, everyone, another stinker from the slums thinks he knows more about chemistry than the doctor. Let me guess, you learned that by sniffing the sewer where you live?"

The whole room laughed.

Lohan felt anger bubbling up, but what really bothered him was seeing the boy from "Rare Base," a few seats to his right, watching the situation with an analytical gaze, alternating between Lohan and the fake graphs on the projector.

Dr. Aris walked to the edge of the stage, his face red with indignation.

"Shut up, Hayes. If you’re not going to contribute anything to my class, you’d better keep quiet before I expel you. Until the end of the semester, I don’t want to hear your voice anymore, unless you bring me a scientific study with technical data to prove what you said."

Lohan rolled his eyes when he heard that. How could he provide technical data to prove this in the Lower Zone? Just a device to analyze air saturation would cost several years of the monthly allowance he received.

Although the students from the Upper Zone showed disdain for Lohan, those from the Lower Zone looked at him differently.

Some mocked him quietly, trying to distance themselves from this problematic figure so as not to attract trouble for themselves, while others changed the way they saw him a little.

Since they also came from the Lower Zone, they knew that the filters in the masks did not last as long as the teacher had said, but not only did they not know how to express this, they also did not have the courage to confront a renowned teacher from the Upper Zone like that.

But for one person, Lohan’s comment was like a divine salvation.

"Cough, cough... thank you very much for your help." The girl who had dropped the tablet thanked Lohan with a weak but sincere smile.

If Lohan hadn’t said anything, she would have had to get up to pick up the tablet from the floor under everyone’s mockery, but with his words, people just ignored it and she was able to return to her seat without any further trouble.

Lohan didn’t care about that; he didn’t speak expecting thanks.

But the attitude of these people was becoming increasingly irritating to him.

Thinking that he would have to study here for another four years, Lohan decided to find out how to make money in Elysium as quickly as possible and abandon his studies.

Students from the Lower Zone like him could only use this degree to become low-level employees in large companies, even if they demonstrated great ability.

With the changes and importance he noticed in Elysium, Lohan knew that this would not be the life he would follow in the future, so it would be better to just abandon it and focus on what matters as soon as he had financial independence.

Chapter 44: 44 - Showing Something Cool

After Lohan’s interruption, he completely lost interest in the class and mentally tuned out, since even the data didn’t seem reliable.

Sitting in one of the back rows, Lohan managed to grab his cell phone from under the table and use that time to search for information about Elysium.

At the end of class, he just got up and went straight to the bus stop, wanting to get home as soon as possible.

What he didn’t realize, as he hurried out, was that two or three pairs of eyes were staring at him with different emotions.

Two pairs of eyes looked at Lohan with a slight trace of genuine curiosity, while the third pair of eyes was more sinister, with a mixture of malice and amusement, as if they had found an interesting toy.

But no one did anything about it, just watching Lohan calmly leave the classroom.

-xXx-

When he got home, Lohan first exercised again.

Now that he could absorb even more nutrients from food, his body was even more full of energy.

And with the [Digestive Filter], his cardiorespiratory capacity had risen to another level, generating breath much faster than before, allowing Lohan to train even longer and with greater intensity.

Feeling his own helplessness, Lohan realized that he could only rely on himself in this world, so he decided to improve himself as much as possible.

Putting aside his concerns about money, Lohan spent the last credits available on his card to buy everything in nutritional solutions, which were not only low in price but also delivered many nutrients per meal.

Unfortunately, he couldn’t spend too much time improving himself in the real world, since every minute spent here was a minute lost in Elysium, and since his improvement here depended on how evolved he was in the game, Lohan knew how to set his priorities.

After finishing the quick and intense exercise, Lohan put on his helmet and felt control of the Slime’s body again.

Having played for so many days, being more physically active as Halon the Slime than as Lohan the Human, he felt that controlling this virtual body was becoming more and more comfortable, as if little by little this body was assimilating more and more with him.

Opening his friends list, he saw that Lisa was offline and didn’t care, scrolling to the clearing where he usually found Aeliana.

With his increased speed, Lohan was now able to capture some insects along the way, but unfortunately, no insects with a unique ability like that leech he found on the first day appeared.

Arriving at the clearing, a beautiful blonde girl with long, silky, shiny hair and naturally smooth skin, much better than the artificial smooth skin of today’s college professor, was looking around, a little worried.

When she saw the small shiny blue ball rolling towards her, the elf girl’s eyes lit up.

"Little friend!" she said excitedly as she ran up to Lohan and bent down to pick him up, as she had done before, but when she held him, she remembered the "argument" they had had yesterday and began to open her hands, letting him go.

But Lohan didn’t dislike the girl’s affection, he just didn’t like being treated like a pet, and seeing how she also liked it, he activated [Selective Viscosity] and stuck to her hand, rolling closer.

Seeing that, Aeliana’s eyes sparkled with excitement, a big white smile appearing on her face as she hugged Lohan tightly and affectionately, until concern appeared on her face again.

"My friend, I’m sorry, but today I couldn’t bring you any Mana Stones... my master realized that I took that hidden stone yesterday and hid the other stones from me." She said worriedly, apparently afraid that the little Slime would leave upon hearing this.

But Lohan didn’t care much, the Mana Stone was still with him, charged enough that it wouldn’t show signs of being fully digested for the next few days.

Not to mention that it was never her obligation to give him anything, it was always her who suggested it. 𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦

Forming his little blue hand, Lohan lightly caressed the girl’s hand, expressing that everything was fine.

Aeliana felt relieved, happy that her little friend wouldn’t leave because she didn’t have anything useful.

"I know!" she said excitedly. "Since I didn’t bring you anything cool, how about I take you to see something cool?"

Lohan was curious, what could it be?

But he didn’t know how to ask that without a mouth, so he stayed quiet, waiting for her to explain.

And Aeliana did not disappoint. "I don’t know if you have anything important to do right now, but how about I take you to see my city? I can’t take you inside, since only contracted creatures, summoned creatures, or sentient races can enter, and unfortunately Slimes are not considered sentient by the Royal Family... sure, if you want to become my Contracted Familiar, I wouldn’t refuse."

Lohan was very tempted to accept this, as from the explanation it seemed that Aeliana lived in a real city, a city that probably had its own currency and where he could finally earn money for the real world!

But the idea of becoming a Contracted Familiar didn’t seem good, mainly because he didn’t know what the requirements and limitations would be.

’Maybe this is a route to getting an Uncommon Class, like knights’ squires, but for me, the appeal of that is very low compared to the limitations it would bring... But not being able to enter the city today doesn’t mean I’ll never be able to enter, right?’

Looking at the small human hand he formed with [Structural Stability Lv 9], Lohan realized that when this Evolution leveled up even further, it wouldn’t be impossible to make a humanoid body to enter the city. Even if it still looked like a Slime, it would be easier to show that it was a Sentient Race than to maintain its faceless round shape.

Using the small hand, Lohan tried to explain that he didn’t want to become a familiar, but he was still curious to go see her village.

Aeliana smiled even more and with a swing of her staff, the two practically flew away from where they were, crossing hundreds of meters in a few seconds.

In a few minutes, they had traveled several kilometers, and Lohan finally saw the outline of Aeliana’s city, but what he saw there was shocking.

Chapter 45: 45 - Real World

Aeliana landed on top of a hill, with a perfect view of the city.

Before them stood a metropolis that seemed to have been carved from nature’s own life force, rather than built against it like human constructions.

Colossal trees, whose trunks were as wide as the apartment buildings of the Lower Zone, served as the foundation for towers of crystal and wood that intertwined in organic spirals.

Suspension bridges of glowing vines connected the different levels of the city, while cascades of crystal-clear water plummeted from hanging gardens, purifying the air with a mist that glowed in rainbow hues under the Elysium sun.

And it wasn’t just Elves walking along those suspended avenues... he saw sturdy figures that looked like Dwarves carrying shiny minerals, winged creatures crossing the skies between towers, and even beast-men trading in stalls filled with exotic items.

What was most shocking was the realism of the routine of each person he saw in the distance.

Normally in the games he saw, even those with more immersive worlds, it was still clear that the characters were just NPCs programmed to follow a fixed path, but here, each inhabitant seemed to have a purpose, moving so naturally that it was impossible to distinguish between a player and a high-fidelity NPC.

Lohan could see a pulsating flow of life that defied any common game logic.

Children of various races ran through central squares where statues of ancient gods seemed to watch over the peace of the place. It was a stark contrast to the soot and gray concrete he had just left behind in the real world.

The energy emanating from the city was so dense that Lohan felt his Slime core vibrate in resonance, just as he felt much more comfortable in college with the purified air than in the Lower Zone filled with polluted air. The air in this city was much richer in Mana than the forest he was in.

Observing that magnificence, Lohan felt even more doubts about whether Elysium was just a game or not.

Even though he had transmigrated, he still thought he was dealing with a case of a very technologically advanced world.

For him, the fact that the game was changing his physical body or that the world seemed "too real" was not proof of magic or a parallel dimension, but rather of the frightening level of technology possessed by large corporations.

Coming from a world where technology was advancing by leaps and bounds and now living in a dystopia where humanity possessed almost godlike technologies, dominating several planets and space exploration, Lohan rationalized that Elysium was just the "next frontier" of biogenetic and neural engineering.

But the level of detail in that "simulation" was reaching an absurd level. 𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞

He saw what appeared to be merchants of various races gesturing fervently in squares, guards in gleaming armor maintaining order at the gates, and ordinary citizens following complex routines, each moving in a unique way.

The air from different areas of the map entered his Slime sensors with a wealth of data that he doubted could be emulated.

"Beautiful, right?" Aeliana commented with a smile, looking at the city with pride.

And she was right to feel that way, this was by far the most beautiful city Lohan had ever seen in both lives.

"This is Thalendor, the Elven Royal Capital, built over 30,000 years ago from the ashes of a historic conflict that fragmented our Race."

"The city was erected as a bastion of light after the Great Rupture, when the High Elves and Dark Elves waged a devastating war over ideologies and control of Mana... With the definitive separation of the bloodlines, the High Elves shaped Thalendor to be the pinnacle of our civilization, while our former brothers isolated themselves in the depths, leaving behind a capital that is both a monument to victory and an eternal scar of this segregation." She said with pride and a little sadness.

Although she had never met a Dark Elf, Aeliana was still curious about these "brothers" she had never known.

Lohan found this story fascinating.

A city that has lasted for more than 30,000 years is unimaginable to him, let alone a civilization that has probably existed for even longer.

But that makes sense, as Elves are usually very long-lived creatures, with their myths saying that they can live for thousands of years.

Even Aeliana, who looked like she was 16, Lohan imagined she was much older than him, even adding up the age of both lives.

One great piece of news he realized was that the Elven city seemed very welcoming to other races, so as long as he could communicate normally, even without a humanoid body, he could gain the right to enter this city.

They stayed watching the view for a few more minutes, with Aeliana telling him more interesting facts about the city and the inhabitants she knew, until Lohan realized that Lisa was online and asked the girl to take him back.

The sky was beginning to darken in Elysium, so Aeliana, who had to report back to her master, did not object and took the little Slime back, leaping forward powerfully and using wind magic to propel herself even faster and slow her descent. In a few minutes, they returned to their usual meeting point.

"I hope one day I can show you what Thalendor is like inside. You’ll love the various shops I visit with my teacher. There’s an amazing candy store you have to see," Aeliana said excitedly, not thinking that Slimes don’t even have taste buds.

But Lohan approved of the idea and also acted like someone excited to see the city, not only because it would be useful to him, but because he really wanted to visit it.

What he saw there was so shocking that he began to doubt the reality of this game.

As soon as Aeliana left, Lohan received a message.

[Lisa: Are you available? It took me a while to connect today, let’s try to get you up to Level 03 today.]

This message came at the perfect time, considering the confidence Lisa showed in creating a Guild, she probably came from an influential family in the real world, maybe she had more information about the truth of Elysium!

Chapter 46: 46 - Open World

In a few minutes, Lohan saw the bushes swaying, and then a small, delicate white fox appeared, looking at Lohan expectantly.

"Hello Halon, I couldn’t connect during the day because of some commitments. Have you made any progress?" She asked curiously. After all, she didn’t know that Halon was also a college student.

Lohan replied, "I just logged in too. During the week, I can’t log in before this time."

"Me too. It’s good that our progress won’t be too far apart," she commented with satisfaction. "But I think starting next week, I’ll be free to play more."

Despite making faster progress than players with lower rarity bases, Lisa was dissatisfied with the little free time she had during the week, and intended to take a break from her studies to invest in the game.

Even though her mother wanted her to graduate before getting directly involved in the family business, Elysium would not wait for anyone, and the time she lost in college was time her competitors used to strengthen themselves, creating a big disadvantage for her.

Gradually, the advantage she had gained in the family through her intelligence, even though she was younger, could now be lost if she did not invest time directly in the game.

Her comment about having more free time to play took Lohan by surprise.

Thinking about his own idea of dropping out of college to invest in the game, he became even more determined to do so. Unfortunately, he could only focus exclusively on the game once it started making him money; otherwise, he would be evicted and have to live on the streets.

Realizing that this was a good moment, Lohan decided to ask about the question that had been on his mind for a while. "Lisa, your idea of forming a guild isn’t just for fun, right? Considering how valuable and powerful guilds are, I believe there must be a reason for this."

Lisa was initially surprised by the question, but remembering that she was talking to a Mythic Race Player, he would have to be stupid not to realize this, after all, Elysium’s gains were even greater for him than for her.

Nodding her head, Lisa replied. "Yes, to be honest, I can’t tell you specifically why Elysium is so valued by the leaders of humanity, unless we sign a confidentiality agreement in person, but the changes you are feeling in the real world are very real, and they will likely only become stronger and more noticeable. It shouldn’t be long before people from lower Bases also notice the changes, which will further increase the importance of Elysium."

Hearing this, Lohan further confirmed his theory that Elysium was more than just a game. The more he analyzed it, the more it seemed like another real world. The problem was that he still couldn’t understand how humans managed to create such a method of connection and strengthening...

But that wasn’t important now, so he asked. "Right, speaking of the Guild, who are the other members?"

When this was said, a silence followed, with Lisa looking away.

Lohan was suspicious of this. "Don’t tell me there are no other members?"

Hesitantly, Lisa nodded in agreement. "Yes, and no..."

Lohan was confused. "What do you mean? Explain yourself better."

Then Lisa continued. "Yes, the two of us are the only members of the Guild, but no, we won’t be the only ones. I have subordinates in the real world who will join our Guild, but when coming to Elysium, each player spawns in a random Novice Village, and we were unlucky enough to spawn in the middle of a forest, and I don’t even know where the nearest Novice Village is... so we can only meet up with them when we and they manage to leave the Novice Village."

"How can we get out of the Novice Village if we’re not even in a village?" Lohan asked, confused.

"I don’t know... initially I thought that since I’m a non-human race, I would spawn outside a Newbie Village, or find my way to a non-human Newbie Village and complete the initial quests like other players with races similar to ours are doing, before being transported to the open world. But I’ve searched high and low and haven’t found the Novata Village I was assigned to." She said, a little disappointed.

"Open World?" Lohan asked, confused. "What do you mean by that?"

Lisa explained. "The Novice Village is so called because it is a small instanced zone, with a small village, usually surrounded by a forest where players can safely level up to Level 10. Upon reaching Level 11, the player can leave this instance and finally go to the Open World, a shared world where all players meet."

The explanation made perfect sense with the idea of Novice Village that Lohan had from other RPGs he had seen, but there was a problem with this logic.

"You mean that in the Novice Village instance, there is only a small village and a forest limited in size?" he asked.

"Yes, but even after searching the entire forest, not only did I not find the boundary, I also couldn’t find our Newbie Village." Lisa sighed. "Without finding our Newbie Village, we won’t be able to complete the quests to unlock the Open World, and even if we reach Level 11, we’ll still be stuck here. I even tried to follow your Elf friend, but she’s much faster than me, and she doesn’t fly in a straight line, so I could never keep up with her..."

Her concern was understandable, but it seemed that something had gone wrong.

"She took me to her city," Lohan said.

--Boom!

A mental explosion occurred in Lisa’s head, causing her to instantly change from her disappointed expression to shock. "What?! Really?! How? Did you manage to accept any quests? Did you see other players? If I’m not mistaken, you have to talk to the village chief to get..."

Seeing her excitement, Lohan found the scene amusing, not imagining that this normally proud fox could act like this.

Noticing Lohan’s silence, Lisa calmed down and waited quietly for his explanation.

"I think our situation may be a little different from what you explained, because she didn’t take me to a small Novice Village, but actually to a large Elven city with at least hundreds of thousands of inhabitants," Lohan said.

This was another shock to Lisa, causing her eyes to widen.

"Are you sure? Every player has to go to a Novice Village as part of their adaptation to this world..." She was confused.

Lohan then explained everything he saw, the structure of the city, the various different races, the number of people, and everything he could understand there.

Upon hearing this, a hypothesis arose in her mind, something she didn’t even know if she believed or not, but which could represent both great risks and a huge golden opportunity.

"Could we already be in the Open World?"

Chapter 47: 47 - Evolutions

"Are we already in the Open World?" Lisa asked in shock. "But why are only the two of us here?"

Thinking about it, the only things the two had in common were that they were non-human and had Legendary Races or higher.

But with only the two of them, it was impossible to determine the real reason for this.

"Anyway, although this is good news for us, since we won’t have to worry about relocating our Guild after going to the Open World, we should be even more careful, because here we may encounter monsters of level 11 or higher," Lisa explained.

Lohan nodded. After all, Aeliana had already given him a Mana Stone from a Level 11 Weaver Spider, and if she had a Mana Stone like that, it meant that a monster of that level existed.

"Although this information is important, the most important thing now is to get stronger," Lohan commented.

Lisa agreed and approached him, looking away, still a little embarrassed, but already treating Lohan climbing on her back more naturally than the day before.

Lohan was not shy either and climbed on the fox’s back.

Today’s hunt would no longer be against Kobolds, since despite killing a few, Lohan had not achieved any new Evolutions.

Sure, he received some free evolutions of the skills he already had, but nothing new.

[Viscous Flow Lv 14 → Lv 16] 0.81 m/s → 0.98 m/s.

[Efficient Digestion Lv 14 → Lv 15]

[Hemolymphatic Tissue Lv 5 → Lv 7]

[Structural Stability Lv 9 → Lv 10]

They only farmed for two hours yesterday, which would have yielded Lohan 57 Biomass if he had just been passively forming, but with these extra upgrades, adding up the costs he would pay to evolve, the efficiency of this practically doubled.

The increase in viscous flow increased his movement speed from 0.81 to 0.98 meters per second, which still didn’t even reach the running speed of a 2-year-old child.

Sure, this explosive speed was better than the 0.61 m/s he had when he started hunting with Lisa, almost doubling his previous speed, but it was still insufficient for efficient solo hunting.

The improvement in [Efficient Digestion] to Level 15 was a huge increase, and combined with the improvement from rising to Level 02, the total biomass digested per hour rose from 28.54 to 39.67, an improvement of 11.13 Bio/h! Something even Lohan didn’t expect to be so big.

That was the advantage of exponential growth. When his biomass gain per hour rose from 0.1 to 0.11, it didn’t seem like much, but adding the 10% growth in base Mana, plus 210% from [Mass Expansion Lv 7], plus 50% from [Passive Digestion Lv 5] and 30% from [Partial Division Lv 3]... the 10% increase in his base value was not just a 10% increase, but much more. 𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎

[Hemolymphatic Tissue Lv 7] is also a skill that could not be ignored, increasing his digestion speed by 20% per level. During combat, Lohan’s digestion now reached a terrifying 95.2 Bio/h... in a few minutes of combat, Lohan was able to make entire limbs of the Kobolds disappear in his digestion.

He even thought about causing himself damage to try to activate this skill constantly, effectively more than doubling his biomass consumption, but it didn’t work.

Apparently, just as a person cannot hold their breath until death because the body’s survival instinct kicks in, the lack of danger in mutilating himself to activate this skill also prevented it from working.

But as long as he remained in battle for a long time, Lohan could take advantage of the bonus from this Evolution.

Sure, being constantly in battle meant that his Biomass consumption was also high, to compensate for the damage he suffered when hit, but the profit was still greater than the consumption!

Finally, there was [Structural Stability Lv 10]. Upon reaching this level, Lohan decided to spend Biomass to evolve this skill once again to gain a Trait in it as well.

So while Lisa rode through the forest, Lohan did not hesitate and evolved this skill.

[After 10 minor evolutions, Structural Stability is undergoing a qualitative evolution...]

[New trait obtained, Morphological Memory!]

[Structural Stability Lv 10 → Lv 11]

[Improves control over one’s own body.]

[Trait - Morphological Memory: After understanding a new physical deformity, it is possible to learn and memorize that shape, reducing the cost and energy required to maintain that shape.]

Upon reading that, Lohan’s eyes lit up!

He quickly tried to form the small child’s hand, and surprisingly, not only was it easier to form this human hand that he used constantly, but keeping the hand in that state was much easier than before!

Excited, Lohan tried to make a face for himself, but his jelly couldn’t hold it and quickly returned to its natural form.

’It’s still very difficult to make details... at my current level, I can probably only make two hands, and with how fragile they are, that’s practically useless in combat.

On the other hand, with two hands, Lohan’s communication with Aeliana could work even better, as it would be easier to wave and interpret with two hands to represent different things.

Satisfied, he didn’t even notice that he had already arrived at the new location and Lisa was crouching down waiting for him to come down.

"The hospitality of my back has a limit, Halon." She said, her voice devoid of emotion, but cutting like ice.

Lohan awoke from his thoughts and quickly climbed down. "I’m sorry, I was distracted."

She just rolled her eyes and didn’t answer, running in a certain direction.

Lohan knew she was going to lure the monsters to him, but he had no idea what monsters he would face.

As he evolved, Lisa was saying something he didn’t pay attention to, and from her reaction, she was upset at being ignored.

As he finished adjusting his evolution notifications, Lisa had commented on the topography of the terrain and the attack patterns of the creatures he would face.

Lohan, immersed in his own numbers, didn’t respond right away.

Lohan didn’t care much. He had already apologized before, there was no point in humiliating himself further for something so small.

Before long, a white head appeared among the trees, running at high speed, and behind it, three bloodthirsty black creatures were chasing.

Reaching the ideal distance, Lisa made her body translucent as she ran through the tall grass, leaving the three creatures confused.

The leader of the group, a gray wolf twice Lisa’s size, stopped abruptly, confused.

The fox’s trail had disappeared, replaced by an appetizing smell coming from the tall grass.

Looking there, a greenish ball was almost camouflaged among the grass.

Without thinking twice, the leader of the trio of wolves howled and ran in that direction, ready to take this delicious meal.

Chapter 48: 48 - 10 In Me 40 In You

"Who does he think he is?" Her thoughts were cold with irritation. "I gave up my own hunt to carry him. I analyzed the pack, calculated the risk, and offered my knowledge... and he treated me like background noise."

From the cradle, Lisa had been the gravitational center of everyone around her. 𝒻𝓇𝑒𝘦𝘸𝑒𝒷𝓃ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝒸ℴ𝘮

Her parents, magnates of the family Group, silenced meetings to hear her. Her brothers, geniuses in their own right, sought her advice. Sycophants begged for a second of her attention... Being ignored was an unprecedented experience.

’He doesn’t know who I am, which makes his insolence genuine... and annoying,’ she thought, watching the two Level 1 Gray Wolves and the Level 2 leader surround the Slime. ’If he’s so self-sufficient that he ignores my analysis, he can certainly handle an unexpected bonus in difficulty.’

In that group, there were two Level 01 Gray Wolves and one Level 02 Gray Wolf.

She knew Halon was strong for his level, but she wanted to see how far the "stability" of that Slime would hold up. If he could handle it, she would talk to him again. If not... she could wait for him to learn a little lesson for ignoring her, and then she would help him.

She didn’t know that even though he got stronger as he leveled up, Lohan’s combat power didn’t increase proportionally to that.

Fortunately, he had several useful evolutions.

-xXx-

Lisa watched from the top of a branch, her tail motionless and her eyes half-closed in cold slits.

She noticed that even before the first growl echoed, Lohan had already acted.

With experience dealing with Kobolds, his Clone was already stationed under a twisted root, remaining motionless, camouflaged by the shadows and configured with such high [Selective Viscosity] that the air around it seemed dense.

When the wolves broke through the line of trees, Lohan’s strategy was tested by the brutal reality of combat.

The first Level 01 Wolf leaped forward, foaming at the mouth with ferocity, but Lohan lured it right into the trap.

A sharp crack sounded, not from bones, but from the wolf’s flesh colliding with the clone’s ultra-sticky mass.

The creature was brought to a sudden halt, its front paws sinking to the bone into the green slime, which, upon suffering damage, activated [Hemolymphatic Tissue], increasing the efficiency of digestion and beginning to corrode the monster’s fur and flesh, turning the predator into a living anchor that whined desperately as it tried to break free from the ground.

However, the Level 02 leader was not stupid.

He figured there was another trap and diverted his route in midair, using the remaining flankers as cannon fodder.

Lohan felt the violent impact when the second Level 01 wolf hit him from the side. The force was so great that Lohan’s [Structural Stability] failed for an instant, and he was thrown against a rock, feeling his core vibrate dangerously.

The leader gave no respite.

Before Lohan could recover, the jaws of the Level 02 wolf closed on his exoskeleton.

Lisa saw the Slime being lifted up and shaken violently. The sound of suction and gelatinous tissue being torn was visceral.

’I think I overdid it.’ She realized too late, regretful and ready to join the fight and help Halon.

Wolf blood and blue fluid mixed on the ground as Lohan lost biomass every second, but the idea of biting such a corrosive creature was not smart.

Instead of trying to escape, Lohan used the pain itself as an anchor. He used [Efficient Digestion Lv 15] and [Hemolymphatic Tissue Lv 7] at maximum intensity only on the part that was inside the wolf’s mouth, while transforming the exoskeleton into hardened spines that pierced the creature’s palate and tongue while corroding its jaw.

The leader let out a muffled howl, with blood gushing from his mouth, but Lohan did not back down. He extended tentacles that were veritable whips of acid and wrapped them around the leader’s neck.

The smell of burning flesh rose, and the fight turned into a chaotic tangle of claws and teeth trying to tear through the gelatin and acid melting fur and flesh.

Lohan was being torn apart. He was visibly smaller, his mass being torn to pieces by the coordinated attacks, but his aggressiveness was even greater.

While the wolf dealt 10 damage to him, he retaliated with 40 or 50 damage!

With his large stock of Biomass, Lohan already had the capacity to endure a prolonged fight while recovering, not to mention the biomass he consumed from the wolf itself.

On the other hand, the wolf had no means of recovery; all damage it received was permanent.

Lohan took advantage of a moment of hesitation from the leader to extend a tentacle into the animal’s open throat, expanding violently to suffocate it from within while widening and destroying its throat.

"Aooooooooo..."

The wolf screamed desperately in pain.

Lisa, who was preparing to help in the battle, tilted her head back and kept her distance.

She saw the small blue creature being chewed and almost destroyed, but at no point did she hesitate or intend to call for help.

Halon fought with confidence and desperation like someone who had already passed through the gates of death and survived.

The battle was bloody and frightening for the faint of heart, but it was over in a short time.

When silence finally returned to the clearing, the scene was a disaster of disintegrated flesh and acrid smoke.

Lisa jumped from the branch, landing silently on the stained grass.

Her eyes, once cold with irritation, now carried a shadow of guilt that she tried to hide behind her upright posture.

She approached slowly, watching the Slime reduced to half its size, feeling a strange tightness in her chest as she saw its core pulsing so exposed and vulnerable. The pride of having been "ignored" now seemed futile in the face of the real risk he had taken.

"You... were reckless, Halon," she said, but the "ice princess" tone failed slightly, sounding more like a sigh of relief than a judgment. "Your trap was brilliant, but it took my breath away to see you ignore your own limits like that. Please, next time, heed my warnings... I didn’t bring you here to see your gelatin wasted by a miscalculation we could have avoided together."

Lohan didn’t respond immediately, too focused on his own regeneration, but this time she didn’t blame him.

Lisa stood motionless there, acting as a silent guard while he recovered.

Finally, after a few minutes of digesting the wolves’ bodies, Lohan commented. "Girl, has anyone ever told you that you’re very vindictive?"

Hearing that, a slight blush appeared on the little white fox’s cheeks, but she just snorted and looked away.

Lohan didn’t worry too much about it, even though he was in a tense battle, when the situation became really desperate, he saw with his 360-degree vision that she was ready to interfere and help him.

And with the notification that appeared when he digested the Lv 02 wolf, his mood improved even more.

Chapter 49: 49 - Level 03

NunuNote: This is today’s bonus Chapter from your Power Stone votes! Enjoy!

-xXx-

Upon digesting the Wolf Level 02’s head, Lohan received a notification.

[New Matter Digested — Pack Instinct]

[Evolution available.]

"Finally, a new Evolution!" Lohan thought excitedly, quickly opening the evolution screen.

[Pack Instinct Lv 1] - 7 Bio

[The user’s consciousness projects beyond the main core, establishing a sensory and motor link with allied or subordinate units.

Reading the description of this Skill, if he had eyes, they would be shining like two headlights right now!

This might seem like a bad skill for someone solo like him, not working on anything other than allies or subordinates, he wasn’t even sure if it would work on Lisa, but that wasn’t the main point.

As soon as he initiated this Evolution, Lohan felt as if the bond and control over the Clone had improved!

Not only could he control the Clone more easily, but the control was also more precise and used less mental energy to function!

Sure, he still couldn’t treat the Clone as a second main body, but considering that raising the level of [Partial Division] increased his control over the Clone very little, [Pack Instinct] would be perfect for that!

As long as he raised the level of this evolution more often, in the future he could even consider forming a second clone at the same time!

Without him noticing, his body began to crackle and vibrate with happiness, receiving a strange look from Lisa, who found the scene of Halon devouring the wolf’s head and brain while trembling with happiness a little grotesque.

After Lohan recovered, Lisa went to get more wolves, this time bringing only one Level 01 wolf, then bringing more and more.

-xXx-

In 3 hours, killing more than 18 wolves, Lohan finally received the long-awaited notification.

[Experience: +11]

[Experience: 205/200]

[Level Up?]

Without hesitation, Lohan accepted.

Then another refreshing wave ran through his body, nourishing his jelly even more, making it denser, the membrane more resistant, and slightly accelerating the base digestion speed by +2 Bio/h.

Seeing his base digestion rise from 8.48 to 10.48 Bio/h, Lohan was surprised.

’Wait, does leveling up increase my base digestion speed by 1 Bio/h per level? Or does it double with each level? And if so, then it would be better for me to level up first before evolving my [Efficient Digestion]? Since if I evolve this after leveling up, the effect of leveling up will be even greater...’

Lohan realized that it was as if these two ways of evolving were different... almost as if they were incompatible, or rather, too compatible.

’Maybe the growth per level comes from my Race and the growth from Evolutions comes from my Class? Or the other way around? If so, it makes sense that my growth speed is so abnormal.’

From what he researched about the game during class, or heard other Players talking about it in college, a Player with a Common Class and Race had a very difficult time facing a monster of the same level, so Players would team up in groups to hunt monsters.

But he was not only dealing with monsters above his level, he could even handle monsters in groups!

And knowing how easy it was for Lisa to level up as well, apparently this really has to do with their Base level.

Lisa narrowed her eyes, picking up on the subtle change in the density of Lohan’s mass. The way the Slime now stabilized and the speed with which the biomass reorganized itself indicated that something had changed in Halon.

So she asked, staring at him curiously. "Have you finally reached Level 03?"

Lohan gave a thumbs up with his small hand at his side. "Yes, now we can go to a more advanced area and level up together. Do you have somewhere in mind for us?"

The fox maintained her elegant posture, but there was a slight glimmer of surprise in her gaze when she heard the "us" being said so naturally, even though it was something common.

Lisa nodded. "Yes, there’s a group of bears a few kilometers from here that are around Level 03, with some weaker ones at Level 02 and the strongest being Level 04. I think that could be a good challenge."

Lohan saw no problem with that. Even though bears were more difficult enemies to deal with, as they were more difficult for him to digest until causing a fatal injury, he still had other cards up his sleeve to get used to in battle.

Just as he had avoided using [Ice Spike] in the previous battle, in order to improve in other ways without becoming dependent on that magic, if things got ugly, he could simply burst the head of the wolf that tried to eat him with the ice spear.

"So, shall we go?" Lohan asked a little uncertainly, remembering how upset she had been with him a few hours ago.

Lisa narrowed her eyes at him for a few seconds, but in the end she bent down and let him climb on her back.

If they were to rely on his speed, even with the improvements he had made, it would take them five hours to get there, but with her running, it would only take 30 minutes.

This time, Lohan paid attention to her, so that if she said something, he wouldn’t ignore her again.

As the trees passed by like blurred shadows, the silence between them was no longer as piercing as before. Lisa felt the light weight of the Slime on her back, and as much as she tried to remain indifferent, as she did in real life, her curiosity and hidden identity in Elysium won out.

"You’re strangely quiet..." She commented in a soft, distant voice, but observing every detail. "The last time you were this quiet, you were almost chewed up by a wolf. Should I worry about another ’distraction’?"

Lohan sensed the slight teasing in her tone and vibrated his membrane as if holding back a laugh.

"I’m not distracted right now, I’m just thinking about how today’s grind will change me in the real world." He replied. "And thanks, by the way."

Lisa stopped running for a second, her feet sinking gently into the moss, before resuming her pace. The "thanks" caught her off guard.

"For what? For almost letting you become wolf food?" she asked, confused. 𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞

"For the ride. And for not leaving when I was an idiot and ignored you. I know that even though you’re valuable, you’re not obligated to be here carrying a Slime you met yesterday to level up."

This time, she didn’t respond right away.

The indirect compliment on her importance made the tips of her fox ears twitch slightly.

"Consider it an investment, Halon. I don’t waste my time on people who aren’t worth it..." she said, regaining her superior posture, but with a less cold gleam in her eyes. "Just try not to make me regret..."

She froze. Lisa’s body stiffened, the hairs on the back of her neck instantly bristling.

Without thinking twice, she became translucent, which highlighted the Slime "floating" on her back, but Lohan also thought quickly and camouflaged himself into the environment, still not knowing exactly what was going on.

To understand, he activated his recognition abilities, but before he could smell anything with [Chemosensory Aptitude Lv 2], he heard noises.

CLANG. CLANG.

The rhythmic sound of metal striking metal cut through the tranquility of the forest.

"Get down..." She hissed telepathically, her voice now laden with seriousness. "From the sound of blades, I think there are humans ahead..."

"Humans!" Lohan was surprised. "Have you encountered humans here before?"

"No, this is the first time I’ve encountered something like this... we need to know if they are Players or people from this world," she said.

’People from this world?’ Lohan was thoughtful about the way she used to describe the ’NPCs’.
