Chapter 50: 50 - Confrontation

-- CLANG!

The sound of metal clashing grew even louder.

With Lisa translucent and Lohan’s skin camouflaged, the two slowly approached the place, curious about what might be happening there.

The closer they got, the louder the noise became, until they could recognize a scream.

"Attack now, Jamie, their reinforcements must be on their way!" A male voice shouted urgently.

"Stop interrupting him, Kase, if he loses focus again, I’ll go crazy!" A female voice shouted angrily.

After that scream, the people fell silent.

With every step Lisa took, Lohan felt the magical saturation in the air growing stronger, but instead of the calm and refreshing Mana he normally felt, the Mana in this place was very chaotic and disorganized.

Getting close enough, they finally managed to see what was happening.

Instead of the bears they had imagined they would see, what was happening in front of them was a group of four humans fighting two elves, who were protecting two white-haired elf children behind them.

The humans looked like experienced and well-equipped adventurers. A man with a large axe exchanged heavy blows with an elf swordsman, while a woman with two daggers tried to flank the battle, but was being prevented from doing so by arrows fired by an elf woman who seemed to be at her limit.

Further back, a human archer tried to provide support, but the biggest problem was the fourth man. He held a staff and recited something under his breath, making the mana around him even more chaotic. It was clear that when he finished, the elves would have no chance.

Seeing the cowardice of four against two, and the children’s state of terror, Lohan felt that the right and wrong sides in this situation were clear.

"Do you want to interfere in this?" He asked Lisa.

He was still unsure about it, considering that he was still weak and that he didn’t see himself as a hero, he was unsure whether he should interfere or not.

Sure, the fact that those who needed help were elves, who were possibly from Thalendor or a nearby town, contributed to his intention to help, not to mention that seeing the two terrified elf children touched his heart.

But considering that Lisa was still the one with the most experience in this "game," Lohan decided to consult her.

Lisa watched the scene in silence for a few seconds, then nodded positively. "As long as we keep our presence hidden, the risk our involvement will bring us will be low, and considering how well-dressed the two children are and that the adult elves act as their bodyguards, the reward for this help may be greater than the risk. How about it?"

It took Lohan only a moment to consider. "Sure."

He wasn’t a hero, but he also wasn’t indifferent to seeing such injustice. If he had the ability to help, he would likely lose nothing by doing so, and if he chose to abstain, he would be no better than those people.

Lisa began to move silently toward the human group.

What she didn’t say was that even if there was nothing to gain from it, seeing the children in that state triggered something in her.

Years ago, Lisa had been in an identical situation: hidden and powerless as she watched her security guards fight people who only wanted her head. The fear on the faces of those elf children was a reflection of a memory she would rather forget, and the desire not to let history repeat itself was what really made her decide to help.

Lohan stood firm behind her, using his 360-degree vision to analyze the battlefield. The humans were slowly gaining the upper hand, and once the human mage completed that spell, the battle would be completely in their favor. 𝗳𝐫𝚎𝗲𝚠𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝘃𝚎𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝗺

-xXx-

Despite their professionalism, it was possible to see the desperation rising on the faces of the two Elven guards.

Vulre swung his sword to block the human’s axe once more, feeling the impact vibrate through his shoulders.

Technically, he was superior. His movements were more fluid, his blade was faster, and his strength, refined over centuries, surpassed that of the brute in front of him. But technique meant little when he had to divide his attention between the warrior, the arrows coming from the human archer, and the assassin’s stealthy advances.

He glanced quickly at Elara, the archer beside him.

She was pale, her fingers trembling from pulling the bowstring, doing her best to gain space for Vulre.

Vulre made a discreet signal with his free hand, an elven military code that said, "I’m at my limit. Take the children and run while I hold the corridor."

Elara shook her head almost imperceptibly, keeping her eyes fixed on the human assassin.

She knew that if she ran, Vulre would die in seconds under the weight of four opponents, and they would likely be hunted down in the forest soon after.

"Go, Elara! That’s an order!" Vulre shouted as he spun his body to dodge an arrow that grazed his face, only to have to parry a downward blow from the axe that left a gash in the ground.

The situation was desperate.

The human mage in the background already had his staff glowing an unhealthy purple, and the pressure of chaotic mana in the air indicated that the spell was ready.

Vulre closed his eyes for a brief second, preparing for one last suicidal advance, when the unexpected happened.

Out of nowhere, a small white fireball crossed the clearing like lightning, hitting the human archer positioned among the trees squarely in the chest.

The impact was so sudden that the man didn’t even have time to scream, being thrown backward by the impact.

Almost at the same time, a sharp cry of pain tore through the air, but it did not come from any of the elves. The wizard, Jamie, dropped his staff and fell to his knees.

Something green and slimy had wrapped itself around his leg with absurd force, pulling him down and digesting his skin with an acidic hiss.

"AAAAARRRRRGHHHH!!!!!!"

Unlike the archer, who didn’t even have time to scream, the human wizard felt his mind go blank for a second, followed by excruciating pain in his leg.

The pain and shock completely shattered the wizard’s concentration.

The spell he was about to cast imploded, generating a small shockwave that threw him to the ground, leaving the group of mercenaries in shock and complete silence for a brief moment.

Vulre and Elara froze, not understanding what had happened, but realizing that the tables had turned.

Chapter 51: 51 - Trap

A few seconds ago, Lohan and Lisa came up with a quick and simple plan.

Lisa would find a good angle for an ambush, using her [Spirit Fire] skill on the farthest target, while Lohan would control a clone to roll up to the distracted human mage and interrupt his spell.

They thought about changing targets, but considering that the archer was more alert, he could notice Lohan’s clone and disrupt the plan, so that’s what they implemented.

Although Lohan wasn’t very fast, he still only needed 15 seconds to roll 15 meters with the clone.

As long as his viscosity remained high, he didn’t need to worry about his main body and could focus his attention completely on the clone.

And with [Pack Instinct Lv 1], his control over the clone became even greater, making it easier for him to control the jelly of the clone’s body to make tentacles that silently wrapped around the mage’s leg.

As soon as Lisa fired the [Spirit Fire] ball, the clone sprang into action and activated digestion.

Even though it was only 30% as efficient as the main body, this was limited only to the area it could cover, and its digestion efficiency was as strong as that of the main body.

To his surprise, that wizard’s body was very rich in biomass, perhaps because of his Mana?

But Lohan didn’t dwell on it, Lisa began to move, running in the direction the archer was thrown, while Lohan focused on controlling the clone to cause as much damage as possible to the wizard.

"AAARRRRGHHHH!" The man continued to scream in pain as he thrashed on the ground with tears and snot covering his face.

In desperation, the man couldn’t think of any countermeasures, but his companion did.

Realizing that something was wrong, the assassin turned around in fear and saw the greenish jelly that had melted part of Jamie’s wizard’s cloak and was digesting his flesh at high speed.

"Is that a Slime?!" She asked confused, not believing what she was seeing.

"You’ve got to be kidding me, you idiot, you got ambushed by a fucking slime?!"

But despite cursing Jamie, she ran towards him with her dagger ready to cut that Slime in half.

However, she made the mistake of underestimating the intelligence behind that "jelly."

Lohan, sensing her approach through the clone’s vision, acted quickly. He didn’t just try to defend himself, he used [Pack Instinct] to the limit to use [Partial Division] on the clone, further reducing its size to shoot a jet of viscous fluid directly onto the ground, right in the assassin’s path.

The woman, focused on piercing the Slime, saw it spitting out a green liquid the color of the surrounding grass but didn’t care, treating it as a stupid action that a stupid creature like a slime would do randomly.

As one of the weakest and dumbest creatures in the world, it was difficult for her, who had killed hundreds of Slimes in the past, to take such a small slime seriously.

So when she reached the liquid ejected by the slime, her foot stuck to the green slime like super glue, and the momentum she carried turned into a violent stumble.

"Shit!" She cursed, trying to pull her leg out, but the slime on the ground, stuck to her foot, began to digest and quickly her boot was digested.

To her despair, the speed of digestion of this slime was something so monstrous that she had never seen before! In a matter of seconds the boot would be digested and her foot would follow.

Meanwhile, the main battle took a turn.

Vulre, the elf swordsman, was not a man to waste an opening. Seeing the wizard out of commission and the assassin distracted, he roared a command to Elara.

"Now!"

Elara, catching her breath, fired three arrows in quick succession at the axe warrior, forcing him to retreat for cover.

Vulre, instead of focusing on the warrior, took an acrobatic leap and advanced on the human assassin trapped in the slime on the ground, who now could not count on her agility to dodge his attack.

-xXx-

Across the clearing, Lisa appeared as a white figure among the shadows of the trees, carrying a slime that constantly changed color to better camouflage itself to its surroundings.

She didn’t give the archer time to recover. With a graceful movement of her tails, she activated [Spectral Step], dashing forward as fast as a blur, appearing behind the man and firing another [Spirit Fire] at point-blank range, silencing him before he could pull a dagger from his waist.

-xXx-

Lohan, seeing through the clone’s vision that the assassin was about to use an escape skill to break free from the slime, was about to break free from the mage to deal with her when he saw the elf warrior jump over the human warrior and run towards her.

"Jamie! Kase!" The human axe warrior shouted, realizing that his elite group was suddenly being dismantled.

But no one answered, the mage’s mind could only think of the pain in his leg being digested and becoming even more frightened when he realized that the pain was rising through his body, towards his head.

Anna, the assassin, managed to break free from the slime on the ground after using a movement skill. 𝙛𝓻𝒆𝓮𝒘𝙚𝙗𝒏𝙤𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝒐𝙢

Even if the viscosity was strong, the contact surface was not large enough to hold someone powerful for long.

But now she had to deal with the elf warrior who was attacking intensely.

Swoosh, swoosh, swoosh.

Suddenly, three arrows cut through the air, hitting the leg, back, and shoulder of the human warrior who turned to help Anna and ignored the elf archer.

From that point on, the battle became dominated by the elves.

But despite dealing with the humans, they were alerted when they saw a white fox coming from the direction the archer had been thrown while carrying a green Slime.

Despite being alert, no arrows were fired from Elara’s bow.

When they saw the Slime absorbing the jelly that trapped the assassin, who was now blue to avoid further Mana expenditure, and then move to the slime that was digesting the human mage and absorb that as well, their eyes widened in disbelief.

Chapter 52: 52 - Suspicious Presentation

NunuNote: Thanks to WyrmWood’s Magic Castle Gift, I am going to release 4 Bonus Chapters today! The Bonus Chapter from the Power Stone Goal will be delayed for tomorrow, I hope you enjoy! And a BIG Thanks again to WyrmWood!!

-xXx-

The atmosphere was tense.

The power that this little fox and the slime on her back displayed was very shocking, especially considering that it was a Slime!

In fact, their power was much weaker than that of the two elves or the humans they defeated, but the usefulness of their attacks, the surprise effect, and the ambush they formed were what determined the victory.

In a battle, it is not always the most powerful who wins. As long as the opponent has enough power to break through the enemy’s defenses, any opportunity can be fatal.

And that’s what happened here.

Because of the high density of Mana in the human mage’s body, Lohan’s digestion speed was much slower than when digesting anything else he had tried so far, only slightly inferior to the Level 11 Weaver Spider Mana Stone.

If it depended solely on his digestion, Lohan would not have been very useful in this battle, but his goal here was only to use the clone to interrupt the spell the mage was casting, so the fact that he was extremely fragile to pain was a very pleasant surprise.

When dealing with the female assassin, Lohan only needed to pin her to the ground, and it was the Elf with the sword who finished her off.

Lisa’s battle, although it seemed more dominant and destructive, also took advantage of the fact that the enemy archer was unaware of her and had no spiritual protection, otherwise the battle could have been different.

So under the gaze of the two elves, clearly more powerful than them, Lisa and Lohan became slightly tense, until Lisa opened a telepathic communication channel with the adult elves and spoke cautiously.

"Don’t worry, we have no ill intentions," she said in a calm voice, her eyes narrowed at the arrow pointed at her.

Realizing that the fox could communicate, the elves’ eyes widened, and with Lisa’s gaze on the bow, the female elf took the hint and lowered her bow slightly.

The first to speak was the elf swordsman. "Thank you very much for your help. If it weren’t for you, we don’t even know what could have happened to us."

Looking at him closely, it was possible to see that the clothes he wore were not made for combat, but were simply beautiful, luxurious fabric torn in different places.

Not only his, but the clothes of the entire group were very luxurious and clearly not made for this purpose.

The silence that followed was filled only by the sounds of the forest.

The tension did not disappear, but it changed form. It ceased to be a threat of death and became a mutual and suspicious curiosity.

This silence was broken by a curious voice. "What a beautiful little fox!"

The little elf girl, with long white hair and a beautiful green princess dress that mixed shiny fabric with colorful leaves, looked at Lisa with bright eyes and walked towards her.

Seeing his sister walk up to the fox, the little boy also looked curiously at the newcomers, but his gaze fixed on the Slime, which at some point ceased to be a dull green (because it was camouflaged with its surroundings) and became a beautiful bright blue.

Having never seen a Slime in person, he also began to walk toward the ’monsters,’ only to be held back by the swordsman, with his sister being held back by the archer.

Keeping her hand close to her bow, she looked at Lohan, who still looked like a harmless gelatinous mass, if we ignore the fact that he had just tried to digest a living wizard, turned to Lisa and spoke, her eyes shining slightly.

"I’m sorry about the children..." replied the elf, her voice soft as silk, trying to hide her exhaustion from the previous battle. She approached her fellow swordsman, helping him to stand. "I am Elara. This is Vulre. May I ask... are you by any chance a Spirit Fox?"

Lisa’s eyes didn’t change, but inside she felt her heart skip a beat. But with a calm voice, she replied. "Yes, do you know anything about Spirit Foxes?"

Upon hearing this, the two elves’ bodies visibly relaxed, although the caution on their faces increased slightly.

This strange reaction confused Lohan and Lisa, who at that moment did not know if it was a good or bad thing.

Elara replied with a smile on her face. "That’s great, again, thank you very much for your help. Spirit Foxes are very famous in our history, although they rarely appear in person."

Despite saying this, the caution was still there, but changing the subject, she looked curiously at the fox’s back.

"May I know what..." She didn’t know how to phrase this question.

’Would it be very rude to ask what that is? It looks like slime, but what slime would have the intelligence to do something like this? ’ she thought.

Lohan, realizing that direct communication would be best to avoid misunderstandings, rolled off Lisa’s back onto the ground, without approaching the group. Using the small distance as a gesture of non-aggression and independence.

"Hello, I am Halon, a Slime," he said, using the mental link Lisa had created.

Hearing this, the elves’ eyes widened, alternating between disbelief that a Slime could have wisdom and the fox, who looked at it as if it were the most normal thing in the world.

The strangest thing was that this Slime even had a name!

And considering the reputation of Spirit Foxes, accepting this situation was even more difficult.

Their distrust was so clear that Lohan had an idea to alleviate it. "We decided to help because we realized that you look like a friend of mine, who is also an elf."

Just as Lohan had imagined, using someone in common to form a close relationship was a good choice, as upon hearing this, the elves became curious.

"Really?

Who is your friend? Maybe we can meet her." Vulre asked.

Although Thalendor was a huge city run by elves, the local elven population was not the largest. After all, as a long-lived race, fertility was never their strong suit.

And for thousands of years, even though they had different and distant lives, living in the same city, the possibility of meeting each other sometimes was very high.

They couldn’t say they knew all the elves in Thalendor, but to say they knew most of them would not be an exaggeration.

Thinking about the elf friend he had made, Lohan remembered the scene of Aeliana introducing herself to him by name, but he was unable to respond because he couldn’t speak or write the language of this world.

But he explained. "I met her a few days ago, her name is Aeliana, a mage."

Hearing that name, the elves’ eyes widened in surprise, obviously knowing the elf the slime was talking about.

This made Lohan curious about his friend.

’Is Aeliana famous among the elves of Thalendor?

Chapter 53: 53 - Reward

"Are you Lady Aeliana’s friend?" Vulre asked in surprise.

He imagined that the friend this Slime was referring to was an ordinary common elf who happened to wander through the forest and met this fascinating creature, not that she was "THE" Lady Aeliana.

"She’s Lia’s friend?!" This time, it wasn’t Elara, who had also heard the explanation, who asked in shock, but the little white-haired girl, who looked at the white fox with even brighter eyes, not knowing that it was the slime who was "speaking."

Lohan noticed the nickname the girl used to refer to Aeliana and felt confident, but he also paid attention to these children, surprised by the calm and tranquility they were showing, despite having just witnessed a brutal and bloody fight between people who probably wanted to harm them.

But it was not his place to judge how someone dealt with difficult situations, so he just answered Vulre’s question, using as much detail as possible from the conversations he had had with Aeliana to lend credibility.

And Lisa was smart, realizing that the child had a favorable opinion of Halon’s elf friend, she extended the mental link so that the children could also hear what they were saying.

"Yes, we haven’t been friends for long, but we’ve known each other for a few days. She’s already told me some stories about her teacher and the endless homework she had to do," Lohan explained.

Hearing a calm and beautiful male voice in her mind, the little girl was only slightly surprised before bursting out laughing. "Hahaha, Lia really hates Aunt Yrneha’s lessons!!"

She received nods of agreement from her brother beside her, who was also not very surprised by the voice in his mind.

Vulre and Elara nodded when they heard that, confirming through these details that this Slime really seemed to know Lady Aeliana.

This made them lower their guard a little more, although they did not change their protective attitude towards the children.

But this attitude did not bother the two ’monsters’.

"How nice that we were helped by acquaintances. I apologize for the rush, but we need to take these children back to Thalendor urgently. Don’t worry, this debt of gratitude will be repaid... but how can we contact you?" Vulre spoke politely, displaying the manners of a refined butler.

Combined with the beautiful appearance of the elves, even acting as a butler, Vulre seemed more elegant than most human nobles.

Lohan and Lisa looked at each other, noticing the positive surprise in each other’s eyes, and Lohan replied. "How about you contact me through Aeliana? Last time she wanted to show me Thalendor, but because I’m a Slime, she was afraid that I wouldn’t be allowed in." Lohan spoke in a slightly regretful voice.

This was perfect for Vulre, as he could not only prove this Slime’s relationship with Lady Aeliana, but also repay part of the favor that had been done to them now.

Although he did not have much physical power or talent for magic, Vulre had enough power to handle a small situation like this in Thalendor, as well as win the goodwill of a Spirit Fox’s friend!

"Don’t worry, just for the intellectual level you have shown us, approval to enter Thalendor would already be guaranteed, this will be quickly resolved. As for compensation for the help you gave us in battle, I will give you an answer as soon as possible through Lady Aeliana." Vulre replied respectfully.

Elara also gave a polite greeting to Lohan and Lisa before dragging away the two children who had started to complain.

-xXx-

Seeing them walk away, Lohan didn’t worry about being deceived.

Even if they had no real power in Thalendor, just the human bodies they left behind would be a great reward for Lohan, who was curious to know what he would gain by digesting them.

Without hesitation, he moved toward the Wizard’s body, which was closest to him, and enveloped his head with the blue jelly.

In a few moments, the man’s skin began to bubble.

Lisa looked at that scene without caring. Even though it seemed grotesque to a normal person, she just looked at it with curiosity before sitting on her hind legs and looking at Lohan curiously.

"It was a good move to bring up the name of an acquaintance in the conversation, Halon. Their hostility towards us decreased considerably after you said that." She commented with approval in her voice, looking at the little Slime with a slight trace of curiosity.

From what she had seen of this Player so far, he had shown himself to be someone possibly from the Lower Zone, someone who was lucky enough to get a Mythical Race, but who intellectually had shown nothing more than a normal person.

He had a temper, was a little proud, and despite knowing nothing about Elysium, he showed a high adaptability to various situations.

In her view, Halon initially had great potential to be a powerful Player in the future, and that was what she valued in him, but realizing the subtleties of how he acted, it seemed that he had more potential than what she had seen?

Lohan looked at Lisa as he digested the wizard’s face, although she didn’t know he was looking at her, and replied casually. "That’s just the basics of human interaction. When talking to someone from a different place or culture, saying that you already know someone like them will naturally raise their impression of you."

Lisa nodded. She already knew this from the family training she had to go through, but most people her age that she knew were too stupid to understand even something so basic.

And considering that the people her age she had contact with were mostly heirs to medium to giant companies in the Upper Zone, if Lohan knew he was being compared to those people, he would roll his eyes.

The two talked a little more as digestion continued, but in a few minutes a message popped up in front of Lohan!

[New Matter Digested...]

Chapter 54: 54 - Great Harvest!

[Evolution available.]

[Magic Core Lv 4 → Lv 5]

[Total Mana: 19.9 → 21.89]

Despite the slight pain he felt, the dopamine rush from the feeling of power growing as he evolved was much more intense than that.

Stopping the conversation immediately, Lohan opened the evolution tab and there was the new skill.

[Artificial Magic Core Harmonizer Lv 1] - 20 Bio

[An artificial organ that synchronizes control over the magic core’s Mana with the organism’s motor needs. This synchronization reduces the delay between thought and execution of magic, increasing the efficiency and control of Mana usage at each level.]

For someone with great magical potential like him, this skill was like giving wings to a tiger!

Without hesitation, Lohan spent 20 Biomass to purchase this evolution and began to feel the change.

The moment the Biomass was consumed, Lohan’s core, which had previously pulsed like a rough engine, flooding the Mana channels scattered throughout the jelly in a chaotic manner, underwent a sudden compression.

First came silence, from a "noise" that he had not even realized existed in his body before.

The constant internal pressure that Mana exerted against the cell walls of his jelly disappeared, replaced by a feeling of lightness and control.

It was as if the messy interior of his bluish mass had suddenly been filled with thousands of invisible filaments of high conductivity.

Then came clarity. 𝕗𝚛𝚎𝚎𝐰𝗲𝗯𝗻𝚘𝚟𝚎𝗹.𝕔𝐨𝕞

Lohan felt the new "organ" mesh around the [Magic Core Lv 5] like a perfect gear, filtering every pulse of energy that had previously leaked out in a crude form, greatly accelerating the process of transporting Mana through his body.

It was an incredible feeling of connection, as if he had previously controlled Mana with a 250 ms ping, and now upgraded his internet to one that let him play at 150 ms. The time discrepancy still existed, but the control that this high speed brought was incredible.

Lohan extended a tentacle, and even before completing the physical movement, the Mana was already there, concentrated and stable at the tip of the limb, ready to conjure an [Ice Spike].

He was fascinated by that feeling.

[Magic Core Lv 5 → Lv 7]

[Total Mana: 21.89 → 26.47]

[Artificial Magic Core Harmonizer Lv 1 → Lv 2]

Upon purchasing these evolutions, Lohan felt the Magic Core inside him pulsing strongly, exuding Mana through his small gelatinous body, but being quickly suppressed and controlled by the Artificial Harmonizer, making the leaking Mana much calmer and more comfortable for his body.

To upgrade the Magic Core by 2 levels, Lohan spent 66 Biomass, and to evolve the Harmonizer, he spent another 27.8 Bio, totaling an expenditure of over 93 Biomass!

This was an astronomical amount for Lohan a week ago, but for the current Lohan, after calculating the Biomass gain per hour after rising to Level 03, he was already digesting 49 Bio/h!

NunuNote: For data nerds like me, here is the current calculation of Lohan’s Biomass Digestion Speed: [Base Digestion: 10.48 bio/h + (210% Mass Expansion Lv 7: 22 bio/h) + (50% Passive Digestion Lv 5: 5.24) = 37.72 /h + (30% Clone Lv 3 : 11.31) = 49.03 Bio/h]

Since his density and body size were greater now, even if he digested biomass for a few hours, he would still be able to maintain this value without waste, but with how cheap some of his skills still were, an idea came to mind.

’After recovering my reserve stock of biomass, I’m going to treat myself to buying a few dozen evolutions hahaha!

He was so excited that he didn’t notice the strange look Lisa gave him when she saw the little creature writhing with happiness while digesting a human head.

Lohan formed a small hand next to his body and gave her a big thumbs up. "Yes, and it was a great Skill, now I’ll be able to cast spells faster and possibly spend even less Mana."

As a race with a high magical and spiritual affinity, she knew how important a skill like that was!

Noticing her impatience, Lohan felt a little guilty.

She could be killing monsters on her own and getting stronger, but because of him, she felt quiet and just waited, chatting to kill the boredom.

Since Lohan entered Elysium, this had been his basic routine, so he was used to it and didn’t realize how boring and unproductive it was for other Players, but on the other hand, he also didn’t want to give up the skills he could receive by digesting these other humans.

With such a good harvest from the Mage alone, what else could he possibly receive from the others?

Instead of trying to trick Lisa into leaving him alone, Lohan was just honest with her.

"I believe staying here is more useful for my growth than going to kill other monsters, do you think you can handle those bears alone?" he asked.

Hearing his question, the fox instantly frowned and stared at him in frustration. "Couldn’t you have said that earlier?"

Angry, she didn’t even answer his question and ran off, leaving the little Slime to digest the bodies of the four humans alone.

Looking at her back as she walked away angrily, Lohan felt guilty. After all, he really could have said that earlier and not "stolen" those 30 minutes of grinding from her.

’Damn... things were simpler when I just rolled around aimlessly, but if it weren’t for her, I’d still be at Level 01 and might not even have this opportunity to digest these humans. What to do?’

When it came to dealing with evolution efficiency or acquiring new knowledge, Lohan was very confident, but when it came to close interpersonal relationships, he had very little experience.

’In the other world, I had no friends because of my physical disability. In this world, I have no friends because of my social and financial disabilities... and when I do make a "friend," I find that I don’t know how to deal with them either.’

While digesting the heads of the other three humans, Lohan’s mind kept thinking about what he could do to make it up to Lisa.

Chapter 55: 55 - Many Evolutions!

If it were anyone else in that situation, having to stay practically motionless for hours while digesting a corpse, that person might have already gone mad.

But for Lohan, it was great.

When he finished digesting a head, the notification of a new evolution would sound, which made him even more excited, and he would quickly scroll to the next corpse.

While he was at it, he also took the opportunity to search the bodies of these people for something useful, and surprisingly, he found some copper coins!

Excited, Lohan generated a small clone and, with difficulty, controlled it to search the bodies of these people even more carefully.

All in all, he had found a total of 23 copper coins!

At the current exchange rate, 1 copper coin was equivalent to $1 in the real world, meaning Lohan would need 30,000 copper coins, or 3,000 silver coins, or 300 gold coins!

Obviously, these 23 copper coins would change almost nothing in the debt he owed, but feeling the texture of those coins and thinking that this was the first money he had received in the game, a very pleasant emotion arose.

To exchange Elysium coins for real-world credits, all he had to do was open an interface in the game’s System, and that was it.

But considering that he didn’t earn this money himself, even though it would probably be worth almost nothing to someone in the High Zone, Lohan still kept it delicately inside him, being careful not to digest these coins, and waited to share them with Lisa.

She might not need this money in the real world, but while it was possible to convert game coins into real money, the opposite was impossible, so the only way to earn money in the game was by playing.

And that made these coins much more valuable than the $1 per copper coin.

From what he had seen on the internet, in some beginner villages there were large guilds that offered up to $7 for each copper coin.

’Unfortunately, I’m not in a beginner village like that...’

But he didn’t let it get him down. Finishing digesting the humans, Lohan finally looked at his Status screen.

Even buying only the cheapest evolutions, this wave of purchases still cost more than 150 Biomass, turning Lohan, who was feeling like a rich and powerful Slime, back into a poor slime again, but even more powerful.

He had even become a little smaller because of the large consumption, but he did not let it get him down.

With the increase in the level of [Memory Resonance] from Lv 2 to Lv 5, by digesting the minds of these humans, Lohan was able to obtain clearer memories from their minds, but with the level still low, Lohan could only see the last memories before they died, with each level upgrade further increasing the distance he could see.

Unfortunately, the gains that the other humans brought were disappointing.

The three evolutions he received were practically useless, at least for his current stage.

[Affinity with Heavy Weapons]

[The organism assimilates the muscle memory and coordination necessary to wield axes and large impact weapons more easily. Improves balance and leverage when handling objects with weight concentrated at one end.]

This skill was gained from the human warrior, and yes, it was a Skill, not an Evolution.

Like [Ice Spike], this Skill did not have an option to spend Biomass to evolve further, and considering that Lohan didn’t even use weapons, it was practically useless.

[Static Shadow]

[Monocular Telescopic Vision Lv 1]

[Allows you to focus your visual perception on a single point at a long distance, reducing your peripheral field of vision in exchange for an optical zoom. Makes it easier to identify static targets at over 200 meters.]

When testing this skill for the first time, Lohan felt no side effects.

’Maybe because my vision is 360 degrees? So the skill can’t narrow my peripheral vision because I don’t have any?

Without the side effect, this skill was the best of the three and could become very good in the future, but for now, the change it brought was not very significant.

It wasn’t a huge change, but Lohan felt much more confident and excited to explore and fight.

The current problem was...

Was Lisa calmer?

Not knowing how to react, Lohan did the only thing he could think of: he acted as if nothing had happened.

Chapter 56: 56 - Gift

[Halon: I’m done digesting here, how are you doing?]

[Lisa: Killing some bears.]

[Halon: Is there room for one more?]

After Lohan’s message, the chat was silent for a few seconds until a reply arrived.

[Lisa: I’ll be right there to pick you up.]

"Okay, it seems she’s calmed down a bit." Lohan thought with relief.

While Lisa was away, Lohan did not continue to absorb the bodies of humans, but returned to digesting the Mana Stone that Aeliana had given him the day before.

As a Level 11 monster’s Mana Stone, the density of biomass in it was insane.

And that made even more sense to him after he rose to Level 03 and realized that the experience needed to level up instead of increasing by 100, actually doubled.

He needed 100 points to rise to level 2, 200 points to rise to level 3, and now he needed 400 points to rise to level 4.

Fortunately, killing more powerful enemies also yielded more experience, to the point that after the battle against the humans, added to the little experience Lohan had left from the last grind, he already had 63 points, with only 337 points left.

In a few minutes, a familiar smell was noticed by [Chemosensory Aptitude Lv 5], now becoming much more noticeable after this evolution leveled up, but mixed with an unpleasant smell of blood.

Looking in the direction he smelled it, Lohan noticed the little white fox approaching, still in a semi-transparent state.

Reading a common human expression was easy, reading a human expression trained not to reveal thoughts was difficult, and doing so with a fox was almost impossible. He didn’t know what she was thinking, but based on the principle of "If I don’t embarrass myself, the embarrassment will be yours," Lohan acted normally with her.

"Hey," he said as he rolled toward her and waved his small, cute hand casually. "I finally finished digesting, I got one useful skill, one almost useless skill, and one that I don’t even know if I’ll ever use."

Lisa looked at him with half-closed eyes, but she didn’t force the issue either. "Great, added to the experience I’ve accumulated over the last few days, I only need to kill two or three more bears to reach Level 04."

This didn’t surprise Lohan. When he was at Level 01, she was already Level 03.

"Right, so let’s help you level up first, I can act as support for you." She said as she rolled onto her back.

The fox looked at him for a few seconds, noticing how naturally he climbed onto her back, and controlled the urge to roll her eyes. "Okay, let’s go, I have to log off in a little while."

"Wait!" Lohan remembered something.

Lisa looked at him suspiciously, hoping he wouldn’t come up with another excuse to delay leveling.

Since she didn’t have an evolution skill like him, or training in the use of skills, the most direct way for her to get stronger was by killing monsters.

Looking back, she saw the slime stick its small hand inside itself and pull something out, still a little wet from the jelly of its body, but which quickly dried after it absorbed it back.

In its palm were 23 copper coins!

"Did you get those from those corpses?!" She asked excitedly, completely losing the exaggerated indifference she had been forcing herself to show.

Lohan was surprised by her reaction, but pleased. "Yes, I think they only carried the coins they needed for daily use, probably the real reserve must have been left at their base, but still, this is the first money we’ve earned."

Lisa looked at it with great curiosity, wondering what could be done with it, until she saw Slime’s little hand go back inside to store the money, and then come back out with half the coins, extending it to her.

"Here, this is your share. I believe a 50-50 split is fair for both of us, what do you think?" Lohan asked.

Her eyes widened, surprised that he wanted to share that money with her.

In her life in the real world, money was practically infinite. There had never been anything she wanted that money couldn’t buy, so to her it was just a convenience.

But in Elysium things had changed, she couldn’t use her family’s money, at least not at this stage. So seeing those coins being offered awakened something new in her heart.

"Are you sure you want to share this with me?" she asked, confirming again.

Lohan reached out his hand again, almost pouring the coins onto the fox’s head. "Come on, take it for yourself. We both fought for this, so it’s only fair that the reward be shared between us, just like the reward the elves will bring."

Lisa was touched, happy with Halon’s initiative to share it with her, especially believing that he came from the Lower Zone and knowing how desperate for money the people there were.

But then came an awkward scene.

Lisa wanted to take the coins from Slime’s hand, but when she reached out with her paw, she realized she didn’t even have a thumb to hold it!

Elysium had no personal inventory; if the Player wanted to carry something, they would need to physically take it from one place to another.

Seeing her reaction and her paw frozen, not knowing how to act, Lohan remembered something.

"Wait a moment," he said as he rolled back to the dead assassin on the floor and rummaged through her body looking for something.

Lisa looked at him with her head tilted to the side in confusion, but waited patiently this time.

After a few moments, Lohan exclaimed, "I found it!"

Raising his small hand, he showed her a small brown cloth bag used to carry coins.

He hadn’t even considered it before because he could carry things inside himself, but realizing Lisa’s situation, it proved useful.

Unfortunately, this was the only bag he hadn’t corroded, as it was the only one without any coins for him to steal.

Seeing a necklace around the woman’s neck, Lohan was not polite and took it without a second thought. The necklace did not emit any magical signals and did not even look like valuable jewelry, so he wrapped the cord around the bag with a knot and made a small handle.

"Come here, let’s see if this will fit you well."

He said excitedly, proud of what he had done.

Lisa looked at it strangely, not quite sure how to react to Halon’s "gift."

She didn’t feel so bad about the coins because she had also fought and believed she deserved them as much as he did, but not the cloth bag, not because it looked valuable, but because it looked like a gift.

Seeing the fox standing there without reacting, Lohan was confused for a moment but didn’t care, rolling toward her and gently passing the string around her neck and fastening it.

"How about it? Is it comfortable? If it’s not good, I can take the money for you too, I’ve gotten bigger and now it even fits more stuff inside," he said casually.

Lisa looked at the small brown bag tied around her neck and realized that moving around with it would not be very comfortable, but for some reason she felt reluctant to give it back to Halon.

"It’s fine, I like it," she said quietly, looking away.

Chapter 57: 57 - Inside Information

"He’s approaching, dodge to the left and take advantage of his movement to counterattack with [Spirit Fire]." Lohan said as he clung to Lisa’s back and controlled his internal Mana to create an [Ice Spike] as well.

With the [Artificial Magic Core Harmonizer Lv 2], Mana flowed through his body naturally, extending out of the membrane with ease and molding itself into an ice spear in less than a second.

The last thing he managed to do was widen his eyes before the fire exploded and sent his large body flying a few meters backward.

Even though the explosion wasn’t powerful enough to send his body flying through the forest, that little push was enough to unbalance the big monster long enough for Lisa to conjure another fireball and hit his head again, killing the large creature.

[Experience: +6]

Lohan didn’t care much about that, having confirmed the bear’s death, he quickly jumped off the fox’s back and began to digest the big guy’s head.

Lisa didn’t mind this, as it had already been decided that this would be the last bear of the hunt today and that Lohan could spend a few minutes digesting it before she took him back to the clearing where he met the elf every night.

At that moment, she was only focused on the improvement she received from rising from Level 03 to Level 04. 𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺

For Lohan, the most noticeable change was that the energy in the air around her became stronger, and her body size also became slightly larger, but she was still slightly smaller than him.

But for Lisa, the changes were incredible.

She became stronger, faster, more agile, more flexible, her internal Mana increased, and even the ease with which she could control her skills increased.

Meanwhile, Lohan extended two small hands and began to turn the bear’s body over, opening its mouth to facilitate the digestion of the head and looking for any sign of something valuable hidden inside.

"Is any part of this big guy worth anything? It would be nice to be able to sell this for money..." Lohan commented a little frustrated.

Having finally opened up a possible channel to earn money, he was eager to use it immediately, but unfortunately he didn’t know what was valuable and didn’t want to carry useless parts of the bear inside him.

As a Level 04 creature, it was even possible that the bear had a Mana Stone inside it, but Lohan had no idea where it was, and with a body as big as this, the time spent finding that Mana Stone would be better invested in digesting more heads and killing more monsters.

Finishing evaluating the gains, Lisa suddenly asked Lohan something confused.

"Halon, why do you only use that ice magic?"

Hearing this question, Lohan replied absentmindedly, still rummaging through the bear’s body. "Because it’s the only offensive magic I know."

At this answer, Lisa tilted her head in confusion. "But haven’t you tried to learn other offensive magic?"

Lohan was confused by her question. "I haven’t received any new magic when leveling up, nor have I encountered any creatures with powerful or useful magic so far, so I haven’t learned anything."

"I’m not talking about that." She interrupted, extending her paw forward and generating a small white ball of [Spirit Fire], controlling it around her and frowning as she concentrated on the ball.

To Lohan’s surprise, the fireball gradually stretched out, turning into a line of fire!

"What?! How are you doing that? Wasn’t your skill a fireball?" He asked in shock.

But Lisa shook her head in denial. "No, my skill is called [Spirit Fire], I just use the fireball form because it’s the easiest right now, but little by little I’m developing my control to use it in more diverse ways."

--BOOM!

This information was a mental explosion for Lohan.

Stopping to think, he had never analyzed how [Ice Spike] actually worked.

In his mind, since he had received the [Ice Spike] skill, that was the skill he had available, and that was what he would use to deal with enemies.

But then he looked again at the description of his evolution.

[Magic Core Lv 6]

[The vital core undergoes a qualitative transmutation, becoming a magical energy engine. Emitting constant pulses that saturate the cellular structure, forcing the opening of Mana Paths through the biomass to support, filter, and circulate raw energy throughout the organism.]

’Actually, the description of this skill is literally the explanation of the formation of a magic core that mages in general use, and considering how deep all the systems and mechanics of this game are... if this really is a game, maybe it’s worth it for me to focus on trying to learn this too?

When this idea popped into his mind, it wouldn’t go away.

Lohan began to analyze his Mana control just as he controlled his own body, using creativity and trying to understand patterns to use it in more efficient or different ways!

Lisa noticed his state and didn’t interrupt.

This information was something her family had paid a fortune in government investments to obtain, and even though she had given it to Halon for free, she had no regrets.

’Now we’re even,’ she thought, shaking the cloth bag with 11 coins that now seemed even lighter.

Chapter 58: 58 - Evolution in the Real World

Taking off his helmet, Lohan slowly reached out his hand and began to feel the physical changes he had undergone.

Not only had he risen from level 02 to level 03 that night, but he had also evolved several skills to a higher level.

If before he had felt only a subtle change when leaving the game, with only small details making his routine slightly different, this time the change was huge.

The same changes he felt in Elysium, he felt in a slightly weaker way in the real world as well!

"Unfortunately, I can’t quantify how much it has actually changed in me now, but I feel like I’ve leveled up in the real world too!" He thought in wonder as he looked at his own hand.

But the most surprising thing about it all was a new sensation he felt.

’It’s like... like I can feel the blood in my veins, but I’m sure it’s not blood...’ He thought confusedly, closing his eyes to feel it better. ’This is a very familiar feeling, similar to... SIMILAR TO MANA!’

The feeling, although familiar, was still different because his body was now solid.

The Mana in Halon’s body flowed freely, with him controlling it in any direction he wanted.

In the human body, however, the Mana followed a fixed path, flowing like blood in the veins and even resembling the visual representations he had seen in the other world about the Chakra paths that characters had.

Then a bold idea came to his mind.

Reaching out his hand, Lohan tried to reproduce the sensation he had felt dozens of times in the other world, controlling the Mana within himself to form a small arcane rune at his fingertips that slowly generated a small Ice Spike!

’No way...’

Having another idea, Lohan kept his hand extended forward and controlled the Mana within himself to reproduce another sensation.

Even without a real ’skill’ in this world, Lohan had used this skill in so many battles in Elysium that just as he digested biomass manually without relying on the skill, the skin on his hand also began to slowly change color with just precise manual control!

Just like the [Ice Spike], reproducing [Pigmentation Mimicry] was painfully slower than in the other world.

Perhaps because of the difference in biology? Perhaps because he was weaker than his Slime body? Perhaps he hadn’t completely merged? There were so many ’maybes’ that he just gave up thinking about it and let himself smile broadly.

It was a difficult night to fall asleep, as the excitement over the changes he was feeling kept him awake.

Having a normal, functional human body was already a gift that Lohan was grateful for every day, but having the possibility of integrating his Slime body into Elysium, which he practically used more than his human body at this point, and improving his body was an idea that wouldn’t let his heart calm down.

Fortunately, the fatigue he felt from the few hours of sleep he had been getting in recent days spoke louder, and his mind shut down.

-xXx-

When he woke up, it was still dark outside, probably still at least an hour before his usual wake-up time, but the feeling of power returned and Lohan woke up quickly.

Apart from Elysium, he wasn’t interested in any entertainment media in this world, so to pass the time, Lohan ate a nutritional solution and started exercising.

Last night he had increased his biomass gain by at least 40%, and this caused his nutrient absorption rate to skyrocket as well, to the point that within seconds of eating the nutritional solution, Lohan felt that he had absorbed everything and the energy in his body reached an unimaginable peak.

With nowhere to expend it, he set out to exercise.

Exercises that he could previously only do 10 reps of, with the gains accumulated in the last few days, he had already increased to sets of 25 reps for each exercise.

It was not yet at the level of human athletes, but the road ahead was bright.

Putting on his protective mask, which probably now only served to blend in with the crowd, Lohan covered his huge smile and went to college.

Unfortunately, without a stable source of income, he still could not miss classes, but that future was near.

Surprisingly, his classmate from the Lower Zone who played Elysium also got on that bus, and Lohan noticed the difference right away.

When the boy got on the bus, the biomass he absorbed from the air had increased considerably.

Apparently, the boy also noticed that something was wrong, because when he got on the bus, he froze, looked around surreptitiously, and decided to continue, squeezing himself between other passengers from the Lower Zone.

Lohan kept his eyes on him, trying to understand what had changed, because the feeling he had was somewhat familiar.

Unfortunately, he couldn’t figure out the reason for it before arriving at college and gave up.

The walk to class was normal as always.

With each passing day, people became more and more excited about Elysium, commenting on how realistic the game was, how fun it was to play, but how frustrating and painful it was to die and have the death penalty increase more and more.

There were even players with above-average bases acting as if they were desperate because when they died, they had lost that advantage, becoming normal like everyone else.

But Lohan noticed that despite their frustration, these players were just that, frustrated, not truly sad or desperate for losing something like that.

"Maybe they haven’t realized how valuable above-average status is..." He thought with a sigh, not really caring.

99% of the players in college were students from the Upper Zone, so for these people to lose some privilege in Elysium was good news for Lohan.

Upon entering the classroom, he was surprised to find Isabella Vance already there, sitting casually in one of the chairs pretending to listen to a group of girls talking about a handsome boy they met in Elysium.

Coincidentally, when the door opened, her gaze moved in that direction and she noticed Lohan.

Their eyes met for a fraction of a second, causing them both to freeze momentarily, feeling a strange familiarity, but Lohan quickly looked away and went to sit in his usual seat.

Even though he was curious about this strange feeling, facing someone who could literally end his life for not liking how she was looked at, Lohan didn’t dare to stare any longer and isolated himself again in the world of the Lower Zone students.

He didn’t notice that Isabella kept her gaze on him for a few more seconds before looking away and pretending to listen to what the girls around her were talking about.

But next to Isabella there was someone who noticed, and that person didn’t like it at all.

Not only because they were jealous of the attention Isabella had given to a beggar from the Lower Zone, but also because they already had reasons to dislike this smelly beggar.

Staring at Lohan for a few more seconds, this person clenched their fists and had an idea.

Chapter 59: 59 - Anger

Julian Neal didn’t like being ignored, but he accepted it coming from Isabella Vance, since he knew how heavy her surname was.

But being ignored because someone he considered part of the disposable furniture of the Lower Zone was attracting the attention of the person he wanted to win over, Isabella Vance, who rarely deigned to look at anyone, dedicating just a second of attention to Lohan was the trigger for his inflated ego.

He got up and walked over to Lohan’s place, stopping arrogantly beside his table.

"You’re very brave today, Hayes. Is that the effect of the pathetic ’help’ you gave the girl yesterday?" Julian said, tapping his knuckles on Lohan’s desk. "I thought that after telling lies in Dr. Aris’ class, you would have the decency to disappear. Has the air of the slums finally fried what was left of your brain?"

Lohan was genuinely surprised, but he didn’t look up right away.

He was busy feeling the Mana circulating through his arm when Julian approached. The sensation was warm and alive, very different from the slightly cold fluidity he felt in Slime’s body.

But this interruption annoyed him.

’Damn, I don’t get in anyone’s way in class, I just want time to pass as quickly as possible so I can go home and play Elysium, but why can’t these people just study in peace?

’Does this guy really have nothing better to do?’ Lohan thought, letting out an audible sigh of irritation.

If it were the old Lohan in his place, he would just bow his head and let Julian humiliate him as much as he wanted, as long as it ensured his safety for a little while longer.

But the current Lohan was getting fed up with these spoiled people from the upper class.

In such an unequal society, rich people got richer and poor people got constantly poorer, and generations upon generations of rich people living in comfort, luxury, and hearing since childhood how superior they were, made most of these children feel special, entitled to step on and humiliate the "poor beggars" of the Lower Zone.

Coming from a world where society, though imperfect, still gave anyone the opportunity for social advancement... a place where even he, a physically disabled man, had earned doctorates while studying from his hospital bed, being treated this way by a boy of no quality was even more humiliating.

Resisting his body’s urge to bow his head and let Julian do as he pleased, Lohan kept his spine straight for the first time.

"The air in the Lower Zone is toxic, Julian. Everyone knows that, even you..." Lohan replied, finally raising his eyes and staring at the boy. "The difference is that some of us are aware of it, and others, like you, just use your great-great-grandfather’s money to buy filters that hide reality. But filters don’t help with your own mediocrity, do they?"

Julian’s face changed from a mocking smile to a mask of restrained anger. In the Upper Zone, insults were veiled and full of etiquette, even people from the most powerful families limited themselves to maintaining decorum, especially in public like this.

Hearing the raw, direct truth from a "stinker" from the Lower Zone was like being hit with a thermal shock.

"You’re talking a lot for someone who depends on government handouts to keep from starving." Julian hissed with disgust, leaning forward while covering his nose in feigned disgust, even though Lohan didn’t actually exude the stench Julian constantly cited. "You know what’s funny? I’ve been looking at your records and noticed that your performance is only average... I can get someone like you kicked out of this college with a text message if I decide you’re a problem."

Lohan felt the anger inside him grow.

This was the same kind of threat he heard from the administrators of the hospitals he stayed in in the other world when he questioned the negligence of the treatment he received. But this time, Lohan wasn’t an invalid in a bed.

Julian gestured dismissively, causing the wrist projector on his right arm to glow. A sophisticated hologram floated between them, displaying the class schedule and Lohan’s data with a clarity that no cheap equipment from the Lower Zone like Lohan’s could reproduce.

Seeing Julian’s pride in using such mundane things to prove his superiority, Lohan had an idea.

He surreptitiously reached under the table.

He didn’t need to touch Julian’s arm; with the [Artificial Harmonizer] and Halon’s muscle memory, the Mana he had trained in the real world now obeyed basic control.

With the absorption of Biomass, he had already realized that Julian only had an Uncommon Base, something that gave him a great sense of pride, but that still had a huge difference between the evolutions that a Mythic class like Lohan’s gave.

"You talk about your power to make me disappear, Julian, but your power is all external.

Take away those toys, take away your father’s surname, and what’s left is just a scared boy who can’t even keep his own image standing," Lohan said quietly, but with the same seriousness and anger he used when dealing with complacent doctors in the other world, making Julian hesitate.

Not only had no one but his father ever had the courage to speak to him like this, he never imagined that a worm from the Lower Zone would have such audacity!

Without anyone noticing, Lohan sent a tiny pulse of Mana, tuned to cause harmonic interference in Julian’s pulse projector.

He didn’t try to cause an explosion or anything flashy, but only tried to control an energetic "prick" directly into the semiconductor circuits of that device.

In the next second, Julian’s hologram emitted a crackling sound, causing the previously clear image to begin glitching violently, turning a sickly green before collapsing into a cloud of blurry sparks.

The projector on Julian’s wrist instantly overheated, releasing a wisp of smoke that smelled like burnt ozone, leaving everyone in shock.
