Chapter 60: 60 - Humiliation

The projector on Julian’s wrist instantly overheated, releasing a wisp of smoke that smelled like burnt ozone, leaving everyone in shock.

Julian jumped back, holding his wrist in shock. "What... what the hell was that?! You did something to my holographic projector!"

"Me? I didn’t do anything. Did anyone see me go near your projector?" Lohan asked, raising his voice slightly as he looked around.

When the students from the Lower Zone saw his gaze, their expressions, which had been those of people watching a hero or gawking at a lunatic, quickly changed to fear, forcing them to look away and pretend they hadn’t seen anything.

Even though they believed Lohan hadn’t done anything wrong, they still didn’t want to get involved and risk losing their careers.

Only one student from the Lower Zone looked at Lohan for a few more seconds, nodding to him while hiding a small satisfied smile at the corner of his mouth.

That student was precisely the boy who exuded the aura of someone with a Rare Elysium Base!

As for the students from the Upper Zone, they just looked at Lohan with scorn, as if watching a clown show.

They knew Julian was wrong, they also believed that Lohan had done nothing wrong, but likewise, they also cared little about the beggar from the Lower Zone, so they just continued to watch the show.

Only a pair of eyes from the Upper Zone looked at it in amazement, feeling a very faint sense that something was wrong the moment Lohan fried Julian’s projector.

Lohan was not intimidated by not receiving anyone’s support, that was completely within his expectations, but this statement was not for these students, but for the cameras that were in the corner of the rooms, recording everything that happened.

Although the students and teachers acted without any consideration for the students from the Lower Zone, the mere fact that the college paid a subsidy for students from that Zone to study for free showed that at least the administration was not totally indifferent to them, so Lohan clung to that.

If Julian did something behind the scenes, there would be nothing the college could do, but being foolish enough to do it in the classroom, with so many witnesses and various recording devices...

So Lohan continued. "Maybe it’s Dr. Aris’ ’Induced Homeostasis’ affecting your cutting-edge technology, Neal." Lohan shrugged, without looking away. "It seems that the air we bring from the Lower Zone doesn’t take too kindly to these things... be careful what you flaunt around here."

Some students from the Lower Zone, who were still listening to the scene from afar, had to cough to hide their laughter. Seeing Julian Neal, an untouchable heir from the Upper Zone, waving his arm to clear the smoke from a piece of equipment that cost more than many of their shacks, was a priceless sight.

Julian clenched his fists, his eyes injected with hatred.

He looked at Isabella, who watched with visible contempt for the loss of control he had shown, and then looked back at Lohan.

The humiliation of having his "superior technology" fail in front of a beggar just as he was showing it off was a humiliation he didn’t know how to process.

"This isn’t over, Hayes. I’m going to find out what you did. And when I do, you’ll beg to go back to the sewer you came from."

He turned on his heel and stormed out of the room, not caring about the next class, with the wrist projector still sputtering pathetically.

Lohan just exhaled the breath he hadn’t even realized he was holding, feeling the Mana calm down in his veins like a river returning to its bed.

"I didn’t cause any of this, Julian, but if you think I’m going to stand by and wait for you to get ready, you’re very much mistaken... now that I know the potential of a Mythic Race, I’m going to show you the result of combining a Mythic Race and a Mythic Class."

Out of the corner of his eye, Lohan noticed that Isabella Vance hadn’t looked away from him, lost in thought.

She knew that cutting-edge technology didn’t break down like that for no reason, and added to the strange familiar feeling she had felt for a fraction of a second before Julian’s projector broke down, she knew it wasn’t a coincidence.

’Could he also...?’ she wondered in surprise.

-xXx-

After Julian left, the students returned to normal, commenting on this minor episode before returning to talking about random things.

Lohan stopped paying attention to this and focused only on himself, feeling the changes that Mana had brought him and how he could make the most of it.

Lohan kept his head down, acting like an ordinary student from the Lower Zone, as if the fight a few seconds ago had nothing to do with him, but his senses were in a state of hyperopia that no ordinary human in that room could comprehend.

His research began quietly, with not even the teacher’s presence in the classroom interrupting him.

He tried to map out how Mana behaved in the solid and restrictive receptacle that was the human body.

In Elysium, like Halon, Mana was like water in an ocean... vast, fluid, and malleable. In the real world, it was more like mercury running through narrow glass tubes. There was physical resistance, friction that heated his internal channels every time he tried to move the energy out of his chest.

"I think my molecular density in this body is my biggest obstacle..." Lohan analyzed, ignoring the buzz around him. "Not only is control over my Mana much worse here, but the recovery of spent Mana is several times slower due to the low concentration of Mana in the air and the high level of atmospheric pollution here..."

He closed his eyes, focusing on the sensation he felt when controlling Mana to fry Julian’s projector. That wasn’t a specific spell, it was just interference.

Lohan realized that, in the real world, his Mana control was still too weak to accomplish such grand things as he did as Halon in Elysium.

But using the advanced vision he received from Halon, he could visualize the frequency of his Mana and a slight oscillation of the holographic signals emitted by the projector, managing to create a short circuit in it.

This was a valuable discovery... in the real world, he wouldn’t need offensive spells so urgently if he could simply shut down the technological world around him.

Considering how advanced the technology was in this world, people’s dependence on these things was at a much higher level than in his previous world.

And with each passing second, he felt as if the connection between Halon and Lohan was becoming clearer.

He realized that level 03 in Elysium had not only increased his strength, but it was as if it had unlocked a connection between them...

Among the students in the upper zone around him, he began to feel the small pulsations coming from these people much more clearly. They were very weak Mana signatures, almost imperceptible at this distance, but still much more noticeable to Lohan, who felt that his detection was more accurate, but also that the energy emanating from these people was more intense today.

"I think this is because they are also passively integrating with their Elysium characters..." he concluded.

The difference between them was that while the others were like unlit lamps accumulating static energy, Lohan felt as if he were the only one there who already knew how to light and control that lamp.

This was both because of his efforts and because of the tips Lisa had given him over the last few days.

During class, no one else bothered Lohan, and he didn’t have the patience to waste time with anyone else, so as soon as class was over, he quickly went to the bus stop to return to Elysium.

Chapter 61: 61 - Weaver Spider

"Finally back in Elysium." Lohan thought contentedly, breathing in the fresh air and enjoying the last rays of sunshine before night fell.

The time in Elysium and on the planet he lived on were very close, with night in Elysium arriving just a few hours after night fell in the real world.

On his way home, Lohan noticed that the boy from the Lower Zone with the Rare Base was occasionally looking at him, but Lohan wasn’t in the mood to deal with it today, so he just leaned against a wall on the bus and continued to focus on improving his Mana control.

The two hours he had to spend on the bus to get home couldn’t be wasted, so he found this good way to pass the time.

With so much time available, his progress in controlling Mana was very good. He went from being a complete novice in the morning to a decent level of proficiency.

He was still far from the level he had as Halon in Elysium, but by the standards of the real world he knew, he felt he had made good progress.

Physical exercise was not avoided either. As soon as he got home, Lohan did as much exercise as his body could handle and only then entered the game.

On his friends list, Lisa was already online, probably killing monsters somewhere far away.

[Halon: Hey, good evening, have you been playing for a long time?]

Lisa took a while to respond.

Meanwhile, Lohan didn’t stand still. The Mana Stone that Aeliana had given him two days ago was finally about to be consumed.

Lohan was shocked at how long it took him to digest it completely.

Considering how high his digestion speed already was, he thought it would only take a few hours to digest everything, but adding to the fact that he couldn’t spend the whole day in the game passively digesting it, and the fact that he had to pause the digestion for a few hours the day before to get evolutions from the humans and monsters he killed, it made sense.

Fortunately, the waiting time came to an end.

After a few seconds with a digestion rate of 53.13 Biomass per hour, the Mana Stone disappeared.

[New Digested Matter — Magic Weaving]

[Evolution available.]

Lohan didn’t even see the notification because an intense memory instantly came to his mind, causing him to lose consciousness.

Suddenly, all Lohan saw was darkness.

Soon, he was thrown into a cold consciousness, where his vision was a chaos of gray blurs that occupied almost his entire field of perception.

While getting used to the Slime’s 360-degree vision was natural, the feeling of having eight eyes was very strange.

80% of what he saw was nothing more than shapeless blurs, while he felt pure indifference to anything that wasn’t food or a threat.

But when the 20% of clarity reached Lohan’s mind, the impact was brutal.

In those moments, the spider’s vision focused like a high-precision lens, revealing details he had never noticed, even with his enhanced Slime vision while using [Monocular Telescopic Vision].

Lohan felt the creature’s legs digging into a tree bark, but what really put him in a trance was the internal flow he was feeling.

He felt the Mana being compressed in the spider’s abdomen, passing through glands that transformed the pure energy into something solid and viscous.

The process was intoxicating... he felt the tension of the Mana being stretched into translucent threads that remained under his control even after detaching from the body.

In one of the clear sections, he saw the target: a Unicorn.

The creature, which exuded a pure and dazzling energy, was stretched between four trees, completely immobilized by a network of threads that barely reflected the light.

Lohan felt the spider’s euphoria, with each time the Unicorn neighed and tried to explode with magic to free itself, the threads glowed blue and absorbed the impact.

Surprisingly, Lohan could taste the prey’s Mana traveling through the threads and entering the spider’s body.

It was a constant drain that transformed the victim’s resistance into fuel for the web itself to grow stronger.

Seeing that mythical creature reduced to an organic battery, trapped in threads that Lohan now knew exactly how to make, made something snap inside him.

A frenzied sensation began to take hold of Lohan.

The hunger for power and the clarity he felt when absorbing it were like a drug!

He wanted to feel that pull, he wanted to feel the Mana of other beings flowing into him through invisible filaments. His mind was working at full speed, superimposing the image of that web onto his own clones and tentacles.

Suddenly, a loud "Ding" sounded in his mind, leaving him confused and making the memory that had been perfectly clear moments ago now blurred again.

When the memory finally dissolved and Lohan returned to his own Slime body, he was panting, or the equivalent of that for a Slime, with the bluish mass vibrating incessantly, expanding and contracting at an erratic pace, while small sparks of Mana jumped from its surface.

In his frenzied state, Lohan opened the game menu and purchased this evolution directly, ignoring the exorbitant price of 100 Biomass, and fired five thin threads toward the surrounding trees with familiarity.

Feeling the tension and perfect grip, a dark and satisfied thought crossed his mind... only to be interrupted again by another mental ’Ding’.

That second whistle finally brought him back to his senses, and he was shocked to realize what he had done.

The act of purchasing the skill and immediately starting to use it was not something he did on purpose, but actually something he did instinctively!

’Damn, it was as if I wasn’t thinking like myself!’

That feeling was so horrifying that Lohan was even afraid to use this evolution again.

Remembering the sound he heard twice that woke him up, he searched for the game interface where it came from.

Chapter 62: 62 - Oppressive Memories

Opening the interface, Lohan saw a red glow indicating an unseen notification.

[Lisa: Good evening, Halon. I was busy dealing with a group of boars that didn’t want to die.]

[Lisa: Halon? Are you in combat? Do you need my help?]

’So that was it... it was because of the two pings I heard notifying me of her messages that I regained consciousness? But why did I lose consciousness in the first place? When I absorbed the memories of other beings, I never felt anything this intense.’

This situation was frightening.

It only served to show him that Elysium really wasn’t just a game.

Because unlike games where the player watched a cutscene and experienced the experience visually, Lohan felt that his consciousness was being affected, his real consciousness!

[Halon: Lisa, we need to talk.

[Lisa: ??????

He knew that at that moment, the only person who could help him with information about Elysium that he couldn’t get anywhere else was this little fox, so he explained.

[Halon: Here’s the thing, a few minutes ago I finished absorbing the Mana Stone that Aeliana gave me...

When his explanation was over, Lisa was silent for almost a minute, until she replied.

[Lisa: Are you at the place I left you yesterday? Wait for me, I’ll come to you right away.

Her response was not reassuring at all.

But now there was nothing he could do but try to understand his situation.

[Halon: Yes, I’m in the same place, I’ll wait for you here.

In front of him were the five strands of Mana he had woven using the new Skill.

Looking at it, Lohan felt a strong sense of familiarity, as if he had been doing this for years, even though he had only just used this skill for the first time.

’This just shows how great an influence this memory had on me...’

Curious about this, he opened the menu and read the skill’s explanation.

[Magic Weaving Lv 1] - 140 Biomass

[Allows the creation of biological threads fused with Mana. The filaments are extremely resistant and adhesive, capable of immobilizing targets and passively draining the magical energy of any living being in direct contact with the web.]

The first thing that shocked him was the price to level up this evolution.

’140 Biomass just to level up this evolution from Level 01 to Level 02?! Damn, and I spent 100 Biomass without hesitation to buy this?! Okay, after trying this out, I really feel like the biomass wasn’t wasted, but still, doing this without my consent was shitty...’

Fortunately, after reading the skill description, Lohan realized that it was an almost perfect skill for a Slime like him!

The spider depended on its abdomen and special glands to transform Mana into the biological threads it produced, but Lohan, being a Slime, didn’t depend on any of that!

He could directly transform his body’s biomass from any part of his body to produce these biological threads!

This meant that he could simultaneously shoot biological threads in all 360 degrees around him!

Sure, this was a ridiculous idea, but being able to put something like this into practice showed how well this skill suited his race.

But Lohan didn’t have the courage to test it again.

He was truly frightened by what had happened a few moments ago, so he decided to wait for Lisa’s arrival to understand it better.

And he didn’t have to wait long, Lisa wasn’t hunting monsters very far away, and as she leveled up, her speed had also increased, so the time spent running back and forth was now shorter.

When she arrived, her worried gaze didn’t leave the slime for almost a minute, until she finally confirmed that it looked exactly like itself, and she let out a sigh of relief that even she didn’t know she was holding.

Then she spoke as she looked curiously at the five small threads. "So this is the magic web that you said was almost controlled to produce...? Explain to me again what happened to you, with all the details you can give me."

Lohan did just that.

Lisa already knew that he needed to absorb enemies to gain new skills, so it wasn’t a big surprise to her.

But hearing that he could enter the memories of the creatures he absorbed was something new; he had never told her that before.

Even when they first met, he learned from the Goblin’s memory that she had attracted the monster specifically for him, he made up an excuse that he had discovered her intention because of his enhanced vision as a Slime, not because he had read the goblin’s memory.

But at that point it didn’t matter, the feeling of losing control of his own consciousness was so terrifying that Lohan didn’t mind giving up this little secret to her.

And although she was a little surprised by this, Lisa wasn’t upset that he had hidden such a detail from her. She hadn’t been 100% transparent with him either, still keeping some secrets of her own, while knowing that he also still hid some secrets from her.

"From what you told me, the elf said that this was a Level 11 monster’s Mana Stone, am I right?" She asked as she looked at Lohan’s ’webs’ again.

He confirmed. "Yes... do you think the high level of the original owner of the Mana Stone was the cause of this?"

Lisa nodded. "That’s very likely. Remember I told you that Players stay in the beginner village until level 10? From level 11 onwards, they are forced to leave there and come to the Open World. This is because when they go from level 10 to level 11, they undergo a qualitative evolution, as if their level of existence had increased by one degree. This is so powerful that in one of these evolutions, it is even possible for a Player to raise their Race level to a higher level! Although the chance of this happening is not great."

Hearing this explanation, Lohan felt that it made a lot of sense.

Unlike the other memories he had absorbed before, the memories of this Spider really acted as if they were dominating his mind, as if he were dealing with a truly superior being!

And unlike other monsters, where he could see a clear image of their last memories, from the spider he only received vague and blurry memories, managing to understand and absorb only 20% of them.

Initially, he thought it might be because he wasn’t used to having eight eyes, but thinking about it now, it made perfect sense.

Looking at the webs it produced, Lohan confirmed that even the skill level he received was on another scale, with the initial price of 100 biomass proving this perfectly.

"Is there any danger in using this skill?" he asked worriedly.

Fortunately, the fox shook its head and replied in a deadly serious tone of voice. "I can’t give you 100% certainty, but I believe your problem was with the memory of the Mana Stone, not with the skill you received. But my recommendation is that until you reach at least Level 10, you avoid trying to capture the memories of Level 11 creatures, and if the creatures are Level 12 or higher, don’t even consider it."

Lohan realized the importance of this and nodded in agreement.

Seeing the sun setting, Lohan finally remembered Aeliana, who was probably waiting for him now!

Chapter 63: 63 - Spider-Slime

"Is it really okay for me to go with you to meet your elf friend?" Lisa asked, a little uncertain, this time walking alongside Lohan instead of serving as his mount.

They weren’t far from Lohan’s usual meeting place, so there was no need for Lisa to carry Lohan around.

And even though he enjoyed riding on the fox’s back, Lohan didn’t dislike the feeling of rolling around either.

At one point, he even felt that this sensation was more comfortable than walking on two legs!

But putting that thought aside, Lohan replied. "Don’t worry, Aeliana has always been a very good girl, and I believe her presence will be more beneficial than harmful to our relationship, since with you I will finally be able to talk to her for real."

Lisa nodded, agreeing with his point of view.

Although she greatly valued the time she had to grind and kill monsters, as the heiress of a giant financial group, she knew how valuable human relationships were in business.

In order to create a guild that would eventually depend on these relationships for trade, making a good first impression was essential, and she already had that, having saved the four elves the day before.

So she relaxed and asked a question. "About those webs of yours, how useful are they?"

Considering that all skills could be useful in some way, she figured the webs weren’t bad, and considering that they came from a Level 11 monster, she became even more curious.

"I feel like they’re more powerful than Spider-Man’s webs and useful for draining energy from enemies like Shang Tsung, so I think that’s my most powerful skill, even if it doesn’t work to eliminate an enemy instantly," he said excitedly.

When his fear of that skill passed, Lohan tested it thoroughly to see how it worked, and everything he noticed made he very satisfied.

"Who? Spider-Man? Shang Tsung?" She asked, confused, tilting her head because she didn’t recognize those names, which, as Halon said, seemed to be common knowledge.

Seeing her confusion, Lohan realized his mistake.

’I’m in an alternate world, it’s obvious that Marvel or Mortal Kombat characters didn’t exist here...’

Realizing this, he tried to find other similar characters for her to relate to in a way she could understand, but he realized that even in the memories of the old Lohan, there were no characters that interesting.

This world had deteriorated so much into rampant exploitation that people like him never had the opportunity to come home from school and watch some fun cartoons for children.

Most of his childhood was spent working or stealing to help buy food at home.

Thinking of a quick explanation, Lohan replied, "They are popular characters from stories that parents told children where I grew up."

Hearing this made the fox’s eyes sparkle with curiosity, turning to face Lohan intently. "What do you mean? Did your parents make up these characters?"

Lohan looked at her strangely. ’Didn’t this girl’s parents tell her stories when she was a child? Isn’t that basic?’

But they had already arrived at the place they had arranged to meet Aeliana, and Lohan had spotted the elf, so he put it off. "I can tell you those stories another time if you want."

"Okay." The fox accepted this with satisfaction.

Shortly after Lohan spotted the elf, Aeliana, who had been standing to the side, suddenly turned to Lohan and was surprised.

"Little friend, you’re back! Your Mana seems denser, did you level up?!" She asked excitedly, approaching the shiny Blue Slime with a diameter of 34 centimeters, but as she got closer, she noticed a small, slender creature next to the slime. "Did you bring a friend?!"

Instead of being worried or disappointed, Aeliana found this situation even cooler.

She learned that apparently this little friend of hers had helped a group of elves in the forest and was shocked to discover that they had even talked to him, excited that maybe she could too!

But when she found out that they only talked because of an ability that a Spirit Fox had used, she was disappointed, saddened by the thought that she wouldn’t be able to do it.

Who would have thought that her little friend would bring the Spirit Fox to see her too?! That way she could finally talk to her little blue friend.

"Hello, Aeliana, yes, this is my friend Lisa, and since I can finally introduce myself, my name is Halon." A calm and pleasant male voice sounded in her mind, causing Aeliana to freeze in alertness for a second, only to realize in the next second that this voice belonged to the little Slime in front of her!

"You can really talk!! Wow, I’m so excited! Why didn’t you ever tell me you were a boy?! All this time I thought you were a girl slime!" She said amused, not caring about the difference between imagination and reality, and crouching down, picking Halon up in her lap.

Suddenly, a slightly playful female voice sounded in her mind. "I don’t think you were that wrong, as far as I know, slimes are hermaphroditic beings, with no distinction between female and male."

Upon hearing this, Aeliana’s eyes sparkled even more, alternating her gaze between the little white fox and the slightly large Slime in her arms.

"I’M A MAN!" Lohan said indignantly, slightly irritated by Lisa’s playful expression.

He knew she didn’t believe what she was saying, since she knew he wasn’t really a Slime, but Aeliana didn’t, so now she would really believe that he was both a girl and a boy...

"Whatever, it’s not like it really changes anything for me." Lohan let it go.

After hugging Halon’s gelatinous, icy body, Aeliana turned to the little fox and asked. "Hello little friend, I’m Aeliana, are you the Spirit Fox who helped my little slime friend deal with the humans who wanted to capture the elven group yesterday?"

Lisa nodded in agreement, explaining the situation to Aeliana as it had happened. During the explanation, Lohan also added some details from his point of view, and Aeliana loved the experience.

"I’m so jealous!!! Even though I’m already a Level 20 Mage, my master said she would only let me go out to explore the world when I reached level 21...

I’ve been stuck at level 20 for 20 years because they don’t capture any monsters strong enough for me to kill and level up..." Aeliana said frustrated, unaware of the shock the slime and the fox felt upon hearing this information.

Chapter 64: 64 - Valuable Reward

NunuNote: Enjoy this Bonus Chapter, you deserve it from your PS and GT goals!

-xXx-

Lohan felt firsthand how terrifying the difference was between his lowly Level 3 and a Level 11 monster when he absorbed the spider’s memory, but hearing that Aeliana was only one step away from rising to an even higher level, he was completely shocked.

Even more so considering that with each level, the experience required to level up increased, if this continued, the experience required for her to level up would be 52 million!

Then a memory came back to him.

When Aeliana gave him the Spider Mana Stone a few days ago, he instinctively used [Chemosensory Aptitude] to smell it, and at that moment he smelled an intoxicating scent of something rich in Mana.

The smell was so good that Lohan even lost his mind for a few seconds just by smelling it... almost like when he was affected by the spider’s memory.

Just out of curiosity, he activated that skill again for a split second, just to confirm this theory, and when he activated it, the smell he smelled this time was even more intense.

It was like the scent of an untouched forest right after the rain, mixed with notes of wild honey and the freshness of a pleasant breeze.

Her pure Mana exuded an ethereal sweetness like a perfume of "concentrated life" that filled Lohan’s senses with an addictive serenity.

Every particle of energy that came out of the elf smelled like renewal and calm, acting like a balm that soothed his core and left him in a state of hypnotic ecstasy.

Fortunately, he only activated this skill for a fraction of a second, because if he had left it active for longer, it would have become worrisome, so no one noticed what he had just gone through. 𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺

’And that day I was thinking that the intoxicating smell I smelled came from the Mana Stone haha...’

At that moment, Aeliana and Lisa were talking about the adventures the two little monsters had had in the forest in recent days, until finally the subject returned to their feat that had reached her.

"Who would have thought that my little friend would actually be so powerful as to deal with a group of human mercenaries! Elara told me that among that group there was a Level 10 mercenary, a Level 9, and two Level 8s!" She said excitedly as she hugged Lohan a little tighter. "But I already knew you were special from the first time we met, hehe."

Lohan was a little embarrassed by that, especially by the playful look Lisa was giving him as she witnessed the scene, but he didn’t refuse Aeliana either.

She had already shown that she really cared about him before, to the point of even "stealing" from her own master to bring him something valuable (which he knew was probably not so valuable to them), but it still made him feel touched. Now small acts like that no longer irritated Slime.

"It was just luck, I admit I’m stronger than my peers, but if we had to deal with those humans head-on, the outcome of the battle would have been different." Lohan explained, not wanting to take more credit than he deserved.

Their ambush on the humans only worked because there were two elves already attracting their attention and holding the group of four people very well, otherwise Lohan’s clone would not have been able to sneak up on the distracted wizard, nor would Lisa’s attack have gone unnoticed by the high-level group.

Lisa also nodded, agreeing with Lohan’s statement, but Aeliana pretended not to hear anything.

"You don’t have to be modest with me..." She said as she gently placed Lohan on the ground and took something out of her pocket.

Looking at it, Lohan saw what appeared to be two wooden plaques with real details.

Lisa also didn’t understand what it was, remaining quiet and waiting for an explanation.

"These are your Thalendor ID cards. With these, you can enter and leave the city at will, and as long as you show them to any High Elf, your identity as a citizen of Thalendor will be recognized," she said as she handed one plate to the Slime and another to the fox.

But then a problem arose.

Halon was able to form a small hand to hold this ID card, but Lisa was a four-legged fox, she couldn’t hold anything with her hands.

Fortunately, Lohan thought quickly, rolling over to her side and forming another hand on the other side of his round body, using it to hold Lisa’s card for her to see.

The name tag was totally disappointing.

It really seemed to be just a wooden plaque, perhaps slightly larger than a credit card, with a drawing of some kind of coat of arms. This coat of arms was represented by an emerald green ogival shield, adorned with a silver ancestral tree with symmetrical branches that rose like living runes. Between the crown of this tree shines a golden eight-pointed star. A delicate bow and wooden staff crossed in the background, while golden leaves seemed to float around. Above, a crown of intertwined branches held bright green gems.

It was truly a beautiful work of art, but as an ID card it seemed rather useless.

Noticing Halon’s confusion, Aeliana quickly explained. "To mark this card as yours, you must drip a drop of blood..." Then she paused, a little lost as she realized that the slime had no blood, only its blue biomass jelly.

"Perhaps you could drip a little of your jelly? Then the card will recognize you and can be stored in a small spatial pocket connected to you. Each card like this is extremely expensive, given only to people who have contributed greatly to Thalendor, or people of great influence."

"Simply by presenting this card at establishments in Thalendor or to citizens of Thalendor will get you better prices on purchases, thanks to the gratitude people have for those who have contributed to the country."

Upon hearing this, their eyes lit up, but soon confusion arose again.

’What did we do that was worth such a valuable reward?’ That’s what they thought.

In their view, they had only saved a group of two adults who were protecting two children.

Although they could see that the dynamic between them was not that of parents and children, but more like two children and two servants, they just assumed they were saving some rich young people, or at most some minor nobles, after all, they didn’t even have guards protecting them.

’Did those children have some special identity in Thalendor?’ The fox’s eyes sparkled, and the Slime’s eyes didn’t sparkle at that moment only because he didn’t have any.

Chapter 65: 65 - Money?!

"Did the people we saved have any special identities?" Lohan asked directly.

Aeliana hesitated for a moment and replied somewhat regretfully. "I’m not authorized to tell you that information yet, but as I said, rewards like this come with many perks and are usually only given in exchange for great service to Thalendor."

For those who understand, half a word is enough.

’So those children definitely had special identities in Thalendor... and from the way the adults were surprised at Aeliana’s mention, and how the children spoke of her, calling her Lia, it’s possible that her identity isn’t simple either. That’s good, at least our start in Thalendor won’t be bad.’

Satisfied with the explanation Aeliana could give, Lohan used [Chemical Sense Lv 5] to try to detect something bad like a trap in this card, but everything he felt and saw proved what she said.

Mythologically, most of what Lohan had heard about elves was about how fair, honorable, and honest they were, but this information he had heard about elves was based only on fictional characters he had heard about in the other world, and among those representations of elves there were also representations that were not so fair and honest, such as the Blood Elves.

Sure, their betrayal of the alliance in WoW wasn’t entirely their fault, but their arrogance and sense of superiority caused them to do bad things in history, showing that even long-lived and wise creatures made mistakes, and Lohan didn’t want to be a mistake that the elves of this world made.

’Is it wrong to use stories from other worlds, which at this point I don’t even know if they are fictional or real, to judge someone who looks like a real person in front of me? Definitely, but at the same time, this is the only prior information I have in a situation like this, and it’s better to be safe than sorry after shit happens.’

Fortunately, Aeliana had always shown great sincerity, never displaying arrogance or anything expected of someone who called themselves a ’High Elf,’ and after seeing Lisa also examine the card he was holding in front of her and find nothing wrong with it, he felt more relieved.

Seeing their hesitation, Aeliana reached out her hand and golden leaves gathered there, quickly forming a wooden card very similar to the one she was offering them, only small differences in the coat of arms were noticeable, besides that her card had only two green gems at the top, instead of the three gems on their cards.

Deciding to give a vote of confidence to someone who had never done anything wrong to him, and who was theoretically giving him a reward for saving someone important to her society, Lohan poured a drop of his biomass onto the card, and a feeling of relief came over him.

He felt nothing wrong happening to him, only the emergence of the possibility of a magical way to store the card inside himself.

Thinking about doing this, the card glowed with golden leaves and crumbled in his "hand," the leaves being absorbed by the gelatinous body and disappearing as if they had never existed.

Imagining it returning to his hand, the same golden leaves formed again from within him and the wooden card solidified once more.

Lisa had also done the same thing, and the card in front of her disappeared.

"Carrying this card this way is much more convenient," Lohan commented, curious if he would gain anything if he tried to digest this card, but considering its current usefulness, it would be better to wait for a time when this card was no longer useful.

Considering how difficult it seemed to get one, according to Aeliana, it was better not to risk it now.

"Yes, haha, these cards were developed and improved by Thalendor’s magical and alchemical researchers centuries ago, and this final product is something that has only been distributed in the last 50 years," Aeliana said proudly.

’It’s ironic how she treats 50 years as if they were 5...’ Lohan found the situation funny, but didn’t comment on it.

Although he didn’t have much experience in relationships, limiting himself only to things he saw on TV or the internet in the other world, he at least knew that talking about a girl’s age was an indelicate subject.

So he changed the subject.

"So now with this we can freely enter Thalendor?" He asked excitedly.

Aeliana nodded excitedly. "Yes! I’d even like to take you there today if you’re free, but considering the time..." She said, looking up at the sky. "I think most of the stores are closed now, so maybe tomorrow would be better for a walk, how about it?"

This made Lohan and Lisa’s eyes light up.

Exploring the city alone with such small bodies could be dangerous, even with the ID cards that they still didn’t know how effective they were, but with a guide like Aeliana, it would be a completely different story.

"That would be amazing," he said in an excited voice, as if he were smiling while speaking mentally, even though he had no mouth.

"But before that, I have a question. Is there anything in the forest of Mythlorien that is valuable in Thalendor that we can get? After all, it would be better to visit the city with money in our pockets."

Lisa’s eyes sparkled even more at his question, which touched precisely on the most important point for them.

Upon hearing the question, Aeliana brought her small white hand to her chin and thought for a few seconds. "Hmm... I don’t know much about these things, but I heard my teacher complaining that she was angry with the Alchemy Shops for not restocking Shadow Serpent Digestive Acid. Maybe that’s something that would sell well?"

"Great! Maybe if I get enough of it, I can pay off the debt at the end of the month?" He thought excitedly.

It had been over a week since the loan was made, and he had just over two weeks to get at least $912 to pay the monthly interest the bank charged on the loan.

"And how much do you think this can be sold for?" he asked expectantly.

Aeliana kept her small hand on her chin and thought for a few seconds, until she shook her head and replied, a little embarrassed.

"I don’t know."

Chapter 66: 66 - Skipping Class

Aeliana explained to them where to find the Shadow Serpents, which she said were only Level 2 to Level 4 monsters, but because they hid in very dirty and cramped places, hunters usually avoided this target.

Lohan and Lisa were much smaller than hunters, so it would probably be easier for them to hunt these snakes.

With a clear goal in mind, Lohan and Lisa said goodbye to Aeliana and set off in the direction she had indicated.

"So, what do you think about that?" Lohan asked curiously, wanting to know Lisa’s point of view on the situation.

For him, digesting monsters or plants didn’t make much difference in his strength growth. In fact, he felt that killing monsters at that moment was slightly superior, since he could level up and use the increased stats to increase his base gains and then use the evolutions to develop even further.

Lisa, who was carrying Lohan, replied through the mental link with a thoughtful voice. "To me, this seems like a great opportunity. If we can create a harmonious relationship with the elves, when we decide to create our guild, we will have a stable source of income, even with the restrictions that our races bring."

Lohan agreed with her; so far, there seemed to be no downside to befriending the elves.

While ordinary players mostly appeared in human villages, they had to deal with what was available, and from the way things were developing, it seemed that things were going well.

"You accepted her invitation for tomorrow, are you thinking of skipping work to play?" Lisa asked in her usual cold voice, but there was a hint of curiosity in the background.

With her status, skipping college would not cause her any problems, but from what Lohan had shown so far, as someone from the Lower Zone, skipping work could cause a lot of problems.

Lohan thought for a moment. It was something he had briefly considered, but considering the possibility it entailed, both of getting a tour of Thalendor and possibly finding a source of income to pay off his debt, he knew he had to do it.

Going to college every day wouldn’t change his situation at all. In a few weeks, the bank would collect the money, and he wouldn’t be able to pay, being sent to prison or worse, having to go mining on some desolate planet to pay off the debt.

"I’ll figure something out... I haven’t missed a single day in the last year, I’ll just say I woke up feeling sick and couldn’t catch the bus to get there tomorrow," he said after a sigh. 𝘧𝑟𝑒𝑒𝘸𝘦𝘣𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝓁.𝘤𝘰𝓂

Lisa felt a little bad for him.

Halon was the first person she had really interacted with from the Lower Zone. Since childhood, her only interactions had been with other people from the Upper Zone, so she didn’t quite know how to deal with this.

’Could I offer him a job at one of Vance’s subsidiaries on his planet? If he worked for the family business, when he needed time off like this, I could easily arrange it... but if I suddenly got a job for a citizen of the Lower Zone of some planet, the family would notice and instead of helping, I could get him into even more trouble...’ She thought, frustrated.

But then she had an idea.

Thinking about how good this idea was, Lisa even stopped running and turned her head to face the Slime with a small confident smile on her fox-like face, breaking for a few moments the coldness she normally exuded.

"Halon, I have direct influence in some interplanetary hospitals, I can get you a three-day medical certificate that will cover your shift from Thursday to Saturday. Since work is prohibited on Sundays by federal jurisdiction, you will have four days of total isolation to focus on Elysium. With this opportunity, I will also do the same and stay home on those days."

Upon hearing this, Lohan’s membrane vibrated with excitement. "That’s perfect! But wouldn’t it be too much trouble for you to get something like that for me? Wouldn’t that get you in trouble with your connections at those hospitals?"

Hearing the concern in his tone, Lisa was a little confused, until she remembered that she was talking to someone who had no idea who she was and who genuinely worried that something could affect her like that.

Normally, people didn’t worry about her for things like that, because they already knew that with her identity, it was unlikely that anything could affect her, but feeling that concern... wasn’t bad.

"Don’t worry about it, just tell me if this medical certificate will be necessary," she asked, looking at him seriously.

Lohan didn’t think twice. "Yes, definitely, but how will you send it to me?" he asked, confused.

"Before we disconnect today, tell me your Syn Code and I’ll send it to you by message," she said in a calm voice.

Lohan gave her a thumbs up and didn’t refuse. Everyone in the human federation had an account on Syn, the largest interplanetary social network.

Since the old Lohan had no friends, his Syn was practically deserted, so he never cared much about it, but even without using it, the old Lohan had memorized his Syn Code, so it wouldn’t be difficult to pass it on to Lisa.

With that decided, Lisa sped up toward the Shadow Serpents’ nest.

The place was a little far from where they were, requiring Lisa to run for 40 minutes at the maximum speed of a Level 04 Spirit Fox to get there.

When they arrived, Lohan noticed that the scene ahead looked like an open wound in the forest.

The Shadow Serpents’ nest was in a narrow crevice between damp rock walls, where sunlight disappeared before touching the ground.

It was a suffocating place, covered in black mud that smelled of iron and decay, with passages so narrow that only the flexible, small bodies of monsters like them could navigate with ease.

The silence there was heavy, broken only by the occasional sound of something slimy slithering against the rocks in the depths of the darkness.

But neither of them felt fear, only excitement for the experience they would receive from killing these snakes, seeing these monsters as big money signs.

"Ready?" Lisa asked Slime, still attached to her back.

"As ever." Halon replied confidently.

Chapter 67: 67 - Serpent’s Crevice

NunuNote: Enjoy this Bonus Chapter, you deserve it from your PS and GT goals!

-xXx-

The black mud beneath Lisa’s paws muffled the sound of her footsteps as they infiltrated the crevice.

Lohan, who was firmly anchored to the fox’s back through [Selective Viscosity], activated [Chemosensory Aptitude].

Even though she didn’t really like carrying someone on her back, Lisa knew that in a situation like this, it was better to work on each other’s strengths and help each other with their weaknesses, which was to solve Halon’s low mobility and maximize his versatility.

The air there wasn’t just still... it reeked of a rotten smell that he hadn’t even smelled from the corpses of goblins or kobolds.

"I’m sensing four different smells ahead..." Lohan’s mental voice resonated, serious and focused. "One seems to be weaker, on the left, with three stronger ones clustered on the ceiling."

From Aeliana’s description, the Shadow Serpents were not just ordinary snakes, but something like filaments of living darkness, with scales that seemed to absorb what little light remained in the environment.

Before the beasts noticed their presence, Lohan began to prepare.

He detached a part of his mass, activating [Partial Division]. The small clone slid silently across the floor, positioning itself in the center of the narrow corridor, acting like a simple and foolish normal Slime, attracting the attention of the four predators that Lohan had sensed in that environment.

Simultaneously, Lohan focused on his new ability.

He felt the biomass being drained from his reservoir at an extremely high rate, merging with the bluish mana of his [Magic Core].

From his sides, fine, almost invisible threads began to shoot out, crossing the corridor just above the clone and attaching themselves to the damp rock walls.

As soon as the trap was set, Lohan felt very weak.

The process of creating the clone was already very tiring and exhausting, but it was nothing compared to the effort required to use [Magic Weaving].

"Now, Lisa!" He said, his voice noticeably weaker.

Lisa shot forward with a dash, like a white blur cutting through the gloom. She didn’t attack the three larger snakes on the ceiling directly, instead throwing a small ball of [Spirit Fire] at the weakest snake that was isolated!

The white glow of the fire momentarily blinded the creatures, creating a perfect opportunity.

The three stronger snakes reacted instantly, plunging from the ceiling like black whips toward the foolish "prey" on the ground, the dumb slime that was carelessly digesting mud biomass on the ground.

The moment the snakes reached the space between the walls, the trap was revealed.

The mana threads, learned from Level 11 Weaver Spider, did not break. The snakes writhed frantically, and the more they struggled, the more [Magic Weaving] drained their energy, transferring small pulses of mana back to Lohan’s core, replenishing some of the energy he had spent on it.

The Level 2 snake, escaping Lisa’s fire, slithered through a side crack and leaped in a desperate counterattack against the fox’s back.

Lohan felt the vibration through his [Instinctive Perception] and saw it clearly with his 360-degree vision.

"My turn," he thought excitedly, despite his weakness.

In a millisecond, Lohan consumed biomass, activating [Reinforced Exoskeleton] and [Membrane Reinforcement].

His bluish surface became as rigid as an insect’s shell and as dense as stone.

The snake tried to sink its fangs in, but instead of the sound of jelly being pierced, what came out was the sound of metal hitting rock, with the creature’s teeth only scratching the protected outer layer.

His protection was not very powerful against strong and destructive blows such as hammers, as his defense was now only one level above an eggshell, but against penetrating attacks with no footholds to fully use his strength, his resistance was more than enough.

Taking advantage of the proximity, Lohan fired an [Ice Spike] at point-blank range, piercing the level 2 snake’s head and pinning it to the cave wall.

Fortunately, the Mana used for spells was different from the Biomass used for his direct evolution skills.

Meanwhile, Lisa circled the three snakes trapped in the web with elegance.

She jumped across the walls, using the momentum to deliver fire-imbued kicks, while Lohan, acting as a mounted gunner, fired additional small corrosive clones to tighten the knot around the exhausted prey with [Selective Viscosity] and began digesting these monsters.

Without the need to actively control the movement of these clones, the process became much easier. He only needed to ’shoot’ them at the enemies, and as long as they weren’t destroyed, he could recover these bodies and not waste any biomass on it!

The mana drain was working, the snakes’ movements becoming increasingly slow and erratic.

"Let’s do this," Lohan said, sounding weaker but with a serious and confident voice.

Lisa let out a low roar and concentrated her Spirit Fire, incinerating what remained of the wills of the trapped creatures, while Lohan began to retract the threads, bringing the biomass of the defeated snakes close to him to initiate [Efficient Digestion] and recover the costs he had incurred in this battle.

Silence returned to the crevice, broken only by the hissing sound of flesh being decomposed by the acidity of the Slime.

With the battle over, Lohan’s jelly was contracting and expanding, like a lung desperately trying to breathe.

But despite his exhaustion, the excitement he felt from this battle was incredible.

In addition to the battle against humans, which relied heavily on the help of the elves, this was the first battle they fought together in this way throughout the entire combat.

Lisa was again resistant to this type of tactic, not feeling comfortable carrying the slime from one side to the other, but even she felt the satisfaction of a well-fought battle.

"Lisa, I think we make an incredible team." He said, genuinely excited about how good their synergy was in this battle.

Lisa was also not unscathed. Although she had not been attacked at any point, the amount of Spiritual Energy and Mana she had used in this battle was not low, leaving the little fox panting but with a subtle proud smile on her canine face, surprised to find herself agreeing with his statement more than she had imagined.

Chapter 68: 68 - Many Evolutions

Unlike other times when they hunted monsters, this time the duo finally had a target of which part of those monsters was valuable to loot.

Neither of them had a knife or anything like that to dissect these snakes, but with Lohan’s [Selective Digestion], the process of removing the Digestive Acid from inside the snakes’ bodies was made much easier.

The digestion process of the first snake was the most complicated, as Lohan had to digest small parts throughout its body to find the exact location of the Digestive Acid in that body.

After discovering where it was, the process became much easier.

Lohan didn’t need to digest the snake completely, he just needed to open a hole in the snakes’ stomachs, drain the Digestive Acid without digesting it, and store the liquid inside himself.

Being a life form almost entirely made of biomass, Lohan’s body was very malleable, to the point that he was able to store the liquid acid in an internal pouch he created, covered by a thin membrane he made inside himself, so that the acid would not be accidentally digested by him, nor would it constantly digest his biomass.

With such a simple way of carrying the acid, not a single drop was wasted from each snake.

And in addition to digesting the snakes’ bodies in search of digestive acid, Lohan also did not ignore the small heads of those creatures, penetrating his jelly through their eyes and digesting all of their brains.

These Snakes were not like the Level 11 Weaver Spider, so he did not bother to recover their memories and skills.

The immersion into the minds of the snakes was smooth, much less aggressive and oppressive than the process with the Weaver Spider.

Lohan felt his consciousness slip into a colorless world, where all he could discern were pulses of heat against the absolute cold of the stones.

There wasn’t much intellect in what he perceived, just basic predatory instinct.

He saw the world through a thermal filter, where Lisa glowed like a white supernova of radiant heat and he himself was a cold, bluish blob of biomass as the recent battle unfolded.

Unlike the previous frenzy, this resonance only refined his senses, without influencing his mind as the spider had done.

Of the four snakes, Lohan received a new skill and four upgrades to skills he already had.

[Thermographic Perception Lv 1]

[Allows you to detect heat variations in the environment through the membrane, mapping thermal signatures of living beings. Facilitates the identification of hidden or camouflaged targets in zero visibility environments through infrared radiation.]

That was the new skill he received.

A little disappointing for someone who expected to receive something related to shadows, given the name of these snakes, but still, something very useful for him, especially when seeing through the snakes’ eyes how practical it was in completely dark environments.

At this point, Lohan was feeling as if he was turning into a living tracker, with so many tracking and perception skills he had accumulated.

The [Thermal Perception Lv 1] in particular did not directly change his combat or tracking power, as he already had a high level in that area, but adding it to the list of tracking skills he already had was very good.

[Thermal Perception Lv 1 → Lv 2]

The first upgrade he received when absorbing another snake was precisely for this new skill, making his thermal perception even more accurate.

[Chemosensory Aptitude Lv 5 → Lv 6]

This was the second upgrade he received, a nice increase in his sense of smell, but another thing that didn’t change his combat power.

[Instinctive Perception Lv 8 → Lv 9]

When he saw yet another upgrade to his perception, Lohan wished he could roll his eyes.

[Efficient Digestion Lv 15 → Lv 16]

The last evolution was an upgrade that left him wondering whether to be happy or sad.

Since he didn’t need to spend Biomass to evolve this, Lohan saved 28 units, which was good, and increased his total biomass gain from 53.13 to 58.40 Biomass per hour, which was a great increase, but considering that he wanted to level up first and only then evolve this skill, he was a little regretful.

"Forget it, it was fate that evolved my skill and I have no reason to be disappointed. That’s the downside of digesting the brains of enemies and using [Memory Resonance] on them... sometimes it can give me a good evolution, other times I’ll have to deal with what I get." He calmed down.

After 40 minutes, Lohan had absorbed everything he needed from these snakes, saving a lot of time by not having to digest everything, and recovered much of the energy spent in this battle.

Lisa had been ready for a while, but considering that Lohan’s presence was essential in combat, since she was having a little difficulty seeing and sensing the spirit of beings with so little intelligence, she waited patiently for him.

"Okay, I’m done here, we can proceed deeper into this crevice." Lohan said as he stretched his gelatinous body as if he were yawning.

Lisa looked at him expectantly, and together they continued hunting these snakes.

Now without having to worry about waking up early, the two decided to hunt for several hours to ensure they would have enough Digestive Acid to sell for a lot of money in Thalendor.

After 15 minutes of cautious walking through the narrow crevice, they found a group of snakes and killed them all, with Lohan storing more and more Acid inside himself during the 40-minute rest they took for his digestion.

During that time, Lohan’s experience bar rose steadily, in addition to the various evolutions he achieved by digesting these snakes.

Unfortunately, he realized that after digesting 10 snakes, the evolutions he received decreased in frequency, with this species ceasing to evolve him after the 15th snake.

With that, the hunting speed became even greater, since now they didn’t have to wait so long for Lohan to digest the skills from the snakes’ brains.

He still didn’t know if this number 15 was the limit of his skills, or if it was because the snakes were too weak.

In short, he received 13 evolutions in total, the previous 4, 1 new Skill, and these 4 subsequent evolutions:

[Thermal Perception Lv 2 → Lv 4]

[Chemosensory Aptitude Lv 6 → Lv 7]

[Body Density Lv 7 → Lv 8]

The new skill he received was not an evolution like the previous one, but a magical skill like Ice Spike and Pigmentation Mimicry.

[Threshold Mimicry]

[While in shadows or dark places, the user’s body absorbs part of the darkness to camouflage itself, making it difficult to locate by conventional low-level means.]

With so much growth in just a few hours, Lohan was extremely satisfied, until suddenly a grotesque smell invaded his senses, putting him on alert instantly!

Chapter 69: 69 - Giant Snake

"Lisa, stay alert, I’m sensing a grotesque smell up ahead... much more intense than the previous snakes we encountered," he said immediately.

Lisa slowed down, her muscles tensed beneath her white fur as she crept through the shadows of the narrow crevice.

The world was bathed in cold blue tones, but just ahead, a colossal mass of pulsating heat filled the corridor.

Just the power it exuded as it breathed made Lohan’s core vibrate in constant alertness to danger.

The central part of its body had a grotesque, deformed bulge, stretching its scales to the limit. The serpent could barely coil itself, moving with a heavy, exhausting slowness.

"Maybe it ate a deer or even another elite monster. At this point, I believe its digestion is at its peak."

Lohan, however, focused on the opportunity.

"If we kill this snake, Lisa, we’ll get more acid than from ten ordinary snakes. And with its belly full, it won’t have the agility to escape my [Magic Weaving]." Lohan argued, feeling an internal euphoria at the fun it would be to fight that creature.

Ever since they started fighting together, Lohan had felt how much fun it was to kill monsters.

Without the disadvantage of being terribly slow, he was just taking full advantage of the advantages he had, and that was much cooler than spending all day digesting grass!

Lisa took a deep breath, analyzing Halon’s words and also feeling a little greedy for the amount of Digestive Acid inside that snake.

So little by little, the fun Halon felt in battle was also infecting her, who was loving the feeling of destroying these monsters.

Confirming that the Serpent, although strong, would probably be at a disadvantage because it was in the process of digestion, she accepted that the advantage was now theirs and decided to continue the battle with Halon.

"Lisa, let’s close off the exits. If she can’t move fast, let’s make sure she can’t move at all," Lohan suggested mentally, already mobilizing [Magic Weaving].

If they could fix that point of gravity, the creature would be at the mercy of their attacks, being kited to death.

However, the moment Lisa took her first step out of the shadows, the air in the cave seemed to freeze.

The Shadow Serpent, which until then had seemed focused solely on internal digestion, raised its triangular head with a speed that defied the laws of physics for a creature of that size.

Its eyes, vertical slits of toxic yellow, fixed on the fox and the slime.

Before any attack was launched, a wave of Murderous Intent flooded the crevice, so dense and heavy that Lohan felt his membrane vibrate violently and his core waver.

"Shit... I miscalculated," Lohan’s thought came like a snap of dread. ’It’s obvious that more powerful monsters would have ways to hide their scent, especially predators like this one!’

With [Chemosensory Aptitude Lv 7], he realized too late that the acid wasn’t just digesting the prey, but seemed to be metabolizing into raw mana, overwhelming the snake’s system.

The snake didn’t seem exhausted, but rather appeared to be in a state of chemical frenzy.

The snake hissed, letting out a much deeper sound than the snakes they had faced before, which reverberated off the polished walls of the crevice, and its tail, which looked like a massive obsidian whip, lashed out at them.

Lisa reacted instinctively, activating her Dash to the side, but the shockwave from the tail’s impact against the rock wall was so powerful that fist-sized shards of rock were thrown in all directions.

"Halon, use your webs! Now!" Lisa shouted mentally, her voice losing its usual coolness for the first time.

Lohan did just that, burning 40 units of biomass at once, casting the thickest strands of [Magic Weaving] he had made so far, imbued with blue mana.

The threads hit the creature’s back and attached themselves to the walls, but the snake’s strength was enormous. With a single twist of its muscular body, the mana fibers, which should have been unbreakable for low-level monsters, stretched to their limit, emitting a high-pitched sound of tension.

The creature ignored the threads and advanced, opening its jaws at an impossible angle. Instead of a bite, it expelled a jet of black, acidic vapor. 𝒻𝓇𝑒𝘦𝘸𝑒𝒷𝓃ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝒸ℴ𝘮

"Dodge!" Lohan shouted, taking advantage of his ability to see in the darkness, while desperately trying to shoot more threads to deflect the monster’s head.

Lisa trusted Halon’s shout and leaped, her paws sliding on the corrosive mud, but the space was too narrow.

The serpent’s tail came in a horizontal arc, anticipating the fox’s evasive movement.

With no angle to escape and Lohan’s web being torn like silk by the brute force of the beast, they found themselves trapped between the acid jet and the crushing blow.

Lohan saw the threads of his web breaking one by one, and for the first time since he was reincarnated, the feeling that death was inches away overwhelmed the euphoria of battle.

"Think, Lohan! If the web won’t hold... what will hold this thing?!"

Looking at it desperately, suddenly an idea came to his mind.

Chapter 70: 70 - Giant Snake 2

Panic was replaced by cold clarity the instant the sound of mana fibers snapping echoed through the air like low whips.

He didn’t shoot an [Ice Spike] outwards, but rather into the biomass clone he had just launched, using that magic as a rocket propellant to launch the clone even further, ignoring the damage he caused to himself and the biomass that was shattered on impact.

[Hemolymphatic Tissue Lv 7]

In the next second, two small, thin ice stakes grew from within that mass, piercing the stretched membrane between the monster’s scales as much as possible.

The effect was immediate and catastrophic for the snake... the pure digestive acid, under immense pressure due to the frantic digestion, began to gush out of it like a broken dam.

He began to drain.

Not just the snake’s Mana, he was using the threads to channel the wounded snake’s biomass directly into his own body.

"It’s weakening... I can see the heat from it dropping!" Lohan said, observing through [Thermographic Perception] that the hot white glow from the snake’s stomach was turning pale blue as he stole its life energy.

[Experience: +94]

[Experience: 411/400]

[Level Up?]

Chapter 71: 71 - Level 04!

[Name: Halon

Race: Slime (Mythical)

Class: Devourer (Mythical)

Level: 04

His digestion took a qualitative leap, to the point that at his current level, Lohan could easily consume several Mana Stones in a day, thus creating a potentially infinite farm of skills!

The snake’s organic matter, which had previously offered resistance, now seemed to disintegrate much faster at the touch of his jelly, converting into pure energy that filled his biomass reservoirs at a dizzying speed.

"At this rate, I need to evolve my biomass storage, both in density and size, so as not to overload myself with excess biomass."

Simultaneously, his control over his own form became slightly more fluid.

The feeling of being a heavy, gelatinous body grew weaker, as if his biomass had become lighter and more malleable again.

Extremely satisfied, he looked at Lisa and noticed a reddish-white glow running through her body. "Have you already reached Level 05?!" he asked in surprise.

"Hmm, it seems that your gains have also been very good." Lohan noted after analyzing her reaction, but he didn’t dwell on it too much.

Now that he could digest more than 1 Biomass per minute, Lohan only needed a few minutes to recover enough to keep [Selective Viscosity] active during the trip, and then he began to collect all the Digestive Acid he could from the snake before other monsters were attracted by the noise and smell of the place.

The first thing he did was stick to the holes in the snake’s belly and suck up as much Acid as he could, causing his body to swell slightly like a balloon.

[Mass Expansion Lv 8 → Lv 9] - 21.36 Biomass

[Conflict with: Reinforced Exoskeleton] 𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶

But this increase also made his body heavier and more uncoordinated, which worried Lisa, who watched in horror.

Before her, the Slime not only grew as it absorbed the Acid... it deformed grotesquely, swelling like a heavy, translucent balloon as it sucked it up nonstop.

’I’m going to have to carry him to Thalendor...’ She was frightened.

Chapter 72: 72 - Normal Girl

The distance between them and Thalendor was not short, and now without any Mana Stones to digest while being carried, Lohan felt the need to increase his speed again.

During battle, not having to focus on movement was great, but losing 40 minutes of digestion was the same as throwing 49 Biomass in the trash... considering how many evolutions he could buy with that amount, he wished he had eyes to shed a tear for it now.

He even thought about taking a piece of the giant snake to digest on the way, but when he noticed the cold look Lisa gave him, he quickly gave up on that.

"It’s okay, I’ll be able to play all day for the next few days, so I’ll be able to make up for it with more grinding... and with the speed of my passive digestion, even if I log off for 8 hours to sleep, I’ll get more than 50 Biomass from it, so it’s not all bad." Lisa rolled her eyes. "I’m going to log off, the night was very productive, but sleeping later than this will hinder my development."

Lohan agreed with her, but they were both so exhausted from the battle and ecstatic about leveling up that they had forgotten this detail. "Wait for me, I’ll disconnect and come back as soon as possible. If something goes wrong, try to save as much of the acid as you can."

Lisa looked at him blankly. She wanted to do what he said, but considering she had no hands or anything to store it in, she knew it would be useless.

Lisa opened her menu and also disconnected, feeling her own body transform into particles of light this time, while her consciousness flew back to the real world.

Opening her eyes, she pressed a button to drain the nutritional liquid from her capsule, then a pleasant breeze swept through the capsule, drying her clothes and hair slightly, but when the glass door opened, her body was still a little sticky and damp.

Putting that thought aside, Lisa, or rather Isabella, went to the bathroom and took a long, relaxing hot bath.

Lying completely naked in the bathtub, her long red hair spread across the crystal clear water, her smooth, white skin contrasted with the ceramic of the bathtub, displaying the impeccable symmetry of her natural curves.

With a slight twitch of her left eye, a golden screen floated in front of her as she opened an app.

[Syn]

’Do I add him to my corporate account or use my personal account for this?

If she used her corporate account, it was possible that political opponents would notice this new person and try to deal with him, even if they didn’t know how he was useful to her... Her personal account, on the other hand, would not cause this problem, as it was an account that only her closest friends had access to, and all her contacts there were private.

After considering it for a few seconds, she finally decided to use her private account.

When she entered his identification code, a profile appeared on her screen.

[Hayes]

"Hayes... is that his last name?" She wondered curiously, thinking again about what her partner was like.

Initially, she thought he might be a middle-aged man, especially after realizing he was from the Lower Zone, considering that this was perhaps the only way someone could afford to buy an Elysium helmet.

But after a few days of living together, she was sure he was young.

To Isabella, Halon was a complete mystery. 𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦

Nothing about him made sense... he was a young boy from the Lower Zone, who despite probably having a bad job, somehow bought an Elysium Helmet, was surprisingly intelligent, both for planning, analysis, or even combat...

When he spoke, he exuded much more confidence and serenity than most of the people from the Upper Zone she had met in her life, and despite acting this way, deducing that she was someone from the Upper Zone (which wasn’t very difficult), he didn’t start acting submissive or subservient, treating her just like a normal girl!

"A normal girl..." She thought dreamily, lowering her head slightly into the warm water and wondering what that would be like, without noticing a pretty small smile appearing at the corner of her mouth. ’At least, there I can be a normal girl..."

Chapter 73: 73 - Company?

NunuNote: Enjoy this Bonus Chapter, you deserve it from your PS and GT goals!

After yesterday’s exhausting battle, Lohan had a pleasant night’s sleep.

He would normally sleep for at least 12 hours, but with his current body, it took less than 8 hours to fully replenish his energy.

Upon waking up, Lohan walked to the refrigerator in his small rented apartment and, upon opening it, found the light inside flashing nonstop until, after a few seconds, it went out completely.

He tried closing and opening the refrigerator door a few times to see if that would fix it, but it didn’t work; the light had probably burned out.

Sighing, he didn’t care and took the last bag of nutrient solution, poured the dirty, smelly water from the sink, and finally poured the contents of the bag into the glass, making the smell disappear, despite its ghastly appearance.

"I think I’ll need to go shopping... I hope the money from selling the Acid is enough."

Looking at it more closely, Lohan was surprised by something.

’Compared to digesting the brains of goblins, kobolds, or giant snakes, the contents of this cup don’t seem so unpleasant.’ He laughed when he realized this fact.

In his human body, he could still taste things, unlike Halon’s body, so he wouldn’t become a brain eater, but still, at least eating this now didn’t disgust him anymore.

After drinking this nutrient solution, in a few seconds all the nutrition from it was absorbed and distributed throughout his body, causing the feeling of infinite energy to return.

Without wasting a second, Lohan bent down and started doing his exercises, until in the middle of a push-up, he remembered something.

"Wait, I still haven’t sent the doctor’s note Lisa prepared for me... or rather, did she really prepare one?"

Although he had decided that he would skip class today anyway, it would still be better to go through with it with the free pass that a doctor’s note would bring.

So he ran back to his room and grabbed his phone, finally seeing a new notification.

[Syn: New friend request from Lisa.]

Lohan didn’t think twice and accepted the friend request.

When the friendship was formed, her profile picture finally appeared.

Unfortunately, instead of a photo of the girl who controlled the character Lisa, the only photo available was a picture of a forest with trees filled with bright red leaves.

Lohan was amazed by that view, totally different from anything he had ever seen in the three worlds he had lived in. ’I don’t even know what planet something like this is from...’

Out of curiosity, he opened his own profile and realized that he didn’t even use a photo, using only the default icon of a blank avatar.

Looking around and seeing that there was nothing worth photographing, and considering that the quality of his old cell phone camera would only embarrass him in front of those who could take realistic photos with their eye holograms, he simply gave up.

[Hayes: Good morning Lisa, I just woke up, how are you?]

The response took less than thirty seconds.

The Syn app glowed in an elegant white tone on his cracked cell phone screen.

[Lisa: I just woke up... I took care of your certificate, check your inbox.]

Lohan opened the file.

It was an official document from the Elite Central Hospital, with government seals that he could never forge. His "friend" really did have scary connections.

[Lisa: Three days of complete rest for ’acute respiratory failure due to exposure to heavy metals’ should be enough for your boss not to question it, you just need to fill in your name.]

’Respiratory failure... little do they know at the college that my Digestive Filter is doing a much better job than the college’s purifiers haha.’ Lohan thought contentedly, feeling the Mana circulating warmly through his chest.

[Hayes: Thank you, Lisa. That saves my life. See you in Thalendor?]

[Lisa: Yes. I’ll log in in ten minutes. Don’t be late... Aeliana is too valuable a contact to keep waiting.]

With her confirmation, Lohan forwarded this certificate to the college contact, finished his exercises, and logged into Elysium again. 𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝚠𝚎𝚋𝗻𝗼𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝚘𝐦

After verifying the authenticity of this certificate, the college staff asked no further questions.

Two students were absent from today’s class, Isabella Vance and a nobody from the Lower Zone. Due to the huge difference in status between them, no one connected that they might be skipping class together, and if the two knew about each other’s absence, they also wouldn’t connect that the coincidence actually had anything to do with each other.

Unlike Isabella’s absence, which was noticed by everyone, Lohan’s absence was noticed by only one person.

-xXx-

In Elysium, the sun was shining brightly in the sky.

"How I missed a beautiful sun like this..." He thought excitedly, feeling the comfortable warmth touch his membrane, causing crackles of satisfaction. "No matter how many times I see it, this sky always makes the Lower Zone seem like a distant nightmare," he continued to think, as he felt the weight of the Shadow Serpent Acid swaying inside his membrane, which had been expanded by the recent mass upgrade.

Next to him was a small, delicate white fox, whose fur looked like strands of white silk in the sunlight, shining with what appeared to be the manifestation of her Mana.

Lisa turned her head, her eyes half-closed in an expression that mixed her usual coldness with a surprising subtle trace of camaraderie after the victory against the giant snake.

"Still admiring the clouds, Halon?" Her telepathic voice resonated in his mind, and although cold, it was sweet and pleasant to hear.

Lohan vibrated the gelatin, forming a small blue hand that made a thumbs-up sign in the air. "Yeah, no matter how much I look, everything I see here is very beautiful."

Since Lohan had no eyes, Lisa didn’t know where he was looking, only able to guess from the hand next to his body, with the thumbs-up sign pointing slightly towards her.

But she had to agree, of the many planets she had traveled to, this world was the most beautiful she had ever seen.

Although his digestion speed had increased so much, he was still not at the point of digesting the entire grass in a second, but to compensate for moments when he would not have enough biomass available, Lohan focused his immediate digestion on the roots of plants to absorb the grass, tree trunks, flowers, small insects, and everything that appeared in his path so that he could digest it later.

Soon they spotted the young elf, looking around excitedly, but there was someone else beside her!

"Hello, Aeliana, I’m sorry we kept you waiting." A clearly young, but calm and surprisingly pleasant male voice appeared in her mind.

Despite hearing that, he froze for a split second again, before acting naturally and saying in a respectful voice. "I am finally able to meet you, Lady Ylasys, this humble Slime is called Halon. I apologize if I caused you trouble, and I hope that when I get money, I can pay you for the damage caused."

Upon hearing that, Yrneha felt that the little creature seemed even more pleasing to the eye.

Having the humility to admit mistakes and offer a proactive form of compensation was a great way to repair the damage caused, even if he was not the cause of that damage. As the biggest beneficiary, admitting guilt and offering compensation was a great move.

’How did a creature as clueless as a Slime manage to develop like this?’ Her eyes sparkled, feeling increasingly tempted to take this blue jelly to her laboratory and study the core that controlled it all.

Chapter 75: 75 - The Splendor of Thalendor!

Lohan was surprised for a moment, but remembering hearing Aeliana comment that her teacher was one of the most renowned magicians in Thalendor, he understood where this interest came from.

Aeliana walked slightly ahead, jumping between giant roots with an agility that Lohan still envied, while he concentrated on rolling without letting the digestive acid sway too much inside him.

’If I stumble and explode now, Thalendor will get a new acid pool before I even pass through the gate... he thought, controlling the inner membrane at just the right point and using [Selective Viscosity] to ensure he wouldn’t slip on the vines that were beginning to appear on the path.

If they were on the main road, this wouldn’t be a problem, but now they were coming out of the forest surrounding the city, so there wasn’t a perfect, flat path for them to follow.
