As they approached, the air seemed to change its "flavor."

Suddenly, a dangerous thought crossed his mind. ’If I activate my [Chemosensory Aptitude] here, will I overdose?!’

"There it is, Thalendor!" Aeliana shouted excitedly, pointing to the main arch where cascades of crystal clear water fell from hanging gardens, creating rainbow mists under the sun.

She had traveled to hundreds, if not thousands, of planets in her lifetime, but no city she had visited in the past could compare to the splendor she saw in Thalendor.

Lohan felt the wooden card vibrate in the space pocket where it was stored and sped up her rolling.

The two girls also sped up, with Lisa excited to see more, and Aeliana excited to show her everything.

Before they arrived, Aeliana made a request.

Lohan looked back and, seeing the trail of destruction he had left behind, felt a little embarrassed, so he suddenly stopped digesting, just rolling around normally while giving Aeliana a thumbs up.

"Actually, I do it more out of instinct, I’m sorry if I damaged something I shouldn’t have," he explained, to Aeliana’s amazement.

"Wait, you can stop digesting things?!" she asked in surprise.

"Of course, after all, I never digested anything on you when you carried me in your arms," he explained.

Upon hearing this, a realization dawned on the elf’s face, which soon gave way to a happy smile, and she walked even more cheerfully toward the city.

When they arrived at the city gate, a line of several dozen people had formed.

In this line were both elves and creatures of other species.

When their group approached, the people looked at them curiously, but seeing Aeliana’s staff, they seemed to understand something and didn’t mind it.

"Maybe they think we’re Aeliana’s hired monsters?" Lohan asked curiously through their mental link.

Lisa also thought the same thing, nodding her head without caring much.

It was very interesting to see such a variety of species.

At least half of the beings they saw were elves, while the other half was quite varied, with humanoids with animal and monster characteristics representing the majority. There were also beings closer to animals and monsters than to humanoids, such as centaurs and other creatures like them.

Each species seemed to have a unique way of acting, some being more taciturn, speaking softly and constantly keeping an eye on their surroundings, others being more relaxed, laughing and talking loudly without worrying too much about the people around them.

Even with such different ways of acting, with some bothering others, no one dared to cause trouble under the eyes of archers, warriors, and elf mages who guarded the gate and city walls.

Finally, it was their turn.

Unlike the people in line who ignored the Slime and the Fox, the guards examined them closely.

Making a polite hand gesture in front of his chest to Aeliana, which she soon returned with an equal gesture, as a greeting, he asked the elf, ignoring the two small monsters. "Excuse me, are these two creatures hired monsters?"

Aeliana then explained. "No, these two are Friends of Thalendor!"

As she said this, she pointed to them, and when the guard looked, the Slime had created arms and was holding two Thalendor ID Cards.

Seeing those cards, and sensing the elven magic within them that could not be faked, coupled with the presence of an elf like Aeliana beside them to attest to their veracity, the guard’s attitude quickly changed.

"I apologize for my previous rudeness, dear guests, I just need you to tell me your identity and your entry will be approved." The guard said respectfully.

He knew that to receive cards like those, one would need to make significant contributions to Thalendor, and not being elves, the level of contribution required to earn something like that was even greater.

Even if it was only a Level 03 Card, it was still a reason for respect. Theodas was a 400-year-old elf, working and contributing to Thalendor by performing his duties vigorously, and he did not have a card like that.

With his attitude, Lohan felt a little disappointed, thinking that he had missed the opportunity to watch an entertaining show, where the guard would humiliate them for being monsters, and then they would show the Thalendor ID Cards to the guard, slapping him in the face and leaving victorious, but it seems that not everyone was as foolish as that stupid kid from college.

Indeed, as Aeliana said, this card made their life in the city much easier.

Seeing that magnificent city up close was incredible, but Lohan was already feeling uncomfortable carrying so much Digestive Acid under the hot sun and asked them to hurry to the Alchemy lodge.

The two girls agreed with him and in a few minutes they arrived at the store.

The place was called "The Silver Crucible," a shop built inside a tree, but strangely, it didn’t seem to have been made artificially, but rather took advantage of an existing opening in the place.

The interior was luxuriously decorated with various silver pieces, with displays showing things like exotic flowers, shiny liquids of different colors, Mana Stones of various sizes, among many other unique items.

Lohan imagined he would see things like animal or monster skulls, but it seemed that those weren’t really related to alchemy.

Suddenly, a polite male voice interrupted their observation. "Lia? Didn’t your weekly visit happen two days ago?"

Moving to get a better look in that direction, Lohan saw a male elf who, by human standards, appeared to be in his 30s, with long blond hair, dressed in an elegant suit mixing white and green, with a polite smile on his face that soon changed to curiosity as he looked at the blue Slime carrying a strange greenish liquid inside itself as it rolled awkwardly.

Looking closely, the elf seemed to recognize the liquid inside the Slime and was even more surprised. "Hoho, was this creative way of carrying Digestive Acid Lady Yrneha’s idea? I must say that perhaps in all of Thalendor, only she would think of using a Slime for this."

"No, no, no, Intervar!

This Slime isn’t being used to carry the Acid, it’s actually my friend who brought this Digestive Acid to sell to you." Aeliana quickly explained.

Hearing this made the elf even more curious.

To make his point, Lohan formed a hand next to his body, using it to make the common elven greeting he saw Aeliana and the guard make, and spoke through the mental link Lisa formed.

"Hello, friend, I am Halon the Slime. It is a pleasure to meet you." Lohan introduced himself politely.

"My friend Lisa and I brought this Digestive Acid to sell at the suggestion of my friend Aeliana. Are you interested in our merchandise?"

As Lohan spoke, the little white fox also approached, looking at the elf refinedly, like a little noblewoman.

Seeing the greeting the slime made, even though it still seemed a little clumsy and could be improved in some ways, Intervar was completely shocked by it. Not only by the fact that the Slime knew how to do the elven greeting, but by the fact that the Slime was intelligent enough to communicate like a normal person!

But maintaining his etiquette, he responded with the same greeting, in a way that was obviously more refined than how the slime did it, and replied. "Would that be Shadow Serpent Digestive Acid? In fact, our stock of it is zero, so if you are willing to sell, and the quality meets our standards, I will be happy to buy it. How much did you bring?"

Although Lohan’s membrane was slightly transparent, because it was carrying the liquid inside, its color was a little opaque, so even though it was possible to deduce what was inside, it was not possible to deduce the quantity well.

Intervar imagined that they had brought 1 or 2 liters of the acid, since it was extremely difficult to extract without injuring oneself or losing quality, so when he saw the Slime extend a finger forward, he imagined that there was 1 liter of acid inside it and nodded with a happy smile, satisfied that he could replenish his stock of this product.

What he didn’t realize was that there was only one zero missing behind the number one that the Slime showed him!

Chapter 77: 77 - Fierce Negotiation

Looking at the basin filled with Shadow Serpent Digestive Acid, Intervar was horrified.

Despite being a magical world, with magic facilitating most of the day-to-day processes, extracting this acid from inside the snakes’ intestines was a very delicate task that magic could not help with.

If a mistake were made, the acid would leak into the snakes’ bodies, corroding their internal organs and mixing with their blood, rendering the acid useless.

But this difficulty did not apply to Lohan.

With [Digestive Filter], he chose exactly what he wanted to digest and left only the purest acid stored inside himself.

And since his body was gelatinous, he could penetrate the dead snake’s body and suck all the acid out from inside, and if any impurities came along, he would just digest them and keep the valuable part.

Because of this, a snake that should yield a maximum of 100 ml of usable acid yielded an average of 500 ml per snake for Lohan!

He had killed almost 20 normal snakes, in addition to the giant snake he fought at the end, which brought the total amount of acid inside him to about 10 liters.

While Intervar was horrified by this amount of acid, he was also very excited about the profit it would bring him when sold.

Making mental calculations, he quickly spoke to the slime.

"Normally we buy a maximum of 1 liter of acid, but since you brought 10 liters, the total price will have to be reduced a little, because we probably won’t have enough demand to sell it all for a long time... is that a problem for you?" he asked.

Before Lohan could answer, Lisa spoke up. "Oh, then there’s no problem, we can sell you just 1 liter and sell the rest to your competitors, how about that?"

Hearing the female voice, Intervar looked at the fox in surprise. "No, no, how could I? As friends of Lia’s, I think I can raise the price and pay the standard price for your entire stock."

He replied, trying to remain calm.

Intervar realized he had found a formidable opponent. "No problem, the standard price we buy Acid at is 50 copper coins per liter. Keep in mind that this is not yet a finished product, so we must filter out all impurities before selling it to the end consumer."

Lohan vibrated his gelatin, interrupting Intervar’s technical speech with a small blue hand forming at the top of his body, and pointed directly at the dark, viscous glow of the liquid in the basin.

"You won’t have to filter anything, Intervar." Lohan’s voice resonated in the mental link, laden with calm. "I guarantee the absolute purity of this acid. "Kid, understand... even if the quality is impeccable, 50 coppers is the standard that the market pays for raw materials..."

Lisa tilted her fox head, her eyes shining with a coldness she had been trained to use in Vance Group meetings in the real world. "Then it seems we’re wasting our time here. Halon, put the acid back. Yrneha mentioned that there are several other alchemy shops in Thalendor desperate to restock."

The distance closed in seconds.

Before the thief could turn the next corner, Lohan was already on top of him, holding him with a force that made him drop the bag immediately.

The little thief trembled, not understanding the reference, but terrified by the aura of power that Lohan now naturally exuded.

In the eyes of this little thief, this man in a black hoodie with a mask covering his face looked like one of those super soldiers from the High Zone army!

’Damn, why did I have to choose this target?!’ He asked himself in frustration.

Honestly, Lohan wasn’t even that angry with this little thief.

Especially when he felt how thin and fragile his arms were, it became clear that this theft was out of necessity, not because he wanted it.

"Sigh... you’re lucky I have a good heart," Lohan said, letting go of the boy’s arm, who cautiously moved away from him like a skittish kitten and bent down to pick up the bag the boy had stolen.

From inside, he took out a bottle of clean, clear water, totally different from the stinky water he had been drinking from the tap for the past few days, and also took two packets of high-quality nutritional supplements.

This was still food for the poor in the Lower Zone, but for them, it was already a luxury that few had the right to enjoy.

Even through his mask, Lohan could see the boy almost drooling, looking at it with desire.

Without saying a word, he threw the bottle and the packets to the boy.

The one who would not like this new news would be Lisa, who would have to carry him, who now weighed a little more than before.

With that in mind, Lohan decided to spend some Biomass to gradually improve his speed, so that in the near future he could be more independent.

[Viscous Flow Lv 16 → Lv 18] - 40.39 Biomass - 0.98 m/s → 1.18 m/s

Lohan spent a total of 61.71 Biomass to purchase these two evolutions, which might seem like a large investment, but it still didn’t represent even what he earned in an hour of uninterrupted digestion.

Feeling the new flexibility of his body, he was excited.

’Finally, my speed will increase by more than 0.1 per level!

Much better than the fraction of that this evolution increased per level in the early stages, hehe.’ He thought excitedly.

Meanwhile, Lisa carefully observed the environment and the village, trying to understand the structure of these little frogs to see if they would be suitable for joining their guild.

They seemed like very close-knit and helpful creatures, quickly gathering to help the wounded while another group met with Elder Gribbit to prepare supplies for their search.

Chapter 84: 84 - Invitation

"Are you sure you don’t need more time to help the wounded?" Lisa asked.

At this point, it was more important for them to secure the goodwill and cooperation of the frogs in this village to try to find someone willing to join the guild than to just find the Swamp Slugs as was the original plan.

They had already noticed the magical insight that the old frog Gribbit had shown when breaking Lisa’s mental link, so if there were more people with such potential, even if it wasn’t anything too great, it could still be useful for future guild groups.

Although they were small and physically fragile, that was what guild groups were for, so that someone else or a creature with advantages in that area could cover their disadvantage, and together they could show a strength greater than 1+1=2, just like Lohan and Lisa.

"Don’t worry about them, this is just the natural cycle of life. The survivors will find an ideal place to bury the deceased, and the younger ones will take care of generating new tadpoles in the coming days. Given our fertility, this will not be a problem haha." Old Gribbit laughed as he held his belly with one hand, proud.

Lohan used his 360-degree vision to analyze the other frogs and realized that they didn’t really seem so sad about the death of other frogs, perhaps even a little indifferent to it?

Looking at Lisa, he noticed the confusion on her face as well and sent a telepathic message just to her. "Is this normal in different species around the world?"

Considering that she was someone from the Upper Zone with great influence, it was very likely that she had traveled to several planets and encountered various civilizations, so Lohan asked.

Lisa looked at Slime and took a moment to respond. "It’s not normal, but it’s also not unique... for some civilizations, especially the more primitive ones, death is often more comforting than life." 𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞

Lohan heard that and thought it made sense.

Although it was a strange situation, considering how dangerous this world was, it made sense not to be so afraid of death, especially for frogs that could spawn hundreds of tadpoles at a time.

"Okay, so let’s go find the slugs?" Old Gribbit asked excitedly.

"Please guide us," Lisa said respectfully, and Lohan followed suit.

As they left the confines of Kroak Village, the environment became noticeably more oppressive. The black, slimy mud bubbled under Lisa’s paws, and the air carried a constant smell of iron and decay.

Gribbit walked ahead, using his twisted wooden staff to test the depth of the swamp with each step, looking like a fragile yet persistent figure against the adversity that this environment brought.

"Gribbit." Lisa began, sending her telepathic voice so that both the toad and Lohan could hear. "How has your village managed to survive here for so long? This swamp doesn’t seem like a place for the weak, and the Kobolds don’t seem to be the only danger."

The old toad paused for a second, wiping a drop of mud from his faded moss-green skin. "Ah, Noble White Lady, the swamp is cruel, but it is also a master. Our village has been here for generations... we move whenever the mud gets too ’hungry’ or the predators get too greedy." He gave a smile that seemed genuinely weary. "We are small, but we are many. That is how nature balances us."

Lohan, who rolled alongside Lisa using [Selective Viscosity] to keep from sinking into the sludge and took the time to digest as much biomass as possible, decided to test the waters for the future of the guild. "Have you ever thought about moving to a safer place? A community with magical talent like yours would be welcome in many less... oppressive places."

Gribbit let out a hoarse, wet laugh, gesturing with his webbed hand toward the dense vegetation. "Who would accept swamp toads like us in other tribes? We belong to the mud, Little Blue Lord. However..." He looked at Halon with yellow eyes that shone with seemingly humble hope. "To hear that powerful beings like you care about our fate... it warms an old man’s heart. Perhaps, if there were a place where we weren’t just ’pests’ or ’snacks,’ my people would be willing to follow."

Lisa looked at Lohan a little surprised, feeling that the seed of the guild was being successfully planted, not only in the old toad but also in her guild’s Vice Leader.

In the toad, she did not see a warrior leader, but perhaps a perfect pillar of support for the guild’s future infrastructure.

"That’s good to hear, Gribbit. I hope that if there is an opportunity for a new monster settlement to arise, you will accept the invitation to join your village," she said politely.

"I’m glad to hear that," Gribbit replied, walking again with renewed vigor. "But now, silence. We are entering the territory of the Swamp Slugs.

They don’t hear like we do, but they sense the vibrations of every agitated touch in the water."

Lohan activated [Spatial Echo Location], sensing the vibrations of the ground and mapping the environment in 360 degrees.

He realized that Gribbit was guiding them as if he had tracking and spatial location skills like his own, avoiding pockets of methane gas and areas where the sludge was excessively deep.

The old toad seemed like an impeccable guide, causing Lohan and Lisa to gradually relax their guard as they delved deeper into the most dangerous part of the slugs’ domain.

In a few minutes, they finally reached the first Slug.

The creature was ’lying’ underwater while constantly excreting poison into that area, making that water highly toxic!

"Pay attention!" Old Gribbit said in a low voice. "Do you notice that this water is slightly yellowish, unlike the normal water around it?

That’s because this water is already saturated with poison. Stepping in a puddle saturated with poison like this would be enough to greatly weaken even a Level 7 Bear."

Hearing the warning, Lohan and Lisa looked at the puddle worriedly, thinking about how to remove this slug and its poison without hurting themselves.

Chapter 85: 85 - Have They Forgotten?

Lohan could digest or isolate poisons within himself very easily, but according to old Gribbit’s description, this Slug’s poison seemed very powerful, perhaps even a few levels more powerful than the Digestive Acid of the Shadow Serpents.

And that raised a question.

"Should I try to digest this? If something goes wrong, I’ll be very vulnerable here and will only become a burden if an enemy appears... but if I can’t digest this, how are we supposed to get it back to Thalendor?" He wondered, a little confused.

"Do you know of any safe way to remove the slug, or the poison from this puddle, Gribbit?" Lohan asked.

Gribbit looked at the puddle with them, and brought a wrinkled hand to his chin, also pondering what to do. "Normally we drain the water from this puddle using branches, causing the poison to dilute with the nearby water, and without the water, the slug is exposed, making it easier to collect, but even without the water, the slug can still expel liquid poison, making the capture process very difficult."

Lohan processed Gribbit’s words carefully.

Although the [Digestive Filter] was powerful, he couldn’t afford to make a miscalculation now. If that poison could really weaken a Level 7 Bear, a Level 4 Slime like him could have his [Magic Core]compromised before he even finished absorbing it.

He needed to conduct tests first.

"Lisa, let’s not risk direct contact yet." Lohan spoke through the mental link. "Let’s follow his method. If I force the digestion of something so saturated, I may be too slow to react to any unforeseen circumstances..."

Lisa nodded, keeping a safe distance from the yellowish edge. "Gribbit, show us how you do it. Let’s use the branches." She said telepathically.

The old toad acted promptly, using his staff to drag thick branches and fallen logs to the edge of the pool. Lohan helped, but even more cautiously.

He didn’t use his main body.

Activating [Partial Division], he created a small 10-centimeter clone to manipulate the plant debris, keeping the main mass safely out of contact with the poison.

As the branches were pushed in, the toxic water began to drain into a nearby depression, diluting into the common mud of the swamp.

After a few minutes of work, the Swamp Slug was exposed at the muddy bottom, writhing and expelling short jets of a viscous, neon-colored liquid.

"Now, Great Blue Lord! She’s vulnerable!" Gribbit shouted, pointing with his trembling staff.

But Lohan did not approach.

Still controlling the Clone, and only after ensuring that the creature was isolated from the saturated pool did he act.

He activated [Non-Newtonian Resilience] to ensure that any sudden jets would hit a rigid membrane and not penetrate his body. With a quick movement, he enveloped the slug with the clone.

Internally, he sealed the creature in an isolated biomass "pouch," allowing the [Digestive Filter] to identify and neutralize the toxin without it touching his core.

"I think it worked..." Lohan transmitted, feeling the weight of the creature inside the clone, but without the burning of the toxin.

"Excellent! Simply magnificent!" Gribbit exclaimed, banging his staff on the ground. "Follow me, there are more slugs waiting for us just ahead! This one is even bigger, and its venom is a gem for alchemists!"

Confirming that the slug’s venom had no effect on him, Lohan absorbed the slug into himself and used the clone to continue digesting the surrounding biomass.

They walked for another ten minutes until they reached a clearing where the air seemed to vibrate with toxicity.

The puddle ahead was not just yellowish... it was a phosphorescent orange.

Lohan used [Spatial Echo Location] and realized that this Slug under the water was massive, but he noticed something else: dozens of small rhythmic vibrations hidden in the slime around them.

Before Lohan could warn Lisa, the sound of a sharp crack echoed.

Gribbit, who was crouching on the edge, leaped backward with agility impossible for an elder. He began to laugh... a sharp, dissonant laugh that was anything but fragile. "You stupid monsters are so easy to lead!" Gribbit hissed, his aura suddenly turning dark.

"Thank you for saving our village from the Kobolds, now we can deliver something even better to the true master!"

With a violent swing of his mana-imbued staff, he leveraged the Giant Slug out of the water.

The colossal creature flew like a toxic projectile straight at Lisa while spewing poison in all directions!

"Receive a gift from Kroak Village!" he yelled. "Digesting such a unique Slime will ensure that my tadpoles will never go hungry again!"

Lohan saw the orange mass cover Lisa’s field of vision as the village’s "helpless" frogs began to emerge from the mud with bone spears in hand.

-xXx-

But Lisa was no ordinary fox... Before the colossal slug could hit her, she activated [Spectral Step], turning into a white blur that moved sideways, letting the toxic projectile crash uselessly into a willow root.

Lohan, for his part, was not paralyzed by shock. His [Spatial Echo-Location] had already mapped the rhythmic vibrations of dozens of toads emerging from the mud around them.

"Lisa, we’re surrounded! They were hiding their Mana under the mud!" Lohan warned through the mental link, feeling a cold rage rise within him.

He realized that Gribbit’s supposed gratitude was just a facade to lure them both in and convert them into food for their tadpoles.

Lohan immediately activated the [Obsidian Exoskeleton Lv 1], coating his membrane with black, rigid hexagonal scales that glistened in the dim light of the swamp.

The biomass cost was high, quickly draining his reservoir, but the superior resistance was necessary against the poison-coated bone spears wielded by the toads.

Lisa growled, her tails swaying in rage as white flames began to lick her paws, preparing the [Spirit Fire] to incinerate the attackers.

Although she felt that something was wrong with the situation so far, she did not imagine that she was falling into such a trap.

Even with years of training in the family, she still let herself be carried away by a situation like this, being deceived in such a foolish manner.

At this point, Lisa’s fury caused her body to glow even brighter in a white light, with faint red flashes appearing through her fur.

"I think they’ve forgotten who saved their village from annihilation..." Lohan spoke in a cold voice, also enraged by the audacity and ingratitude of these toads. "Well... it seems we must remind them."

Chapter 86: 86 - The Difference Between Common and Mythical

Gribbit, who still held his staff aloft, stopped laughing for a brief second when he saw the white trail left by Lisa’s [Spectral Step], his yellow eyes widening at the speed of this fox.

However, he quickly regained his composure, letting out a dry, confident croak as he watched the colossal slug throb against the tree root where it had collided.

"Impressive, Noble White Lady... your agility matches your power." Gribbit hissed, his voice now laden with a dark authority that he had previously hidden beneath the mask of a frail old man. "But you will have to deal with my scouts alone. Your little blue friend may have isolated the first slug, but their venom isn’t instant... it acts like a slow tide that corrodes the core from the inside out in ten or fifteen minutes, mwahahaha!"

He twirled his staff, pointing it at Lohan with scorn: "By now, the paralysis must be rising through his gelatin, turning him into nothing more than a static mana battery for my children."

What the old toad didn’t know was that Lohan’s [Mythic Devourer] class didn’t follow the common biological rules of Elysium.

Internally, the [Digestive Filter Lv 16] had already identified and isolated each molecular toxin the instant the membrane came into contact with the first slug, turning what should have been deadly poison into pure biomass to sustain his defenses.

Lohan felt the [Magic Core Lv 7] vibrate with renewed vigor, not with the weakness Gribbit had expected.

If he didn’t want to store as much of this poison as possible to sell in Thalendor, he could use it directly as fuel for battle!

Lisa, feeling the fury within her, let the [Spirit Fire] envelop not only her paws, but her entire silhouette, causing the red flashes in her fur to glow with destructive intensity.

Then she shot like a reddish-white blur toward the scouts closing in.

Lohan was not far behind.

Covering his 37 cm diameter mass with black hexagonal plates that reflected the light from Lisa’s flames, using the [Artificial Magic Core Harmonizer Lv 2] to synchronize his Mana, he simultaneously fired three strands of [Magic Weaving] toward the branches above Gribbit, preparing to digest this traitor completely while releasing two small clones to help Lisa deal with the other toads.

Upon feeling the first blow of the bone spears against his armor, the [Hemolymphatic Tissue Lv 7] boosted his digestion rate to 151 Bio/h, making this little Blue Slime even more lethal!

"What?! How can you still move like that?!" Gribbit asked in shock, unable to believe the agility the Slime showed as it rolled and flew towards him.

Seeing the large blue-black mass flying towards him, Gribbit swung his staff and a burst of bright poisonous water flew from the puddle below him towards the Slime, slightly changing its flight path.

The burst of poisoned water hit Lohan’s body with force, but the resulting sound was not that of an impact on soft flesh, but rather that of metal colliding with solid rock.

Thanks to [Non-Newtonian Resilience], Lohan’s membrane instantly hardened at the point of contact, dispersing the kinetic pressure without suffering a single scratch as the [Obsidian Exoskeleton] glowed in an absolute black tone under the light of the swamp.

"Who are you going to call for help now, Gribbit?" Lohan transmitted his mental voice through Lisa’s link, which was still active.

Ignoring the recoil, Lohan used [Selective Viscosity] to anchor himself in the air through the threads of [Magic Weaving] he had fired earlier.

With a violent tug, he propelled himself downward, falling on Gribbit like a black jelly meteor. Before the frog could jump, Lohan fired five Mana-fused biological filaments that dug into the elder’s limbs, initiating the energy drain.

Meanwhile, Lisa turned the scouts’ encirclement into an open-air morgue.

She was a reddish-white blur moving with [Spectral Step], rendering the frogs’ bone spears mere useless obstacles in the air.

Her [Spirit Fire] not only burned flesh, Lohan saw, through his [Thermographic Perception], the heat signatures of the frogs collapse instantly as their souls were incinerated by the legendary flame.

The difference in scale was overwhelming.

The scouts, who were just common low-level monsters, could barely process the fox’s speed before being torn in half or reduced to ashes.

Beside her, Lohan’s two clones acted as mobile anchors.

Using [Selective Viscosity] at maximum adhesion, the clones stuck to the feet of the surviving frogs, immobilizing them so that Lisa could finish them off or dissolve them right there.

Gribbit screamed in pain, but the sound was muffled by the mass of Lohan that now enveloped his right arm.

The elder felt his Mana being sucked away by the blue threads as his green skin was corroded at an alarming rate of 151 Bio/h.

"P-please! Have mercy!" Gribbit begged, watching his scouts being slaughtered like insignificant insects.

"You have already received our mercy, and you refused it," Lohan replied mentally.

Lohan didn’t stop.

He condensed icy Mana and fired an [Ice Spike] point-blank at Gribbit’s knee, just to make sure he wouldn’t escape digestion.

At this point, the battle was not a contest between equals... it was a demonstration of why beings of Mythical and Legendary races had such advantages over races of lower rarities, treating the local "predators" as nothing more than raw biomass waiting to be processed.

If these frogs were at least level 10, or even level 11, they might have had a chance, but being roughly the same level, or even lower as a Common Race against Races at the top of the pyramid, it was an impossible battle from the start.

Honestly, it was a little disappointing to see this small warrior race wiped out by them instead of joining the ranks of the guild they were forming, but at that point, they wouldn’t be stupid enough to trust a group that had already betrayed them to participate in something that depended completely on trust like a guild.

Chapter 87: 87 - Disappointment

"Then we’ll have to look for other members for our guild," Lohan commented as he digested the body of old Gribbit.

Lisa was a little out of breath, having expended a lot of Spiritual Energy to kill those dozens of frogs that ambushed them, responding in a still cold voice. "Yes, we’ll have to raise our selection criteria..."

Lisa, or rather Isabella behind Lisa, was very disappointed in herself.

This was the biggest mistake she had made in judging people in recent years.

Perhaps because she had entered a much lighter and more pleasant environment when she met Halon, with him showing that he didn’t care so much about her identity, nor that she was just an aggregate of benefits that the Vance surname would bring along, her guard was down a little.

Even more so after meeting Aeliana and the other elves in Thalendor, who treated her as a slightly unusual monster, obviously with some value for what she had already shown, but still far from the value that everyone tried to extract from the Vances.

Looking at the Slime, who was also a little out of breath as he digested the disgusting body of that filthy toad, Lisa couldn’t help but compare.

Halon would obviously have many more reasons to try to deceive, or even use the advantages she had at her disposal. And for the potential he had shown so far, she would admit that he deserved those advantages she had to offer, but at no point did he ask for anything or even hint that he wanted anything from her.

All the while, Halon had only treated Lisa as a partner in the game, acting as he saw fit, not actively trying to flatter her, but still listening to her opinions, following instructions he considered correct, and also giving instructions he thought he had thought through better than she had.

The balanced relationship the two were developing was something she never imagined she could receive.

And compared to those frogs who tried to stab her in the back at the first opportunity, the discrepancy between the two became even greater!

"Yes, haha, we’ll definitely have to raise our selection criteria." Halon replied with a laugh, totally unconcerned about it.

Even though he had been betrayed, he didn’t seem to care that he had almost invited snakes into the nest they were developing.

’But come to think of it... it makes sense. He has seen that guilds are valued and that large corporations are doing their utmost to produce successful guilds, but he doesn’t know why, nor how these guilds would demonstrate value corresponding to the investment they are making... much less how important the guild we are setting up will be for me and my future in the Vance Group. She thought worriedly. 𝐟𝗿𝐞𝚎𝚠𝐞𝚋𝕟𝐨𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝕔𝕠𝚖

Even though they hadn’t talked much in the last few days, or deepened their relationship by talking about life in the real world, every day Isabella felt that this strange Slime from the Lower Zone was someone who was proving to be more and more trustworthy.

But then her thoughts cooled again. With a warning like those damn frogs, she forced herself to return to rationality and see things clearly.

Although Halon was very important, and every day proved to be more essential to the success of her plan, they had only known each other for a short time, and even though everything seemed to be going well, she had to focus on the present and leave those daydreams for later.

Meanwhile, Lohan was exactly as Isabella had imagined.

He was thoroughly enjoying this frog feast.

Sure, it was a good thing he couldn’t taste anything, because just the appearance of these creatures’ rotten flesh looked terrible.

But on the other hand, while the bodies of the smaller frogs were quickly digested by his two little clones, showing that they had no useful evolution or enough biomass for him, Gribbit’s body was very good!

By digesting the old man’s head, Lohan absorbed his memories and understood what had happened.

Basically, these frogs were a village of tricksters who used the poison of these Swamp Slugs to set traps around the area to capture enemies.

With the powerful paralyzing effect that this poison brought, any enemy that came into contact with it would fall motionless to the ground in a few minutes, becoming easy prey to be devoured by the small tadpoles and slugs, thus increasing the vicious cycle they caused.

Unfortunately, a Level 4 Kobold was caught in one of these traps, and to avenge their fallen leader, the rest of the Kobold gang followed the scent of their dead leader to the frog village and decimated these creatures.

It was at that moment that Lohan and Lisa arrived, saving these frogs from the death that awaited them, but because of the greed of these creatures, they became the new executioners of this village.

From the old man’s memories, Lohan realized that there were still younger frogs in the village, but those young frogs were not even conscious enough to speak, only knowing how to follow Gribbit’s orders and do what they were told.

Not even the mating of these poor creatures was by their own choice, only staying with the females that Gribbit had already used and no longer wanted.

Seeing no need to return to the village and carry out a "Young Master"-style massacre, Lohan continued to digest these frogs, and although he did not receive any new skills, he was satisfied with the level he received in an evolution he already had.

[Magic Core Lv 6 → Lv 7] - 48.54 Bio - Total Mana: 24.07 → 26.47

Even though it wasn’t a big evolution, it was still a good advance that saved Lohan 37.34 Biomass.

Unfortunately, the other frogs were very weak, yielding only Biomass and a single level in another evolution.

[Membrane Reinforcement Lv 11 → Lv 12]

It wasn’t as useful as something new to his repertoire, but it was still something that would help his development.

And looking at the Swamp Slugs on the ground, Lohan felt that this was the real treasure, probably capable of yielding him a new evolution focused on poison?!

Chapter 88: 88 - Riches!

"Are you sure it’s okay to carry those slugs inside you?" Lisa asked, looking at Lohan uncertainly.

If she had previously found the scene of the slime carrying a large amount of acid inside him a little strange, seeing him carrying several slugs that practically floated inside him as if they were in a zero-gravity chamber took her concept to another level.

Lohan didn’t care. He couldn’t smell, taste, or feel disgust, so for him it was perfectly acceptable.

"Yeah, no problem, the poison from these slugs doesn’t hurt me," Lohan replied cheerfully.

’That’s not what I was talking about...’ Lisa thought to herself, but said nothing out loud. She knew that only Halon could carry these slugs among them, and considering that this was what would bring them money, she didn’t insist.

His happiness did not come from carrying slugs, but from the new Evolution he had received.

[Poison Production Lv 1]

[By consuming biomass, the user can produce small amounts of poison.]

He had tested how powerful this poison was, and its level was much weaker than the Slime’s poison, but considering that it was still only a Lv 1 Skill, he didn’t mind so much.

As time went by, he could further increase the level of this skill with biomass to the point that this poison could no longer be ignored.

Imagine, while the enemy thought he was just digesting their skin and flesh, the little Slime was also injecting poison into their bodies and decreasing their combat efficiency?

The strategy he uses of using clones to trap and digest enemies could be further improved with the use of this poison!

If it weren’t for him having spent a large amount of Biomass in recent battles, Lohan would have evolved this skill a few times by now.

The road to Thalendor was long, but not that long, so before nightfall they were already in the elven city.

Lisa was a little out of breath from running all that way carrying the Slime on her back, which was already carrying several slugs inside it, but she didn’t complain, since the worst work was still being done by Halon.

When they arrived at the entrance to Thalendor, the guards had changed since the morning, so they had to present their Thalendor ID Cards again.

Fortunately, no clichés happened, and they were able to quickly go to the Silver Crucible.

Looking at the Slime carrying so many Swamp Slugs with ease, Intervar’s eyes sparkled at the sight.

"My little friends are back, and with a big surprise!" The elf said with a smile on her face. "Not only did you bring me the slug poison, but you managed to bring the poison-producing slugs themselves! That’s amazing!"

"Yes, we agree that since we brought you the producer of the product you wanted, the value will also be considerably higher, am I right?" Lisa asked, with a subtle change in tone compared to how she spoke to Halon, now speaking a little more coldly.

Lohan noticed this and was a little surprised, but he didn’t think too deeply about it.

Intervar showed no negative reaction.

"Sure, don’t worry, Silver Crucible’s integrity isn’t that low. How about this, I offered you 10 copper coins for every 100 ml of poison, considering that you brought 5 Swamp Slugs directly, I’ll pay 10 silver coins for each one? The equivalent of the value of 10 liters of poison for each Slug."

Lohan and Lisa looked at each other, thinking about this proposal.

That wouldn’t be bad. The slugs were small, which meant that the poison they would produce per day in a sustainable manner would not be that high, and considering that this would require a suitable environment and great care for the continuous production of poison, the price offered by Intervar was fair.

Feeling that the price was fair, Lisa didn’t make things difficult for Intervar, and after confirmation from Halon, her partner, she accepted the proposal.

They needed a reliable contact to sell these materials in Thalendor, so earning a little less but maintaining a good relationship with the elf was a good investment.

Not to mention that 25 silver coins each was not a small amount!

According to Lisa, players in Newbie Villages were struggling to earn 50 copper coins per day, so with the 5 silver coins they received that morning, in a single day they received 30 silver coins! A total of 60 times more than normal players.

Sure, this rate of gain couldn’t be maintained for long, since they also wasted a lot of time on it, missing out on gaining a lot of experience today.

With 30 silver coins in their pockets, the two decided to pause their immediate money-making and focus on gaining strength for the next few days.

With the amount of experience needed to level up doubling each time, they couldn’t ignore this aspect of Elysium.

Leaving the Silver Crucible, the small bag around Lisa’s neck was heavier and fuller, making more noise as it shook from side to side.

With the 11 copper coins that had been there before, adding the 30 silver coins made the weight she carried slightly uncomfortable, but she didn’t complain.

Even without anything very useful to buy, she still saved this money for after the Guild was founded. With humanoid members joining in the future, these coins would be of great use to them.

As for Lohan, after selling 10 silver coins in the game’s System, converting them into $1,000 for the real world, he returned with Lisa to the Mana Stone shop that Aeliana had introduced them to!

"Those Mana Stones seemed so expensive this morning, but now I think I can choose at least one useful Mana Stone, right? I feel like a Pay To Win player buying Skills in a Cash shop haha." He thought cheerfully.

What he didn’t know was that a surprise awaited them at the Mana Stones store!

Chapter 89: 89 - Spider-Slime Strikes Again!

Arriving at Horizon Bazaar, Lohan was happy to see that the store selling Mana Stones was still open!

Or rather, calling it a store would be an exaggeration; it was just a wooden stall where a beast-like man had put the Mana Stones up for sale.

Don’t underestimate this small stall, after all, the value of the goods it had on display in the morning was almost a gold coin, which represented a reasonable fortune even in Thalendor, where prices were relatively expensive.

As he approached the store, Lohan realized there was a problem. Without Aeliana to pick him up, he couldn’t see what was on the counter...

There weren’t many people looking at the Mana Stones on display, but they were still people he would disturb, or even scare, if he just jumped on the wooden counter.

Looking around, he finally realized a way to make it work.

"Lisa, I’m going to climb up, don’t be scared," Lohan said in a playful voice.

The fox heard that and was confused, tilting her head, not knowing what Halon meant by that, but she didn’t refuse, curious about what he would do next.

This small wooden stall was not mobile, but something fixed in the Horizon Bazaar that shopkeepers could rent to sell whatever they wanted.

Because of this, the roof structure of this store was also fixed, and made in a seemingly very sturdy manner, so Lohan spent a little biomass and wove a Magic Web, attaching it to the roof of the store and pulling himself up like Spider-Man!

In order not to leave Lisa on the ground, he used [Selective Viscosity] to attach himself to her, pulling the fox up as well.

Suddenly, in front of the elves and other races visiting that stall, a strange scene of a relatively large blue Slime attached to a white Fox, hanging from the roof by a blue thread, appeared, with them slowly climbing up as if in an elevator!

Ten minutes turned into thirty, then forty. The buzzing from above was constant, but no beetle dared to descend.

The silence on the first floor became oppressive, broken only by the sound of digestion inside Lohan.

"I don’t think they’re coming out, Lisa. If we want the Core of this Dungeon, we’ll have to go up and deal with the welcoming committee," Lohan stated. "If we had to deal with this many bugs normally, I don’t even know if we could do it, but if we go with my Living Armor idea, I think our chances increase greatly."

Lisa hesitated for a second, remembering the previous sensation, but looking at the still-fresh cut on her flank, she gave in. "All right, Halon. But if you try any funny business, I swear I’ll finish you off."

Lohan did not respond with words. He expanded his biomass, activating [Membrane Reinforcement Lv 22] and [Biological Elasticity Lv 5].

The dark blue gelatin began to flow like living lava over Lisa, covering her chest, flanks, and neck, leaving only her paws, tails, and silver eyes free for combat.

Then, he activated [Obsidian Exoskeleton Lv 3].

Rigid black hexagonal plates sprouted from Lohan’s mass, fitting over Lisa’s body like a complete symbiotic armor.

Lisa felt its weight on her, which made her movements a little awkward compared to how she normally moved, but since the weight was evenly distributed across her body, it didn’t compromise her movement as much as she had imagined.

And considering how much her resistance had increased, the slight decrease in flexibility was only a small price to pay.

"Let’s go," Lohan commanded.

Lisa fired off [Spectral Step], leaping up the walls in a spiral until she broke through the hole in the ceiling.

What awaited them on the second floor was like a nightmare banquet.

Fifteen Glass-Shelled Beetles were positioned in a semicircle, their metallic jaws snapping in unison.

As soon as Lisa landed, the encirclement closed in around her.

The battle was instantly bloody.

Three beetles dove at Lisa’s chest, but instead of tearing through flesh, their scythe-like legs collided with Lohan’s obsidian armor.

CRACK!

Lohan felt the sharp pain, but the [Hemolymphatic Tissue Lv 10] was activated, and as the beetles’ legs touched Lisa, Lohan attacked back, digesting any part that came into contact with the black armor, not only causing damage back to the attacker, but also recovering energy for him.

While Lisa delivered kicks of [Spiritual Fire] that incinerated the attackers’ heads, Lohan used [Selective Viscosity] to "bite" the beetles that touched her, injecting [Poison Production Lv 7] directly into their joints.

The dance between Lisa’s flames and the beetles’ tough shells became frantic as the fifteen beetles closed in around the pair, turning the second floor of the tree into a bloody arena of attrition.

Lisa moved desperately, using [Spectral Step] while leaving trails of light that the beetles tried to intercept with strangely coordinated dives.

Lohan, acting as Living Armor, felt every impact that should have struck the fox’s body, and the sound that came from those impacts was no longer pure metal, but shrapnel flying as the level 10 jaws pushed his resistance to the limit.

The difficulty of dealing with so many enemies above his level simultaneously was taking its toll.

As Lisa spun to incinerate two frontal attackers, a larger beetle leaped out of a side tunnel, striking her flank with a force that overwhelmed Lohan’s [Non-Newtonian Resilience].

The hexagonal plates, unable to absorb so much kinetic pressure at once, shattered with a sharp, painful crack. One of the monster’s serrated legs pierced through Lohan’s membrane, tearing through the deep blue gelatin and reaching Lisa’s flesh beneath him.

Lohan felt that the biomass inside him was falling at an alarming rate, to the point that the stockpile he had accumulated over the past few days had already fallen to a critical 38%!

Lohan felt the sharp pain run through his core with that attack, but anger suppressed the shock.

The [Hemolymphatic Tissue Lv 10] skyrocketed his digestion rate to the max as soon as the enemies’ green ichor and his own vital fluid began to mix.

"Lisa, hang in there, I need fuel!" Lohan transmitted through the mental link, his voice vibrating with urgency.

In a risky move, Lohan used [Partial Division Lv 7] to expel three clones directly onto the corpses of the first beetles Lisa had slain.

While Lohan’s main body writhed to close the gap in the armor and protect her wound with what remained of the biomass stockpile, the clones acted as biomass "suction pumps," ignoring any caution to dissolve the carapaces in seconds, taking advantage of the fact that the [Hemolymphatic Tissue] was still active.

Renewed by the large influx of energy, Lohan gradually increased the thickness of the armor and fired a net of [Magic Weaving Lv 3] from Lisa’s back, creating anchor points that glowed neon blue. 𝑓𝘳𝘦𝑒𝑤𝑒𝘣𝘯ℴ𝘷𝘦𝓁.𝑐𝑜𝑚

Lisa, understanding his tactic without him having to explain anything, used the threads as pivots to change direction instantly, delivering [Spirit Fire] kicks that turned the beetles’ insides to ash before they even touched the ground.

Lohan, now with a steady influx of biomass, did not limit himself to defense alone. He projected small spikes of [Ice Spike] from all directions of his armor, trying to control his Mana expenditure as much as possible, impaling the beetles that tried to flank the fox, while [Monocular Telescopic Vision Lv 9] ensured that each shot hit the vulnerable joints of the monsters’ wings.

The battle of attrition swung in their favor when the last group of beetles, seeing his power regenerate through the death of their own companions, tried to retreat. But they wouldn’t let anyone escape... With a final burst of power, Lohan and Lisa cleared the floor in a brutal synchrony of destruction.

By the time they dealt with the last beetle, both of them were mortally exhausted.

The armor that had completely covered Lisa’s body at the beginning of the battle was now much thinner and had several painful holes in Lohan.

Lisa, who had beautiful, silky white fur before this invasion, now had her fur completely messed up and stained with a mixture of her own blood, the beetles’ blood, and the dirt that had flown around.

Neither of them looked like someone who had emerged victorious from a glorious battle, but reading the notification that appeared next made them both very excited.

[Experience: +2,683] [Experience: 5,003 / 12,800]

In just a few hours of battle, the amount of experience they received was almost equivalent to what was needed to go from level 7 to level 8!

Considering that they had only been raiding this dungeon for two hours, if they could find other dungeons like this to raid today, even leveling up from level 8 to level 10 would not be impossible!

But this speed could not be maintained for long, so they would have to make the most of it while they could.

"Huff... that was... more intense than I imagined... can you sense anyone else?" Lisa asked worriedly.

Even with Lohan protecting her as much as possible, she still sustained some injuries, and unlike Lohan, who could digest biomass to heal himself in a short time, even though she was a Legendary Fox, her body was still a physical organism that needed nutrients and time to recover, so the wounds would remain with her for some time.

If they had to deal with a few dozen more beetles like these, Lisa wasn’t even sure she would survive until the battle against the Boss.

Lohan heard her question and was also concerned.

While using his main body and three clones to digest the beetles as quickly as possible, he began scanning the tree as thoroughly as he could, hoping not to find anything else.

This dungeon invasion was much more difficult than he had imagined...
