Chapter 152: 152 - New Tactic! [PS BONUS]

By spending 303 Biomass, Lohan leveled up his new Evolution directly to Level 7!

[Explosive Steps Lv 1 → Lv 7]

With this evolution, Lohan’s control over it increased tremendously; he could now much better control the power he wanted to use for this skill—lowering the intensity to a point where he could use it even without his artificial tendons, or increasing the power to a point where he had to double the number of magical webs within himself to withstand the resulting pressure!

Sure, at that point the cost of using this skill became almost unsustainable, since creating these magical webs was already expensive to begin with, and after its evolution to [Weaver Mother Lv 2] the cost skyrocketed even further.

If he wanted to keep those tendons within him to improve his close combat, he would have to give up using this evolution for external combat, no longer being able to use it to bind and steal Mana from enemies.

Seeing this, Lohan realized there was no need to spend more biomass on this evolution, so he decided to invest 412 Biomass into the other new evolution he had recently received, which was still at Level 01.

[Sharpened Instinct Level 1 → Lv 7]

[The organism assimilates the synaptic patterns and nervous reflexes of an elite feline predator, increasing reaction speed by 5% per level.]

Increasing the level of this skill by 6 caused Lohan’s reaction speed to increase by 30%!

Unfortunately, Lohan was disappointed when he realized that this increase wasn’t exponential, but considering how weak and common the monster he had digested to achieve this was, it made sense.

Few monsters in the world had great potential, and even fewer were like Slimes.

But this 30% increase was still very good.

Considering that the average human reaction time was 250 milliseconds, Lohan felt that after weeks of killing in Elysium, his reaction time without any active skills had been trained to be slightly faster than the human reaction time.

Assuming he had reduced that time to 200 ms, a 30% upgrade meant his reaction time was now 140 ms!

That was already a very good level! From what he had studied in his previous world, only 1% of the human population achieved such reaction speed, and among those people were F1 drivers and fighter pilots, or even pro players of shooting games like Valorant or Counter-Strike.

To reach this level of reaction speed solely through an evolution he’d achieved in Elysium, Lohan was feeling incredible.

It wasn’t quite as dramatic as saying he could see the world moving in slow motion around him, but the sensation was similar to a delay he hadn’t even known existed suddenly vanishing.

And this improvement in reaction time paired very well with the Explosive Steps he had just acquired, since with a faster reaction time, he could react much better to the high speed at which he was propelling himself forward.

Finishing the tests, Lohan climbed onto Lisa’s back again, and the two continued the hunt.

Even though they had already hunted five rabbits, they would receive only two silver coins and fifty copper coins for them, which, divided between the two, would amount to just 125 copper coins each.

Since the rabbits weren’t as difficult to hunt as the Shadow Serpents and Swamp Slugs, the price for their materials wasn’t as high as the others’, but they intended to make up for it in quantity!

Needing experience to level up as quickly as possible, hunting these rabbits would be a great way to grind.

Lisa then began to move more slowly, while Lohan acted as a mobile radar, scanning everything around them for the slightest sign of rabbits.

Thanks to his keen perception, Lohan picked up new vibrations coming from a denser section of the woods, detecting a pack of six Explosive Rabbits—this time three Level 9 and three Level 10—that were approaching rapidly, drawn by the scent of mana and the heat of the previous battle.

"Lisa, they’re coming in a pincer formation. If we try to fight in open terrain again, the cumulative impact of their kicks will control the pace of the battle once more, and I don’t know if I’ll be able to create enough magic webs to handle this larger group..." Lohan warned in a serious voice through the mental link, using parallel processing to calculate the likely trajectories.

Lisa fell deep in thought, looking around for any sign of the rabbits. "I trust you didn’t bring us here to hunt more rabbits without a plan in mind, right?"

"Hehe... we’re going to use their physiology against them. I’ve observed that they rely on advanced visual perception to calculate the explosive leaps they make... if I take that away from them, we’ll dominate the battle." Lohan said.

Already wrapped around Lisa’s body, Lohan prepared for battle as rigid, black hexagonal plates sprouted from his membrane, overlapping to form the obsidian armor that protected the fox’s body.

As soon as the first rabbit leaped from a branch, Lohan tensed his body and expelled a dense, gray cloud of opaque smoke that saturated the clearing in seconds.

For the rabbits, it was as if the world had vanished into an impenetrable fog. Unable to see the footholds on the trees or even the ground for their kicks, the pack lost its rhythm. Several of them crashed violently into the trunks, disoriented by their own high speed.

However, for Lohan, the smoke was no obstacle. With his heightened perception, he began to see the environment through thermal signatures, visualizing the monsters as vibrant orange blurs amid the cold blue of the scene.

Through the mental link, he described everything he saw in real time to Lisa’s mind, without the delay of speech, allowing her to "see" the targets through him.

"Ten o’clock, Lisa! The Level 10 is frozen, trying to sniff out our position!" Lohan said immediately.

Lisa didn’t hesitate and shot out like a white ghost through the mist.

If she didn’t trust the Slime, this window of opportunity might close, but after so many days of fighting side by side, her trust in this companion was at its peak when it came to combat.

Suddenly she emerged from the shadows and unleashed a burst of white flames directly into the flank of the confused monster.

Lohan didn’t miss the opportunity and fired the translucent threads imbued with Mana just to trap the most vulnerable rabbits trying to jump blindly, avoiding wasting Mana on them.

Now with experience dealing with these monsters, the battle unfolded much more easily than the first time, until suddenly a much louder explosion erupted, blowing the smoke away.

--BOOOOOM!

Chapter 153: 153 - Level 11 Explosive Rabbit

The cloud of ash and smoke that Lohan had expelled was instantly swept away by a violent gust of wind, revealing the silhouette of a monster that made the other rabbits look like puppies.

In the center of a small crater of scorched earth, what they had initially thought was just a Level 10 Elite Rabbit actually looked more like a Level 11 Explosive Rabbit snorting with eyes bloodshot in vibrant crimson.

Its fur wasn’t the ordinary gray of smaller rabbits, but displayed a dark metallic sheen, and the Mana emanating from its hind legs was so dense that it visually distorted the space around them.

Lohan felt a chill run through his core.

According to what they had understood from Elysium, reaching Level 11 meant undergoing a qualitative evolution.

That rabbit wasn’t just stronger; at this point, it operated on a higher plane of existence than the rabbits they had been facing moments ago, and perhaps even a level above them.

"Lisa, I think this is a Level 11 Rabbit, be very careful!" Because of the chaos the confrontation was causing on the ground, Lohan wasn’t sure if Lisa had carefully analyzed this new enemy, so as a precaution he decided to warn her via the mental link, feeling his parallel processing working frantically to map the new thermal trajectory.

The rabbit didn’t hesitate or try to exchange words with them.

Lohan didn’t even know if it was capable of speech.

With a crack that sounded like a cannon shot, it vanished from where it stood. Lohan barely had time to react before the monster loomed above them.

The rabbit didn’t try to punch or bite... it simply delivered a downward kick with both hind legs.

’I can’t join a guild directly... or else I’ll just end up working for some big corporation like my father.’ She thought, looking at a group of people who clearly weren’t from around here, walking through the town square. ’But even if I don’t join a guild, I believe my Epic Class has enough value to warrant an equal partnership with others, right?’

With an idea in mind, Brynn smiled and walked confidently toward that group.

The Upper Zone wasn’t exclusive to the planet of Lohan, but a distinction that people in the Human Federation had adopted to refer to different classes of people.

"Are you saying we’re like walking air purifiers?" Lohan asked, trying to keep his voice steady.

"Or biochemical bombs..." Devon retorted seriously. "The leader of my group noticed that when she gets nervous, the pollution around her starts to ’curdle.’ Small solid particles form and fall to the ground like black soot. If you have a Rare Base like mine, or something higher, the effect is proportional to your Mana density and even more pronounced if your control over Mana is weak. Luckily for me, my control over Mana is exceptional, so I’ve never had a problem losing control." 𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺

Lohan swallowed hard.

He had a Mythic Race and Class. If Devon’s rule was correct, the "environmental signature" Lohan could cause would be equivalent to a lighthouse on a starless night. He recalled how Isabella Vance’s Mana felt 50 times more intense than that of an ordinary student, with her scent exuding a fragrance of wildflowers and dew, and thought that his Class and Race were even greater than hers.

If a person with an Epic Base can already cause these phenomena with ease, imagine what he, a Double Mythic, could cause?!

’Shit...’ Lohan thought, subtly activating his [Structural Stability] to suppress the flow of energy. ’That’s why Isabella stopped in front of me today and started sniffing the air. She didn’t smell my human body... she might have sensed the molecular processing of my Mana trying to clean up the lab’s pollution, or maybe some scent I naturally give off because of a process like that..."

"We’ve noticed this happens more when we’re stressed or using abilities," Devon continued, oblivious to Lohan’s internal conflict. "That’s why my group is training in ’suppression.’ Basically, we try to keep Mana locked in our core even in moments of crisis, which surprisingly also helps improve our Mana control in Elysium. Hayes, if you really have the level of power I suspect, be careful. If you ’leak’ too much Mana in your apartment, that place will have the cleanest air in all of the Lower Zone within a week... and that will attract Federation scouts like flies, or maybe you’ll create the most chaotic air in the place, and attract just as much attention."

Lohan nodded, sensing that this information would be of great value to him.

The real world was no longer just a place to rest between grinding sessions; the rules of Elysium were literally rewriting the atmosphere around him.

A few minutes later, the Devon bus stop arrived, leaving Lohan alone and pensive on the bus. ’I need to ask Lisa about this!’

Chapter 169: 169 - Message

Despite his eagerness to contact Lisa, Lohan didn’t let that disrupt his daily routine, since it was his constant, repetitive training that had brought his physical condition in the real world up to its current level.

He drank a Grade A nutritional supplement, absorbed as much of it as he could, and performed the routine exercises he did every day.

With his improved control over his body, these exercises, which he had previously only been able to do a few repetitions of, now reached a limit at least 10 times greater.

Sure, that doesn’t mean Lohan was literally 10 times stronger, but with training time, not only did his strength increase, but so did his endurance and the technique to perform the exercise correctly.

And an increase in endurance and exercise technique improved the gains he received from those exercises on the next training day.

With Efficient Digestion, Lohan absorbed all nutrients in the richest and most refined form possible, greatly accelerating the body’s process of utilizing those nutrients, thereby accelerating his growth rate several times over.

Satisfied with the day’s workout, Lohan took a luxurious bath under the dirty water flowing from the showerheads, which, despite these conditions, was still a luxury the old Lohan couldn’t afford, and with his body refreshed and clean, he lay down on the bed and logged into Elysium.

Upon "opening his eyes", considering he had no eyes in this world, Lohan found himself in the center of Thalendor, in a dark alley between two shops, where he had gone to disconnect from the game the previous day without drawing much attention.

Looking around and not seeing Lisa, Lohan wasn’t surprised. She was a girl from the Upper Zone; the time it took her to get home from college, considering she was actually Isabella Vance, would be much shorter than the time it took him to get there by bus.

Knowing her, it was quite possible she was hunting monsters on her own right now.

Opening his friends list, Lohan saw she was online and sent her a message.

[Halon: Hey Lisa, how are you?]

After a few seconds, realizing her reply would likely take a while, Lohan looked at the Astral Chest and noticed that the tendons from the rabbits they’d hunted yesterday were gone, and in their place were 42 silver coins.

Smiling, Lohan calculated the value of those coins and was pleased to see that he could sell half of them to Lisa for $2,100.

With that money, he could not only pay the $912 in loan interest, but he could even pay down some of the principal.

’Although paying more than just the interest to the bank right now might not be a good choice, if I use only 912 copper coins to pay that interest, I’d still have 11 silver coins and 88 copper coins left to spend on whatever I wanted here in the game to speed up my progress, allowing me to earn even more money in the near future and get the snowball rolling.’

Even if he spent those remaining $1,188 to pay down the debt, that expense would only reduce the amount of interest he paid monthly from $912 to $877... spending over a thousand credits to reduce the monthly interest by $35 was a terrible investment.

Sure, if he were only going to earn that amount of money every month forever, it would be well worth it to pay down that debt little by little, but considering that if he invested that money in items for himself, increasing his coin-earning efficiency in Elysium, the extra earnings he’d receive next month would be much greater than the $35 savings. 𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦

So Lohan decided to sell only 10 silver coins for $1,000 to Lisa and keep the other 12 silver coins to buy something useful in Thalendor.

With the $92 he still had in his bank account in the other world, after paying the $912 in bank interest, he would have $180 to buy supplies for the rest of the month.

Having grown accustomed to the terrible taste of the nutritional solutions, Lohan no longer saw any need to buy natural, more expensive foods, preferring the efficiency and low price of these solutions.

With nothing particularly important to do now, since Lisa was in the middle of a hunt, Lohan decided to wander through Thalendor toward the Great Horizon Bazaar, hoping to find some Mana Stones that might come in handy.

While Lohan wandered through the city waiting for Lisa’s reply, the fox in question was standing atop a rock, surrounded by a dozen corpses of Level 4 to 5 Goblins, which, despite being stronger than the Goblins she hunted when she was a low-level player, were much weaker than the Level 10 monsters she hunted with Halon.

These solo hunting sessions she undertook were mainly spent warming up for future combat and keeping her own fighting style sharp.

Even though fighting with Halon’s help was much safer and more ruthless, Lisa didn’t want to get used to fighting only with him and end up becoming dependent on her friend.

Especially now that Halon likely knew her real-world identity, Lisa was completely unsure of how to face him in Elysium.

Ever since he sent the message letting her know he was online, Lisa had been standing there staring at that message, her mind working at full speed, formulating replies, deleting them, and formulating new ones.

’Gosh, how can I respond? Do I pretend nothing happened? Pretend I don’t know anything? Do I admit that I’m the Isabella Vance he knows? Pretend I’m NOT Isabella Vance?! Gosh, what do I do?!’ Lisa reread Halon’s message for the twentieth time, still unsure how to respond.

[Lisa: Hey Halon, I’m doing just as well as always... nothing out of the ordinary—how about you?]

Reading the message she had written, Lisa let out a cry of agony and quickly deleted it, not daring to send such an awkward message to Halon.

’Ugh, why is it so hard to just send a normal message?!’

Chapter 170: 170 - Invitation

[Lisa: Hey Halon, I’m hunting some goblins. How about you? Do you want me to come pick you up now?]

That was the best message Lisa could think of, one that wouldn’t seem suspicious at all and was something she’d say on any normal day.

’Please, don’t ask about my identity...’ She pleaded mentally, hoping he’d just pretend not to know, just as she was doing.

The time until his reply felt like an eternity, but in reality only 30 seconds had passed.

[Halon: Oh, okay then, you can continue your hunt for now. I just ran into Aeliana and her Master here in Thalendor, and they invited me to their magic tower. Let me know when you’re done, and I’ll tell you where the tower is so you can come too!]

Reading Halon’s reply, a mix of feelings welled up in Lisa’s chest.

On one hand, she was relieved to see that he wasn’t bringing up the subject of her identity, practically acting as if he knew nothing about it.

That was exactly what she wanted to happen, but the reason he wasn’t bringing up that subject stirred another feeling in her chest.

’Geez, going to explore Aeliana’s master’s magic tower is more important than asking me about my identity?!’ she wondered, frustrated.

When she discovered Halon’s identity, that was what she thought about most during the day. Many times while she was alone, Lisa would recall his face and imagine what it would feel like to talk to him in person.

But when he discovered her identity, instead of confronting her until she admitted it and they could act like they did in Elysium in the real world, he went out with other girls to explore a magic tower?!

Besides this strange feeling she was experiencing, another feeling was also taking hold of Lisa’s chest, an anxiety she had been keeping under control in recent days, but which had grown even stronger because of Halon’s behavior. 𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚

’Is he avoiding me now that he knows who I am?’

Lisa didn’t even know how to reply to that message, wanting to rush back to Thalendor to see him and figure out how they’d resolve this, but also afraid of returning and seeming desperate, or worse, returning and seeing that he was looking at her differently, seeing that the friend Halon she’d made had vanished, replaced by the boy intimidated by the Vance surname...

With such conflicting feelings swirling in her chest, she let out a frustrated scream and didn’t reply, running toward the goblins’ lair and deciding to take out her anger on those grotesque creatures.

-xXx-

While Lisa was taking it out on the goblins, Lohan was in Aeliana’s arms, heading toward her mistress’s tower.

Just a few minutes before Lohan sent that reply that left Lisa in a state of fury and confusion, he was idly wandering through the wide, magnificent avenues of Thalendor.

The air of the elven capital, saturated with Mana and freshness, made his core vibrate with a sense of comfort he couldn’t feel in the real world.

He was on his way to the Great Horizon Bazaar, thinking about how to use the silver coins when suddenly, a shrill cry, charged with contagious joy, cut through the city’s murmur.

"Halon! Little friend! You’re back!"

Lohan barely had time to react before being spotted by Aeliana, who ran toward him with her long blonde hair swaying in the wind and a pout of frustration on her face. She crouched down, picking up the slime and cradling it in her lap with ease, something that, at this point, didn’t bother him in the least.

"Where have you been?! I’ve been looking for you all along the edge of the forest these past few days..." Aeliana exclaimed, pretending to be angry as she pressed him against her chest. "I thought you’d forgotten me after getting that ID card! How dare you leave your only elf friend waiting?!"

Lohan vibrated his membrane, trying to explain himself. However, he realized an immediate problem: Lisa wasn’t there to act as the usual mental link.

Without the fox, he was just a mute Slime to Aeliana’s ears. He began gesturing frantically, forming a small bluish hand that waved apologetically and pointed toward the horizon, trying to indicate that he had been on an important hunt.

"What’s the matter? Are you trying to tell me you were busy?" Aeliana tilted her head, trying to decipher the clumsy movements of the little jelly hand.

It was then that the air around them crackled with a cold, purple pressure. In the blink of an eye, Yrneha Ylasys materialized beside the apprentice, her wooden staff still pulsing with a soft glow of spatial magic.

She was apparently about to say something to Aeliana when she noticed the little blue ball in the girl’s arms.

"Stop shaking the poor Slime, Lia. He’s probably trying to say that his partner isn’t here to translate for him." Yrneha’s voice resonated, and Lohan felt a slight mental touch as she effortlessly established a telepathic link between them.

As soon as the connection was established, Yrneha froze for a millisecond. The expression of disdain she normally reserved for slimes was replaced by genuine shock. She sensed not only the dense Mana and the [Artificial Magic Core Harmonizer] operating at high frequency, but something much deeper.

’That fluctuation...’ Yrneha thought, her eyes shining with a dangerous scientific curiosity. ’He isn’t just saturated with Mana. Is that... Natural Energy?!’

She realized that Lohan now carried a vital essence that synchronized his cellular structure with the very nature of the world, something she had only seen in ancient texts or in monsters made of nature itself. For a nature-loving High Elf, sensing that pure energy in a Slime was like finding a rough diamond in the middle of a garbage dump.

A creature known for the rampant destruction of life, now exuding an aura of life, was something utterly contradictory.

"Little creature... what have you been devouring?" Yrneha asked, her voice carrying an authority that made Lohan’s core waver. "Your level of existence has changed qualitatively in just a few days... I demand that you come to my Magic Tower now for a more thorough analysis."

Lohan felt a chill run down his spine and immediately shook his jelly-like hand. He remembered the last time she had shown interest in taking him to the lab and knew that, without Lisa there to mediate, he might end up as a potion ingredient.

"I appreciate the invitation, Lady Ylasys, but I really need to find my companion soon." Lohan replied mentally, trying to stay calm.

Yrneha clicked her tongue impatiently.

She knew this Slime was a "Friend of Thalendor" and couldn’t simply kidnap him, but the knowledge regarding that Natural Energy Core was far too valuable. She looked at the Slime, realizing how much he valued his own growth.

"What if I offered you a Mana Stone from a Level 13 monster?" she proposed, watching the Slime freeze instantly. "You should know that just as our core needs twice the energy to level up each time, monsters are the same... imagine the energy load of a Level 13 core."

Lohan hesitated.

He wasn’t even worried about the large amount of biomass he could gain from it, but rather excited to think about what Evolution he might achieve from it? Considering he had gained very good powers from the other Mana Stones above Level 11, he figured that this time might not be any different.

He looked at Aeliana, who was smiling hopefully, and at Yrneha, who was already preparing the teleportation circle.

"All right... I accept. But only with an oath sworn on your magic that you won’t put me in danger and that I can leave at any time." He gave in, but still set conditions.

Honestly, he was curious about the mage’s tower, drawn to the Mana Stone, and trusted Aeliana enough to believe she wouldn’t be smiling like that if her master intended to dissect him.

It was at that moment that he received the message from Lisa.
